assignment.review_focus: Identify all candidate consistency issues across the PT9L DHF/DMR corpus. Priority signals: (1) documents referencing PT2L, PT3SBT, BP3L, or PT9C outside clearly marked historical or draft folders; (2) PT9C appearing as a PCB sub-component number vs. standalone product in clinical/user-test documents; (3) PT3SBT references in design output lists or label review documents filed under T1 sample folder; (4) BP3L software diagrams appearing in the main software design folder or T1 sample subfolder; (5) PT2L risk document F0013 carrying a PT9L document number internally despite residing in a '历史文件' subfolder; (6) version, revision, and approval-signature gaps across all document ID patterns (PT9L-KHXQ01, PT9L-KXPS01, PT9L-FXJH01, PT9L-FXGB01, PT9L-EBOM01, PT9L-T1EB01, PT9L-SJSC01, PT9C-CNTP01); (7) regulatory-standard applicability inconsistencies between draft and final design inputs (EN ISO 80601-2-56, MDR 2017/745, CE registration status).

key_entities.product_description: 红外非接触式额头温度计 (Infrared No-Touch Forehead Thermometer)
key_entities.intended_use: Intermittent measurement of body temperature from forehead skin surface on people of all ages; consumer home use and healthcare provider use
key_entities.bluetooth: PT9L can transmit temperature to smart device with Bluetooth (per Risk Management Report)

regulatory_baseline: EN ISO 80601-2-56:2017+A1:2018 (EU, applicability differs between draft and final design input)
MDR 2017/745 (EU, applicability differs between draft and final design input)
ISO 14971:2019 / EN ISO 14971:2019 / EN ISO 14971:2019/A11:2021 (risk management)
CE registration: applicability not yet determined per final design input
candidate_discovery_hints: PT9C appears as a sub-component PCB document number and as a standalone product in clinical evaluation and user test documents
PT3SBT appears in design output list two and a label review document filed under T1 sample folder

PT2L risk documents are in a '历史文件' subfolder but one (F0013) carries a PT9L document number internally

mandatory_audit_matrix.check_goal: Verify that key PT9L design-input parameters are carried into design outputs and validation conditions consistently.

Verify consistency across BOM, process, inspection, packaging, labels, drawings, and transfer records.
Verify controlled status, version history, review signatures, and document-control completeness across all stages.

regulatory.goal: Check regulatory baseline, standards applicability, formal reports, controlled status, version history, review signatures, and document-control completeness.
regulatory.system_prompt: Review regulatory and document-control consistency using only supplied evidence IDs.

| 8 | **常温精度测试** | 环境要求：室温：23.0±2.0℃ 相对湿度：50%RH±20%RH
将恒温水槽分别设定在32℃、32.5℃、35℃、38.5℃、42℃、42.5℃、42.9℃，待恒温水槽温度稳定后，使用体温计进行测量：
1. 在断电情况下按住按键后装入电池，显示“CAL”后松开按键，产品进入黑体模式；
2. 对被测水槽连续测量三次；
3. 精度要求：≥35℃且≤42℃：±0.2℃，其它：±0.3℃。
4. 对测试结果不符合规定的温度计，可复测两次，两次复测合格，亦可作合格处理。 | 见测试记录二 | 见测试记录二 | 合格 | |

1. 跌落高度为 1M，跌 3 次，依次顺序底部、LCD 面、有测量键 面朝下方跌落各一次，探头部位不可跌落。
2.应跌落于密度为 700kg/M3，厚度为 50mm 的硬质木板或混凝 土地面，若未完成跌落次数就已经解体或严重损伤时，应立即 停止后续动作。并分析。
3.以产品自身的重量自由下落，不可有外力加持，下落过程中 产品不可在空中翻转，否则无效。

primary_scope_rules: PT9L is the target product model for this DHF
Documents in '2L风险改 - 历史文件' folder are explicitly historical
Documents referencing PT2L, PT3SBT, BP3L, or PT9C outside clearly marked historical/draft folders require justification

key_entities.product_description: 红外非接触式额头温度计 (Infrared No-Touch Forehead Thermometer)
key_entities.intended_use: Intermittent measurement of body temperature from forehead skin surface on people of all ages; consumer home use and healthcare provider use
key_entities.bluetooth: PT9L can transmit temperature to smart device with Bluetooth (per Risk Management Report)

regulatory_baseline: EN ISO 80601-2-56:2017+A1:2018 (EU, applicability differs between draft and final design input)
MDR 2017/745 (EU, applicability differs between draft and final design input)
ISO 14971:2019 / EN ISO 14971:2019 / EN ISO 14971:2019/A11:2021 (risk management)
CE registration: applicability not yet determined per final design input
candidate_discovery_hints: PT9C appears as a sub-component PCB document number and as a standalone product in clinical evaluation and user test documents
PT3SBT appears in design output list two and a label review document filed under T1 sample folder
BP3L software diagrams appear in both the main software design folder and T1 sample subfolder
PT2L risk documents are in a '历史文件' subfolder but one (F0013) carries a PT9L document number internally

mandatory_audit_matrix.check_goal: Verify that key PT9L design-input parameters are carried into design outputs and validation conditions consistently.

software.goal: Check software requirements, design, tests, validation, traceability, versioning, and legacy software artifact references.
software.system_prompt: Review software lifecycle consistency using only supplied evidence IDs.

findings.claim: reviewable conclusion
findings.rationale: evidence-based reason

evidence_catalog.source_text: 我公司天津九安医疗电子股份有限公司研制开发的PT9C型红外体温计是一款通过接收人体额头部位散发的红外能量，来测量人体温度的红外体温计。

evidence_catalog.rel_path: 18 设计确认\废案与备份\PT9L医用电子体温计临床评价报告-中国版本不适用.via_lo_html.clean.md
evidence_catalog.source_text: PT9C与本公司注册生产的红外体温计 PT3（注册证号：津械注准20192070046）为实质性等同的同类产品，基本原理、结构组成、制造材料、性能要求、安全性评价、符合的国家/行业标准、预期用途等方面完全等同，且该同类产品上市销售无不良事故记录。依据国家食品药品监督管理局发布的《临床评价指导原则》规定，将本公司生产的红外体温计与上述公司生产的红外计进行了对比，具体对比情况说明见申报产品与同品种医疗器械对比表。

evidence_catalog.rel_path: 18 设计确认\废案与备份\PT9L医用电子体温计临床评价报告-中国版本不适用.via_lo_html.clean.md
evidence_catalog.source_text: 通过《申报产品与目录中已获准境内注册医疗器械对比表》中对比表明，拟注册的PT9C红外体温计产品在结构性能、材料组成、性能要求、灭菌消毒方式、适用范围、使用说明上与柯顿（天津）电子医疗器械有限公司注册生产的红外体温计PT3（注册证号：津械注准20192070046）基本相同，表明拟注册产品与已获准境内注册的产品基本等同。

llm_output.summary: Cross-corpus scan of the PT9L DHF/DMR package reveals 14 candidate consistency issues spanning legacy product residue in active documents, document-number mismatches, unsigned approvals, wrong-product references in BOM and label documents, regulatory applicability conflicts, software diagram contamination, and blood-pressure-specific language appearing in a thermometer DHF.
review_notes: All documents in '2L风险改 - 历史文件' and '原版 - 历史文件' subfolders are acknowledged as historical; PT2L/PT9L cross-contamination within those folders is noted but lower priority than contamination outside them.

PT3-P10, PT3-M01, PT3-M02 appear in the ABOM as shared/common parts with 'PT3' as the source project; this may be intentional shared-component reuse and requires engineering confirmation rather than automatic rejection.
The 'PT9C设计确认E0 23.11' document (SW-023) is filed under folder '18 设计确认' without a clear 'historical' or 'draft' marker; its scope relative to PT9L requires clarification.
Biocompatibility reports are filed under 'PT5' product name; cross-product biocompatibility bridging is common practice but the bridging justification document is not visible in the evidence catalog.

The draft safety report (VV-086/VV-087/VV-088) carries report number 'ETX2023-07-078-02' (missing '03' segment) while the final report (VV-043) carries 'ETX202303-07-078-02'; this may be a transcription artifact in the draft cover page rather than a separate report.

findings.claim: F0013 (PT2L risk management plan) carries the PT9L document number 'PT9L-FXJH01 V1.0' internally while its filename and folder identify it as a PT2L document, creating an irreconcilable document-number conflict within the '2L风险改 - 历史文件' folder.
findings.rationale: RISK-007 shows the file title as 'V1.0-1 Risk Management Plan PT2L美亚-FXJH01 V1.0' and RISK-008 shows the internal document number field reads 'DN: PT9L-FXJH01 V1.0 Risk Management Plan'. The same document number PT9L-FXJH01 V1.0 is also used by the legitimate PT9L risk management plan (RISK-056, RISK-002). Two distinct documents—one for PT2L and one for PT9L—share the same controlled document number, which violates document-control uniqueness requirements regardless of folder placement.
challenge_questions: Was F0013 intentionally assigned document number PT9L-FXJH01 V1.0, or is this a copy-paste error from the PT9L template?
Which document is the authoritative PT9L-FXJH01 V1.0: F0012/F0021 or F0013?
Has the document control system been updated to retire or renumber F0013 to avoid the duplicate DN?

findings.claim: A label review document titled 'PT3SBT标签审核表（海外更新）' referencing product model PT2L and PT2L-specific document numbers is filed directly in the PT9L T1 sample folder ('11 T1样机') without any historical or draft designation, suggesting it may be used as a PT9L label compliance record.
findings.rationale: SW-007 and SW-008 show the file header reads 'PT2L(美亚)标签检查报告' with product model 'PT2L' and project number '2020-DEV01'. SW-009 through SW-012 show the reviewed label documents are PT2L-SMSP09, PT2L-CBZP07, PT2L-F96, and PT2L-F97—none of which are PT9L document numbers. REG-067 through REG-071 show the compliance checklist references PT2L(美亚)-ZXBQ01 through ZXBQ06 as the basis documents. The file is located at '11 T1样机\\PT3SBT标签审核表（海外更新）' with no historical folder marker, placing it in the active T1 sample evidence set.
challenge_questions: Is this PT3SBT/PT2L label review document intended to serve as a bridging or equivalence record for PT9L label compliance, and if so, where is the formal bridging justification?
Should this document be moved to a clearly marked historical or reference folder, or replaced with a PT9L-specific label review?
Which PT9L label document numbers (PT9L-SMSP01, PT9L-CBZP01, PT9L-F02, etc.) have been formally reviewed against IEC 60601-1 labeling requirements?

findings.claim: A document titled 'BP3L 软件图样E0 23.11' containing BP3L software flow diagrams is present in both the main PT9L software design folder ('07 软件设计方案E0 23.11\\软件图样E0 23.11') and the PT9L T1 sample subfolder ('11 T1样机\\软件文件底稿\\软件图样E0 23.11'), neither of which is marked as historical or draft, raising the risk that BP3L software architecture is being used as the PT9L software design record.
findings.rationale: SW-001 through SW-006 show F0052 titled 'BP3L 软件图样E0 23.11' residing in '07 软件设计方案E0 23.11\\软件图样E0 23.11'. SW-017 through SW-022 show F0131 with the identical title residing in '11 T1样机\\软件文件底稿\\软件图样E0 23.11'. Both files are flagged excluded_from_primary_scope=false. No PT9L-specific software diagram document is visible in the evidence catalog to replace these BP3L diagrams.
challenge_questions: Is there a PT9L-specific software diagram document that supersedes the BP3L diagrams in these folders?
Were the BP3L software diagrams intentionally retained as the PT9L software design baseline, and if so, is there a formal equivalence or reuse justification?
Do the BP3L software diagrams accurately reflect the PT9L firmware architecture, including Bluetooth functionality specific to PT9L?

findings.claim: A clinical evaluation report filed under the PT9L design confirmation folder describes the product as 'PT9C' and 'PT9CL', and a user field test plan is titled 'PT9C V1.0', indicating that PT9C-specific clinical and usability evidence may be substituted for PT9L without a documented equivalence justification.
findings.rationale: SW-057 shows F0255 (filed in '18 设计确认\\废案与备份') with internal text 'model: PT9CL' and SW-058 shows the body text explicitly states 'PT9C型红外体温计'. SW-059 and SW-060 show the clinical comparison is between PT9C and PT3, not PT9L. SW-061 shows F0260 titled '用户现场测试计划 PT9C V1.0' filed in '18 设计确认\\用户测试'. While F0255 is in a '废案与备份' subfolder, F0260 is in the active '用户测试' subfolder with no historical marker.
challenge_questions: Is the PT9C user field test plan (F0260) intended to serve as the PT9L usability validation record, and if so, where is the formal equivalence or bridging document?
What are the design differences between PT9C and PT9L that would affect clinical evaluation conclusions?
Is there a separate PT9L-specific clinical evaluation report and user test plan, or are the PT9C documents the only records?

findings.claim: The PT9L EBOM (PT9L-EBOM01 V1.0) and T1 EBOM (PT9L-T1EB01 V1.0) both list a sensor PCB with drawing number 'PT9C-CNTP01 V1.0', which is a PT9C-prefixed document number appearing in active PT9L production BOMs without any explanatory note or cross-reference justification.
findings.rationale: HW-041 and HW-078 show the EBOM entry: 'PCB | K0118000084609A1106 | FR4 | PT9C-CNTP01 V1.0 | 1 | PCB'. HW-043 shows the same entry in the T1 EBOM. SW-015 and SW-016 confirm the same entries. The design output list one (HW-079 through HW-084) lists only PT9L-HFMP01 V1.0 as the main PCB drawing, with no mention of PT9C-CNTP01, suggesting the sensor PCB drawing is not formally listed in the design output index.

| 8 | **常温精度测试** | 环境要求：室温：23.0±2.0℃ 相对湿度：50%RH±20%RH
将恒温水槽分别设定在32℃、32.5℃、35℃、38.5℃、42℃、42.5℃、42.9℃，待恒温水槽温度稳定后，使用体温计进行测量：
1. 在断电情况下按住按键后装入电池，显示“CAL”后松开按键，产品进入黑体模式；
2. 对被测水槽连续测量三次；
3. 精度要求：≥35℃且≤42℃：±0.2℃，其它：±0.3℃。
4. 对测试结果不符合规定的温度计，可复测两次，两次复测合格，亦可作合格处理。 | 见测试记录二 | 见测试记录二 | 合格 | |

1. 跌落高度为 1M，跌 3 次，依次顺序底部、LCD 面、有测量键 面朝下方跌落各一次，探头部位不可跌落。
2.应跌落于密度为 700kg/M3，厚度为 50mm 的硬质木板或混凝 土地面，若未完成跌落次数就已经解体或严重损伤时，应立即 停止后续动作。并分析。
3.以产品自身的重量自由下落，不可有外力加持，下落过程中 产品不可在空中翻转，否则无效。

mandatory_audit_matrix.check_goal: Verify that key PT9L design-input parameters are carried into design outputs and validation conditions consistently.

assignment.review_focus: MATRIX-001 — Design input to output parameter consistency for PT9L. Verify that key design-input parameters (measurement range, accuracy, response time, environmental conditions, Bluetooth specification, intended-use population, forehead measurement site) stated in the design input document (PT9L-KHXQ01 or equivalent) are carried forward without alteration or omission into design output documents (drawings, specifications, verification/validation test conditions). Flag any parameter value, unit, or scope discrepancy between design input and output layers. Also check whether PT9C PCB sub-component parameters are correctly scoped to PT9L system-level requirements rather than being inherited verbatim from a PT9C standalone specification.

agent_runs.summary: Cross-corpus scan of the PT9L DHF/DMR package reveals 14 candidate consistency issues spanning legacy product residue in active documents, document-number mismatches, unsigned approvals, wrong-product references in BOM and label documents, regulatory applicability conflicts, software diagram contamination, and blood-pressure-specific language appearing in a thermometer DHF.

llm_output.summary: Hardware audit of PT9L DHF/DMR reveals five substantive consistency findings: a blood-pressure residue phrase in the battery design-verification plan/report, an unresolved BOM conflict between PT3-P10 dual-spring and PT5-M02/M03 separate springs, a total-assembly drawing part-number anomaly (T-Z1-P10 used for two distinct PCBs), missing pass/fail verdicts in multiple T1 sample review checklists, and object-temperature mode accuracy tolerance (±0.2 °C) applied at 30 °C and 45 °C in software test plans despite the design-input accuracy specification only requiring ±0.2 °C for ≥35 °C and ≤42 °C.
review_notes: Measurement accuracy specification ≥35 °C and ≤42 °C: ±0.2 °C; outside that range: ±0.3 °C is consistently stated across design input (HW-003), product inspection standard (HW-035), design verification plan (HW-056), design verification report (HW-051), product overview (HW-063), and defect definition (HW-064). No discrepancy found for body-temperature mode accuracy.
Measurement range 32 °C–42.9 °C stated in label audit (HW-024, HW-025) and operation guide (HW-034) is consistent with each other.
PCB design review checklist items (HW-004 through HW-009) all show 'pass' verdicts; no anomaly found in those items.
Battery polarity marking confirmed present in label audit (HW-023, HW-028); battery removal warning confirmed in operation guide (HW-026, HW-029).

Low-battery software requirement (HW-060) and battery-voltage sampling function (HW-044, HW-059) are present; no explicit low-voltage cutoff threshold value was found in the supplied evidence to cross-check against a hardware specification, so no finding is raised on threshold value alone.
PCB part number PT9L-HFMP01 V1.0 is consistently referenced across EBOM (HW-040, HW-077), T1 BOM (HW-042), SMT instruction (HW-062), and design output list (HW-079 through HW-084).

PT9C-CNTP01 V1.0 sensor PCB appears in EBOM (HW-041, HW-078) and T1 BOM (HW-043); its presence as a sub-component is noted but no standalone PT9C accuracy specification was supplied in evidence to compare against PT9L system-level requirements, so a separate finding is not raised beyond what is observable.
ASTM accuracy reference in operation guide (HW-031) cites ±0.2 °C for 37–39 °C range for IR thermometers, which is consistent with the design-input accuracy requirement for the clinical range.

findings.claim: The design verification plan and one section of the design verification report for the PT9L thermometer contain the phrase '次血压测量' (blood pressure measurements) in the rechargeable-battery capacity requirement, which is a blood-pressure-monitor residue that does not apply to a thermometer and creates a traceability break between the design input and the verification documents.
findings.rationale: HW-002 (design input, F0031) states the battery requirement as '□可充电电池：在充满电后，电池电量至少能进行 次测量' using the generic word '测量' (measurements). HW-058 (design verification plan, F0121) and HW-055 (design verification report section, F0114 line 110) both replace '测量' with '血压测量' (blood pressure measurements). HW-053 (design verification report, F0114 line 54) correctly uses '测量' without the blood-pressure qualifier, showing the error is not universal but is present in at least two documents. This inconsistency means the verification plan and one report section are tracing to a wrong-product requirement.
challenge_questions: Which document version control step introduced '血压测量' into the PT9L verification plan and report, and has a formal correction or deviation been raised?

Is there a separate battery-life test report referenced in HW-053 ('电池使用寿命测试报告') that also contains the blood-pressure phrase, and if so, does it affect the validity of the battery verification conclusion?
Has the design verification plan (F0121) been reviewed and approved after the '血压测量' phrase was introduced, and by whom?

findings.claim: The PT9L total-assembly drawing (F0178) lists PT3-P10 dual-spring as BOM item 20, while the PT3-P10 drawing itself (F0176) states that PT9L production BOM uses separate springs PT5-M02 and PT5-M03 instead, and the ABOM (F0094) also lists PT3-P10; this unresolved conflict means the released assembly drawing and the drawing-level annotation are contradictory, creating a risk of wrong-part procurement or assembly.
findings.rationale: HW-092 (F0178, total assembly drawing) lists 'PT3-P10 双连弹簧' as item 20 with quantity 1. HW-088 (F0176, PT3-P10 drawing) confirms the drawing number is PT3-P10. However, HW-089 and HW-090 (F0176, same drawing, lines 81 and 89) explicitly state that PT9L production BOM uses PT5-M02 + PT5-M03 as separate parts and that PT3-P10 'does not necessarily enter the PT9L production BOM.' HW-039 (F0094, ABOM) also lists PT3-P10. No evidence in the supplied catalog shows PT5-M02 or PT5-M03 in any PT9L BOM line. The positive-spring drawing (HW-137, F0190) references PT5-M02 but only in the design-output drawing folder, not in any BOM line.
challenge_questions: Which part is actually installed in production units: PT3-P10 dual-spring or PT5-M02 + PT5-M03 separate springs, and is there a formal ECO or design change record resolving this?
If PT5-M02 and PT5-M03 are the production parts, why does the released total-assembly drawing (F0178 v1.0-20240627) still reference PT3-P10, and has the drawing been updated?
Does the ABOM (F0094) need to be revised to remove PT3-P10 and add PT5-M02/PT5-M03, and has a change request been initiated?

findings.claim: In the PT9L total-assembly drawing (F0178), part number T-Z1-P10 is assigned to the sensor PCB (item 11), yet the same drawing also lists a separate unnamed PCB at item 08, and the annotation flags that T-Z1-P10 simultaneously refers to both a bare board and a PCB assembly; this dual-use of one part number for two distinct items is a BOM integrity defect.
findings.rationale: HW-091 (F0178, line 7) contains the annotation 'BOM 中 T-Z1-P10 同时指导光板和 PCB（一图号两零件）⚠️'. HW-093 (F0178, line 51) shows item 11 as 'T-Z1-P10 / PCB ⚠️' and HW-094 (F0178, line 54) shows item 08 as an unnamed PCB. HW-095 and HW-096 (F0178, lines 72–73) describe item 08 as the main board PCB and item 11 as the sensor PCB. The EBOM (HW-040, HW-077) uses PT9L-HFMP01 V1.0 for the main PCB and PT9C-CNTP01 V1.0 for the sensor PCB, neither of which matches T-Z1-P10, further deepening the traceability gap between the assembly drawing and the EBOM.
challenge_questions: What is the correct and unique part number for the sensor PCB (item 11) in the PT9L assembly drawing, and has T-Z1-P10 been formally retired or reassigned?
Why does the assembly drawing use T-Z1-P10 while the EBOM uses PT9C-CNTP01 V1.0 for the sensor PCB — are these the same part, and if so, which number is the controlled identifier?
Has a drawing change notice been issued to resolve the one-number-two-parts anomaly flagged in the assembly drawing annotation?

findings.claim: Multiple T1 sample and prototype review checklists contain PCB-related inspection items (PCB fixation, PCB component interference, PCB dimension) with no pass/fail verdict recorded, meaning the hardware review evidence is incomplete and cannot demonstrate that these checks were actually performed.
findings.rationale: HW-014 (F0076, PT9L-T1 checklist item 20 'PCB固定'), HW-015 (item 21 'PCB元件与结构干涉检查'), and HW-016 (item 38 'PCB尺寸检查') all show '□通过 □不通过 □不适用' with no box checked. The same pattern appears in HW-017, HW-018, HW-019 (F0078, T1 checklist) and HW-020, HW-021, HW-022 (F0080, prototype checklist). All three checklists across two separate documents have identical blank verdicts for the same PCB inspection items. FMEA evidence (HW-012) identifies sensor PCB fixation as a severity-9 failure mode, making the blank PCB-fixation verdict particularly significant.
challenge_questions: Were the PCB fixation, interference, and dimension checks physically performed during T1 sample review, and if so, where are the recorded results?
Given that the structural FMEA (HW-012) assigns severity 9 to sensor PCB fixation failure, what compensating control exists if the checklist verdict for PCB fixation was never formally recorded?
Are the blank checklists the final released versions, or are there signed/completed versions in the DHF that were not captured in the evidence catalog?

findings.claim: The software test plan and test record apply an accuracy tolerance of ±0.2 °C to object-temperature mode measurements at 30 °C and 45 °C blackbody targets, but the design-input accuracy specification only mandates ±0.2 °C for the body-temperature range ≥35 °C and ≤42 °C; outside that range the requirement is ±0.3 °C, so the test plan imposes a tighter-than-specified tolerance at 30 °C and 45 °C without documented justification.
findings.rationale: HW-003 (F0031, design input) and HW-035 (F0090, inspection standard) both state: '≥35 °C and ≤42 °C: ±0.2 °C; other: ±0.3 °C.' HW-045 and HW-046 (F0101, software test plan lines 343–344) specify acceptance criteria of '30±0.2 °C' and '45±0.2 °C' for object-temperature mode blackbody tests. HW-048 and HW-049 (F0102, software test record lines 68–69) repeat the same ±0.2 °C criteria at 30 °C and 45 °C. Since 30 °C and 45 °C are outside the ≥35–42 °C range, the design input would permit ±0.3 °C at those points. Applying ±0.2 °C is more stringent than required; if units fail at ±0.2 °C but pass at ±0.3 °C, the test plan would incorrectly reject conforming product, or alternatively the tighter tolerance represents an undocumented design intent that has not been captured in the design input.
challenge_questions: Is the ±0.2 °C tolerance at 30 °C and 45 °C in the software test plan an intentional tighter requirement for object-temperature mode, and if so, has it been formally documented as a design input or design output specification?
Were any units rejected during software testing at 30 °C or 45 °C that would have passed under the ±0.3 °C design-input tolerance, and how were those dispositioned?

Should the design input (HW-003) be updated to separately specify accuracy requirements for object-temperature mode versus body-temperature mode, or should the test plan be corrected to use ±0.3 °C outside the 35–42 °C range?

mandatory_audit_matrix.check_goal: Verify that risk items, risk controls, and verification activities form a closed traceability chain.

assignment.review_focus: MATRIX-002 — Risk-to-verification traceability chain for PT9L. Verify that every risk item identified in the Risk Management Report (which references Bluetooth transmission per project profile) has: (a) an assigned risk control measure, (b) a corresponding verification or validation activity, and (c) a closed-loop record confirming the control was implemented and effective. Specifically check: whether PT2L risk document F0013 (which carries a PT9L document number internally) introduces any risk items or controls that are not re-evaluated under PT9L-specific conditions; whether Bluetooth-related hazards are fully traced to verification tests; and whether any risk items reference PT9C, PT3SBT, or BP3L without a documented rationale for applicability to PT9L.

agent_runs.summary: Cross-corpus scan of the PT9L DHF/DMR package reveals 14 candidate consistency issues spanning legacy product residue in active documents, document-number mismatches, unsigned approvals, wrong-product references in BOM and label documents, regulatory applicability conflicts, software diagram contamination, and blood-pressure-specific language appearing in a thermometer DHF.

Hardware audit of PT9L DHF/DMR reveals five substantive consistency findings: a blood-pressure residue phrase in the battery design-verification plan/report, an unresolved BOM conflict between PT3-P10 dual-spring and PT5-M02/M03 separate springs, a total-assembly drawing part-number anomaly (T-Z1-P10 used for two distinct PCBs), missing pass/fail verdicts in multiple T1 sample review checklists, and object-temperature mode accuracy tolerance (±0.2 °C) applied at 30 °C and 45 °C in software test plans despite the design-input accuracy specification only requiring ±0.2 °C for ≥35 °C and ≤42 °C.

llm_output.summary: The PT9L risk management file set contains multiple traceability chain breaks: the current Risk Management Report references document number PT9L-FXGB01 V1.0 while the active risk set has been revised to V2.0; the active Risk Management Plan carries document number IFT-FXJH01 rather than PT9L-FXJH01; F0013 (PT2L risk plan) internally carries a PT9L-series document number creating a product-identity conflict; no evidence of Bluetooth-specific hazard verification is present in the supplied corpus; DFMEA files (F0071, F0074) are not cross-referenced to the ISO 14971 risk assessment; and the design verification plan/report cites only PT9L-FXGB01 V1.0 while the current report is V2.0, leaving the closed-loop confirmation potentially misaligned.
review_notes: The four-document risk chain structure (Plan → Assessment → Control Verification → Report) is present for both the IFT product line (F0017–F0020) and the PT9L product line (F0021–F0024), which is a positive structural observation.

Version history entries in F0018 (RISK-040) and F0019 (RISK-045) confirm that the V2.0 revisions were made on 2024-05-30 and are traceable to named authors (Wang Di / Hou Guangwei), indicating a functioning change-control process for those documents.

The design verification plan (F0121) and report (F0114) both include ISO 14971:2019 as an applicable standard and reference the risk management report as the expected output, which is structurally correct.

Software design documents (F0135, F0139) contain hazard and control measure tables, indicating that software-level hazard analysis was initiated, though its linkage to the ISO 14971 risk assessment report is not confirmed by the supplied evidence.
The IEC 62366-1 checklist (F0243) cross-references ISO 14971:2019 and document PT9L-FXGB01 V1.0, providing partial usability-to-risk linkage.

findings.claim: The design verification report and the IEC 62366-1 checklist both cite the Risk Management Report as PT9L-FXGB01 V1.0, but the current active Risk Management Report in the DHF is V2.0 (dated 2024-05-30), meaning the closed-loop verification record does not confirm acceptance of the current risk management output.
findings.rationale: RISK-128 and RISK-129 (F0114, design verification report) reference 'PT9L-FXGB01 V1.0' as the risk management report that passed. RISK-138 (F0243, IEC 62366-1 checklist) also cites 'PT9L-FXGB01 V1.0'. However, RISK-049 and RISK-073 show that the active Risk Management Report files are titled V2.0 (20240530). The V2.0 report supersedes V1.0, but no updated design verification record or checklist citing V2.0 is present in the supplied evidence, leaving the traceability chain open at the verification closure step.
challenge_questions: Has the design verification report (F0114) been updated to reference PT9L-FXGB01 V2.0, and if so, where is that updated record?
What specific risk items or controls changed between V1.0 and V2.0 of the Risk Management Report, and were those changes re-verified?
Does the IEC 62366-1 checklist (F0243) have a V2 revision that references the V2.0 Risk Management Report?

findings.claim: The active Risk Management Plan filed under the PT9L DHF (F0017, F0021) carries document number IFT-FXJH01 V1.0, not PT9L-FXJH01, creating an ambiguity about whether the plan governing the PT9L risk file is the PT9L-specific plan or an IFT-product plan.
findings.rationale: RISK-032 (F0017) shows the document number as 'IFT-FXJH01 V1.0 Risk Management Plan'. RISK-056 (F0021) shows 'PT9L-FXJH01 V1.0 Risk Management Plan' for the PT9L-prefixed copy. However, the Risk Assessment Report (F0022, RISK-062) carries 'PT9L-FXPJ01 V1.0' and the Verification report (F0023, RISK-067) carries 'PT9L-FXYS01 V1.0', while the Risk Management Report (F0024, RISK-074) carries 'PT9L-FXGB01 V1.0'. The plan document number inconsistency (IFT vs PT9L prefix) means the downstream documents reference a plan that may not be formally identified as the PT9L plan, breaking the traceability chain at its first link.
challenge_questions: Is IFT-FXJH01 the same document as PT9L-FXJH01, or are these two distinct plans? If the same, which document number is the controlled identifier?
Do the Risk Assessment Report and Verification Report explicitly cite the plan by document number, and if so, which number do they cite?
Has a formal equivalence or supersession record been created to link IFT-FXJH01 to PT9L-FXJH01?

findings.claim: Document F0013, filed in the '2L风险改 - 历史文件' folder and titled as a PT2L risk management plan, internally carries the document number PT9L-FXJH01 V1.0, creating an unresolved product-identity conflict that could cause PT2L-specific risk items or acceptance criteria to be attributed to PT9L.
findings.rationale: RISK-007 shows the file title as 'V1.0-1 Risk Management Plan PT2L美亚-FXJH01 V1.0', indicating a PT2L product. However, RISK-008 shows the internal document number as 'PT9L-FXJH01 V1.0 Risk Management Plan', which is the same document number used for the PT9L plan. This means the same document number exists in two files with different product identities. Any risk item, acceptance criterion, or control measure derived from the PT2L plan that was carried forward under the PT9L document number has not been re-evaluated under PT9L-specific conditions per the project profile's primary scope rules.
challenge_questions: Were the risk acceptance criteria in F0013 (PT2L plan with PT9L document number) reviewed and confirmed as applicable to PT9L before being adopted?
Are there any hazards or risk control measures in F0013 that are specific to PT2L hardware or intended use that differ from PT9L?
What is the formal disposition of F0013 — is it superseded, withdrawn, or still considered a controlled document?

findings.claim: The project profile confirms PT9L transmits temperature data via Bluetooth, yet no evidence in the supplied corpus demonstrates that Bluetooth-related hazards (e.g., data integrity failure, unauthorized access, transmission error leading to incorrect clinical decision) have been identified in the risk assessment, assigned control measures, or verified through a documented test or validation activity.
findings.rationale: The Risk Management Report (F0024/F0020, RISK-073–RISK-078) and Risk Assessment Report (F0022, RISK-061–RISK-066) are present in the corpus but their content sections covering specific hazard entries are not supplied beyond table-of-contents lines. The design verification plan (F0121, RISK-130–RISK-134) and report (F0114, RISK-127–RISK-129) reference EMC testing and risk management report passage but contain no explicit Bluetooth data-integrity or cybersecurity hazard verification entry. The software test record (F0123, RISK-135) references WiFi auto-connect state detection but no Bluetooth transmission accuracy or failure-mode test. No evidence ID in the corpus links a Bluetooth hazard to a control measure and a closed verification record.
challenge_questions: In the Risk Assessment Report (PT9L-FXPJ01), is there a hazard entry specifically addressing Bluetooth transmission failure or data corruption, and what is its risk control measure reference?
Is there a software validation or integration test record that verifies Bluetooth data transmission accuracy and failure handling for PT9L?
Has a cybersecurity risk assessment been conducted for the Bluetooth feature, and is it referenced in the Risk Management Report?

findings.claim: The DFMEA files (F0071 packaging FMEA, F0074 structural FMEA) use a detection-ranking methodology but are not cross-referenced to the ISO 14971 risk assessment report or risk control verification report, leaving FMEA-identified failure modes potentially outside the closed ISO 14971 traceability chain.
findings.rationale: RISK-103 through RISK-114 show that F0071 and F0074 contain detailed DFMEA detection-ranking tables with design control criteria. However, none of the ISO 14971 risk documents in the corpus (F0018/F0022 Risk Assessment, F0019/F0023 Verification Report, F0020/F0024 Risk Management Report) contain evidence IDs that reference the DFMEA document numbers or cross-link FMEA failure modes to ISO 14971 hazard IDs. ISO 14971:2019 requires that all hazard identification inputs be documented; DFMEA is a recognized input method, but the linkage must be explicit.
challenge_questions: Does the Risk Assessment Report (PT9L-FXPJ01 V2.0) explicitly reference the DFMEA files as hazard identification inputs?
Are any DFMEA RPN-high items mapped to specific hazard IDs in the ISO 14971 risk assessment table?
Has a reconciliation been performed to confirm that all DFMEA failure modes with safety implications have corresponding entries in the ISO 14971 risk file?

findings.claim: The Risk Management Report document number PT9L-FXGB01 is used in both the PT9L-specific file (F0024, V1.0 internally) and the IFT-prefixed file (F0020, also V1.0 internally), while both are filed as V2.0 documents dated 2024-05-30, creating ambiguity about which report is the authoritative PT9L risk management closure document.
findings.rationale: RISK-050 (F0020) shows internal document number 'PT9L-FXGB01 V1.0' in a file titled 'IFT-FXGB01 V2.0'. RISK-074 (F0024) shows internal document number 'PT9L-FXGB01 V1.0' in a file titled 'PT9L--...IFT-FXGB01 V2.0'. Both files carry the same internal document number and version (V1.0) despite being filed as V2.0. The design verification report (RISK-128, RISK-129) cites 'PT9L-FXGB01 V1.0' as the passing document, which matches the internal number but not the file version. This version labeling inconsistency undermines confidence in which document represents the final approved risk management closure.
challenge_questions: Is PT9L-FXGB01 V1.0 (internal number) the same as the V2.0 file version, or does V2.0 represent a new controlled revision that should carry a new internal document number?
Which of F0020 and F0024 is the authoritative PT9L Risk Management Report, and has the other been formally superseded or withdrawn?
Does the document control system reconcile the internal document number version with the file revision version?

findings.claim: Software design documents (F0135, F0139) contain hazard and control measure tables, but no evidence in the corpus links these software-level hazards to specific entries in the ISO 14971 risk assessment report or to closed verification records confirming the software controls were implemented and effective.
findings.rationale: RISK-136 (F0135, software design) and RISK-137 (F0139, software requirements) both show hazard tables with columns for hazard, hazardous situation, and planned control measures. These are consistent with IEC 62304 / ISO 14971 software safety requirements. However, the Verification of Risk Control Measures report (F0019/F0023) and the Risk Management Report (F0020/F0024) do not have evidence IDs in the corpus that explicitly reference these software hazard table entries or confirm their verification status. The software test record (F0123, RISK-135) covers functional tests but does not reference hazard IDs.
challenge_questions: Are the hazard IDs in F0135 and F0139 software hazard tables mapped to corresponding hazard IDs in the ISO 14971 Risk Assessment Report?
Does the Verification of Risk Control Measures report (IFT-FXYS01 V2.0 or PT9L-FXYS01 V1.0) include a section specifically addressing software risk controls?
Is there a software-level residual risk evaluation that feeds into the overall residual risk acceptability conclusion in the Risk Management Report?

findings.claim: Multiple risk documents in the '2L风险改 - 历史文件' and '原版 - 历史文件' folders (F0012–F0016, F0025–F0028) remain in the DHF without explicit supersession records linking them to the current active documents, creating a risk that an auditor or reviewer could rely on outdated risk acceptance criteria or control measures.
findings.rationale: RISK-001 through RISK-030 cover F0012–F0016 (2L historical folder) and RISK-079 through RISK-102 cover F0025–F0028 (原版 historical folder). These documents include Risk Management Plans, Assessment Reports, Verification Reports, and Risk Management Reports at V1.0. The folder naming convention ('历史文件' = historical files) implies supersession, but no evidence ID in the corpus shows a formal change notice, supersession record, or document status field marking these as obsolete. ISO 14971:2019 requires the risk management file to be maintained and controlled; uncontrolled historical documents in the same DHF folder structure create traceability ambiguity.
challenge_questions: Is there a document control record (e.g., ECO or change notice) that formally obsoletes the documents in the '历史文件' folders and identifies their replacement documents?
Are the historical documents accessible to risk management team members in a way that could cause confusion with current controlled versions?
Do the current active risk documents (F0017–F0024) contain explicit statements identifying which prior documents they supersede?

findings.claim: The design verification report and the IEC 62366-1 checklist both cite the Risk Management Report as PT9L-FXGB01 V1.0, but the current active Risk Management Report in the DHF is V2.0 (dated 2024-05-30), meaning the closed-loop verification record does not confirm acceptance of the current risk management output.
findings.rationale: RISK-128 and RISK-129 (F0114, design verification report) reference 'PT9L-FXGB01 V1.0' as the risk management report that passed. RISK-138 (F0243, IEC 62366-1 checklist) also cites 'PT9L-FXGB01 V1.0'. However, RISK-049 and RISK-073 show that the active Risk Management Report files are titled V2.0 (20240530). The V2.0 report supersedes V1.0, but no updated design verification record or checklist citing V2.0 is present in the supplied evidence, leaving the traceability chain open at the verification closure step.
challenge_questions: Has the design verification report (F0114) been updated to reference PT9L-FXGB01 V2.0, and if so, where is that updated record?
What specific risk items or controls changed between V1.0 and V2.0 of the Risk Management Report, and were those changes re-verified?
Does the IEC 62366-1 checklist (F0243) have a V2 revision that references the V2.0 Risk Management Report?

findings.claim: The active Risk Management Plan filed under the PT9L DHF (F0017, F0021) carries document number IFT-FXJH01 V1.0, not PT9L-FXJH01, creating an ambiguity about whether the plan governing the PT9L risk file is the PT9L-specific plan or an IFT-product plan.
findings.rationale: RISK-032 (F0017) shows the document number as 'IFT-FXJH01 V1.0 Risk Management Plan'. RISK-056 (F0021) shows 'PT9L-FXJH01 V1.0 Risk Management Plan' for the PT9L-prefixed copy. However, the Risk Assessment Report (F0022, RISK-062) carries 'PT9L-FXPJ01 V1.0' and the Verification report (F0023, RISK-067) carries 'PT9L-FXYS01 V1.0', while the Risk Management Report (F0024, RISK-074) carries 'PT9L-FXGB01 V1.0'. The plan document number inconsistency (IFT vs PT9L prefix) means the downstream documents reference a plan that may not be formally identified as the PT9L plan, breaking the traceability chain at its first link.
challenge_questions: Is IFT-FXJH01 the same document as PT9L-FXJH01, or are these two distinct plans? If the same, which document number is the controlled identifier?
Do the Risk Assessment Report and Verification Report explicitly cite the plan by document number, and if so, which number do they cite?
Has a formal equivalence or supersession record been created to link IFT-FXJH01 to PT9L-FXJH01?

findings.claim: Document F0013, filed in the '2L风险改 - 历史文件' folder and titled as a PT2L risk management plan, internally carries the document number PT9L-FXJH01 V1.0, creating an unresolved product-identity conflict that could cause PT2L-specific risk items or acceptance criteria to be attributed to PT9L.
findings.rationale: RISK-007 shows the file title as 'V1.0-1 Risk Management Plan PT2L美亚-FXJH01 V1.0', indicating a PT2L product. However, RISK-008 shows the internal document number as 'PT9L-FXJH01 V1.0 Risk Management Plan', which is the same document number used for the PT9L plan. This means the same document number exists in two files with different product identities. Any risk item, acceptance criterion, or control measure derived from the PT2L plan that was carried forward under the PT9L document number has not been re-evaluated under PT9L-specific conditions per the project profile's primary scope rules.
challenge_questions: Were the risk acceptance criteria in F0013 (PT2L plan with PT9L document number) reviewed and confirmed as applicable to PT9L before being adopted?
Are there any hazards or risk control measures in F0013 that are specific to PT2L hardware or intended use that differ from PT9L?
What is the formal disposition of F0013 — is it superseded, withdrawn, or still considered a controlled document?

findings.claim: The project profile confirms PT9L transmits temperature data via Bluetooth, yet no evidence in the supplied corpus demonstrates that Bluetooth-related hazards (e.g., data integrity failure, unauthorized access, transmission error leading to incorrect clinical decision) have been identified in the risk assessment, assigned control measures, or verified through a documented test or validation activity.
findings.rationale: The Risk Management Report (F0024/F0020, RISK-073–RISK-078) and Risk Assessment Report (F0022, RISK-061–RISK-066) are present in the corpus but their content sections covering specific hazard entries are not supplied beyond table-of-contents lines. The design verification plan (F0121, RISK-130–RISK-134) and report (F0114, RISK-127–RISK-129) reference EMC testing and risk management report passage but contain no explicit Bluetooth data-integrity or cybersecurity hazard verification entry. The software test record (F0123, RISK-135) references WiFi auto-connect state detection but no Bluetooth transmission accuracy or failure-mode test. No evidence ID in the corpus links a Bluetooth hazard to a control measure and a closed verification record.
challenge_questions: In the Risk Assessment Report (PT9L-FXPJ01), is there a hazard entry specifically addressing Bluetooth transmission failure or data corruption, and what is its risk control measure reference?
Is there a software validation or integration test record that verifies Bluetooth data transmission accuracy and failure handling for PT9L?
Has a cybersecurity risk assessment been conducted for the Bluetooth feature, and is it referenced in the Risk Management Report?

findings.claim: The DFMEA files (F0071 packaging FMEA, F0074 structural FMEA) use a detection-ranking methodology but are not cross-referenced to the ISO 14971 risk assessment report or risk control verification report, leaving FMEA-identified failure modes potentially outside the closed ISO 14971 traceability chain.
findings.rationale: RISK-103 through RISK-114 show that F0071 and F0074 contain detailed DFMEA detection-ranking tables with design control criteria. However, none of the ISO 14971 risk documents in the corpus (F0018/F0022 Risk Assessment, F0019/F0023 Verification Report, F0020/F0024 Risk Management Report) contain evidence IDs that reference the DFMEA document numbers or cross-link FMEA failure modes to ISO 14971 hazard IDs. ISO 14971:2019 requires that all hazard identification inputs be documented; DFMEA is a recognized input method, but the linkage must be explicit.
challenge_questions: Does the Risk Assessment Report (PT9L-FXPJ01 V2.0) explicitly reference the DFMEA files as hazard identification inputs?
Are any DFMEA RPN-high items mapped to specific hazard IDs in the ISO 14971 risk assessment table?
Has a reconciliation been performed to confirm that all DFMEA failure modes with safety implications have corresponding entries in the ISO 14971 risk file?

findings.claim: The Risk Management Report document number PT9L-FXGB01 is used in both the PT9L-specific file (F0024, V1.0 internally) and the IFT-prefixed file (F0020, also V1.0 internally), while both are filed as V2.0 documents dated 2024-05-30, creating ambiguity about which report is the authoritative PT9L risk management closure document.
findings.rationale: RISK-050 (F0020) shows internal document number 'PT9L-FXGB01 V1.0' in a file titled 'IFT-FXGB01 V2.0'. RISK-074 (F0024) shows internal document number 'PT9L-FXGB01 V1.0' in a file titled 'PT9L--...IFT-FXGB01 V2.0'. Both files carry the same internal document number and version (V1.0) despite being filed as V2.0. The design verification report (RISK-128, RISK-129) cites 'PT9L-FXGB01 V1.0' as the passing document, which matches the internal number but not the file version. This version labeling inconsistency undermines confidence in which document represents the final approved risk management closure.
challenge_questions: Is PT9L-FXGB01 V1.0 (internal number) the same as the V2.0 file version, or does V2.0 represent a new controlled revision that should carry a new internal document number?
Which of F0020 and F0024 is the authoritative PT9L Risk Management Report, and has the other been formally superseded or withdrawn?
Does the document control system reconcile the internal document number version with the file revision version?

findings.claim: Software design documents (F0135, F0139) contain hazard and control measure tables, but no evidence in the corpus links these software-level hazards to specific entries in the ISO 14971 risk assessment report or to closed verification records confirming the software controls were implemented and effective.
findings.rationale: RISK-136 (F0135, software design) and RISK-137 (F0139, software requirements) both show hazard tables with columns for hazard, hazardous situation, and planned control measures. The software test record (F0123, RISK-135) covers functional tests but does not reference hazard IDs.

assignment.review_focus: MATRIX-003 — Software lifecycle traceability for PT9L. Verify that software requirements, architecture/design documents, unit and integration test records, software validation records, and the software traceability matrix are mutually consistent and all scoped to PT9L. Specifically investigate: (1) BP3L software diagrams appearing in the main PT9L software design folder and/or the T1 sample subfolder — determine whether these are shared-component references with documented rationale or erroneous inclusions; (2) whether the software version identifier in test records matches the version in the design document and the released BOM; (3) whether Bluetooth software requirements are traced to test cases and validation evidence; (4) whether any software document header, footer, or internal reference cites PT9C, PT3SBT, or BP3L as the primary product model without justification.

input_package.goal: Check software requirements, design, tests, validation, traceability, versioning, and legacy software artifact references.

mandatory_audit_matrix.check_goal: Verify that software requirements, design, test records, validation, and traceability records are consistent.

assignment.review_focus: MATRIX-003 — Software lifecycle traceability for PT9L. Verify that software requirements, architecture/design documents, unit and integration test records, software validation records, and the software traceability matrix are mutually consistent and all scoped to PT9L. Specifically investigate: (1) BP3L software diagrams appearing in the main PT9L software design folder and/or the T1 sample subfolder — determine whether these are shared-component references with documented rationale or erroneous inclusions; (2) whether the software version identifier in test records matches the version in the design document and the released BOM; (3) whether Bluetooth software requirements are traced to test cases and validation evidence; (4) whether any software document header, footer, or internal reference cites PT9C, PT3SBT, or BP3L as the primary product model without justification.

agent_runs.summary: Cross-corpus scan of the PT9L DHF/DMR package reveals 14 candidate consistency issues spanning legacy product residue in active documents, document-number mismatches, unsigned approvals, wrong-product references in BOM and label documents, regulatory applicability conflicts, software diagram contamination, and blood-pressure-specific language appearing in a thermometer DHF.

Hardware audit of PT9L DHF/DMR reveals five substantive consistency findings: a blood-pressure residue phrase in the battery design-verification plan/report, an unresolved BOM conflict between PT3-P10 dual-spring and PT5-M02/M03 separate springs, a total-assembly drawing part-number anomaly (T-Z1-P10 used for two distinct PCBs), missing pass/fail verdicts in multiple T1 sample review checklists, and object-temperature mode accuracy tolerance (±0.2 °C) applied at 30 °C and 45 °C in software test plans despite the design-input accuracy specification only requiring ±0.2 °C for ≥35 °C and ≤42 °C.

The PT9L risk management file set contains multiple traceability chain breaks: the current Risk Management Report references document number PT9L-FXGB01 V1.0 while the active risk set has been revised to V2.0; the active Risk Management Plan carries document number IFT-FXJH01 rather than PT9L-FXJH01; F0013 (PT2L risk plan) internally carries a PT9L-series document number creating a product-identity conflict; no evidence of Bluetooth-specific hazard verification is present in the supplied corpus; DFMEA files (F0071, F0074) are not cross-referenced to the ISO 14971 risk assessment; and the design verification plan/report cites only PT9L-FXGB01 V1.0 while the current report is V2.0, leaving the closed-loop confirmation potentially misaligned.

llm_output.summary: PT9L software lifecycle audit reveals five substantive findings: BP3L software diagrams appear in the primary PT9L software design folder and T1 sample subfolder without documented shared-component rationale; the software design document version identifier (E0 23.11) cannot be reconciled with the V1.0 identifier cited in test/validation records and BOM; no Bluetooth software requirements or corresponding test/validation evidence is present in the supplied corpus; the IEC 60601-1 test report references software design document DN:PT9L-RJFA01 V1.0 which does not appear in the evidence catalog; and a label review document filed under the active T1 sample folder carries PT2L as the primary product model without justification.
review_notes: SW-023 (PT9C设计确认E0 23.11) is scoped to PT9C; its presence in folder 18 is noted but may be a legitimate sub-component design confirmation — no software-specific inconsistency is independently raised here beyond what is already flagged by the Risk Traceability Agent.

SW-057 through SW-060 (clinical evaluation report referencing PT9CL/PT9C) are filed in a '废案与备份' (obsolete/backup) subfolder; this reduces but does not eliminate concern about residual product-model contamination.

SW-024 through SW-035 and SW-045 through SW-056 (IEC 62366-1 checklist and usability engineering file) consistently reference document CE-PT9L-12 version 1.0 and PT9L-SMSY01 version 1.0, which is internally consistent across both PDF and HTML renditions.

SW-050/SW-055/SW-056 show 'Software Design personnel: Wang Di' listed in the usability engineering file; this is noted as a personnel record observation with no inconsistency detected within the supplied evidence.

SW-062/SW-063 confirm that the IEC 60601-1 test report records a unique version identifier as 'P' (pass) for instructions for use, which is consistent with SW-013/SW-014 showing Version 1.0 in the PT9L operation guide.

findings.claim: BP3L software diagrams are present in both the primary PT9L software design folder (folder 07) and the T1 sample subfolder (folder 11) without any documented rationale establishing BP3L as a shared or reused software component of PT9L.
findings.rationale: SW-001 through SW-006 show 'BP3L 软件图样E0 23.11' residing in '07 软件设计方案E0 23.11\软件图样E0 23.11', which is the primary PT9L software design folder. SW-017 through SW-022 show the same titled document residing in '11 T1样机\软件文件底稿\软件图样E0 23.11'. The document title explicitly names BP3L — a different product model — as the subject. No evidence in the catalog establishes a documented shared-component relationship, a software reuse justification, or a configuration management record linking BP3L software to PT9L. The project profile confirms BP3L is a separate product family member and that cross-product references outside clearly marked historical folders require justification.
challenge_questions: Is BP3L a software component or sub-assembly of PT9L, and if so, where is the documented rationale (e.g., software reuse record, configuration item list) that establishes this relationship?

Why does the BP3L software diagram appear in both the primary software design folder (07) and the T1 sample subfolder (11) — are these two separate controlled copies, and if so, which is the authoritative version?
Has a software configuration management plan been established for PT9L that explicitly lists BP3L software diagrams as controlled inputs, and can that document be produced?

findings.claim: The software design documents use version identifier 'E0 23.11' while the operation guide, BOM, and IEC 60601-1 test report all use 'V1.0', and no version mapping or equivalence record is present in the supplied evidence to reconcile these two identifiers.
findings.rationale: SW-001 and SW-017 title the software diagram as 'BP3L 软件图样E0 23.11', using the 'E0 23.11' versioning scheme. SW-013 states 'Version 1.0' and SW-014 states 'Software version: V1.0' in the PT9L operation guide (F0083). SW-015 and SW-016 reference 'PT9C-CNTP01 V1.0' in the BOM, using the V-series scheme. SW-064 through SW-067 in the IEC 60601-1 test report cite 'Software design solutions DN:PT9L-RJFA01 V1.0' as the evidence for PEMS development lifecycle compliance. No document in the catalog maps 'E0 23.11' to 'V1.0' or explains whether these are parallel versioning schemes for different artifact types or a genuine mismatch. IEC 62304 and IEC 60601-1 clause 14 require that software version identifiers be unambiguous and traceable across lifecycle artifacts.
challenge_questions: What is the relationship between the 'E0 23.11' version designation used in the software diagram and the 'V1.0' designation used in the operation guide and test report — are these the same software release?
Is there a software version control table or release note that maps document revision codes (e.g., E0) to software version numbers (e.g., V1.0)?

Does the released BOM (PT9L-EBOM01 V1.0 and PT9L-T1EB01 V1.0) reference the software version that was validated, and can the traceability from BOM software version to validated software version be demonstrated?

findings.claim: The IEC 60601-1 test report cites 'Software design solutions DN:PT9L-RJFA01 V1.0' as the primary evidence for PEMS development lifecycle compliance, but this document does not appear anywhere in the supplied evidence catalog, creating an unverifiable traceability link.
findings.rationale: SW-064, SW-065, SW-066, and SW-067 all reference 'PT9L-RJFA01 V1.0' as the software design solutions document supporting PEMS lifecycle compliance under IEC 60601-1 clause 14. No evidence item in the catalog corresponds to document number PT9L-RJFA01. The project profile lists expected document ID patterns (PT9L-KHXQ01, PT9L-KXPS01, PT9L-FXJH01, PT9L-FXGB01, PT9L-EBOM01, PT9L-T1EB01, PT9L-SJSC01, PT9C-CNTP01) but PT9L-RJFA01 is absent. Without this document, the audit cannot confirm that the PEMS development lifecycle milestones, verification methods, and risk management integration cited as passing in the test report are actually documented.
challenge_questions: Can document PT9L-RJFA01 V1.0 ('Software design solutions') be produced for audit review?
Is PT9L-RJFA01 the same document as the software design plan referenced elsewhere in the DHF, or is it a separate artifact?
If PT9L-RJFA01 V1.0 has been superseded, which version was current at the time the IEC 60601-1 test report was issued, and has the test report been updated to reflect the current version?

findings.claim: The project profile confirms PT9L includes Bluetooth functionality, but no Bluetooth-specific software requirements, software design elements, test cases, or validation evidence appear in the supplied software lifecycle evidence, leaving the Bluetooth software sub-system without a demonstrable traceability chain.
findings.rationale: The project profile states 'PT9L can transmit temperature to smart device with Bluetooth (per Risk Management Report)'. SW-013 and SW-014 describe the operation guide at Version 1.0 with no Bluetooth software version or test reference visible. SW-064 through SW-067 reference the PEMS development lifecycle document PT9L-RJFA01 V1.0 but provide no Bluetooth-specific test or validation line items. SW-026 through SW-035 (IEC 62366-1 checklist) and SW-045 through SW-056 (usability engineering file) address usability but contain no Bluetooth software requirement traceability. challenge_questions: Where are the software requirements for the Bluetooth communication sub-system documented, and what document number and version do they carry?
What software test cases cover Bluetooth data transmission accuracy, connection reliability, and security, and have these tests been executed and recorded?
Is the Bluetooth module treated as a SOUP (software of unknown provenance) or OTS component under IEC 62304, and if so, where is the SOUP evaluation record?
Has the Bluetooth software been included in the software validation summary, and can the validation record be produced?

Is PT2L a market variant of PT9L sharing the same label artwork, and if so, where is the variant management record that authorizes shared label documentation?
Should this document be removed from the PT9L DHF, or does it require a cross-reference annotation to explain its relevance to PT9L?

primary_scope_rules: PT9L is the target product model for this DHF
Documents in '2L风险改 - 历史文件' folder are explicitly historical
Documents referencing PT2L, PT3SBT, BP3L, or PT9C outside clearly marked historical/draft folders require justification

key_entities.product_description: 红外非接触式额头温度计 (Infrared No-Touch Forehead Thermometer)
key_entities.intended_use: Intermittent measurement of body temperature from forehead skin surface on people of all ages; consumer home use and healthcare provider use
key_entities.bluetooth: PT9L can transmit temperature to smart device with Bluetooth (per Risk Management Report)

regulatory_baseline: EN ISO 80601-2-56:2017+A1:2018 (EU, applicability differs between draft and final design input)
MDR 2017/745 (EU, applicability differs between draft and final design input)
ISO 14971:2019 / EN ISO 14971:2019 / EN ISO 14971:2019/A11:2021 (risk management)
CE registration: applicability not yet determined per final design input
candidate_discovery_hints: PT9C appears as a sub-component PCB document number and as a standalone product in clinical evaluation and user test documents
PT3SBT appears in design output list two and a label review document filed under T1 sample folder
BP3L software diagrams appear in both the main software design folder and T1 sample subfolder
PT2L risk documents are in a '历史文件' subfolder but one (F0013) carries a PT9L document number internally

mandatory_audit_matrix.check_goal: Verify consistency across BOM, process, inspection, packaging, labels, drawings, and transfer records.

assignment.review_focus: MATRIX-004 — DMR chain consistency for PT9L. Verify consistency across: (a) Engineering BOM (PT9L-EBOM01) vs. manufacturing BOM and any released BOM revision; (b) process SOPs and work instructions vs. BOM line items; (c) incoming inspection and in-process inspection criteria vs. design output specifications; (d) packaging and labelling documents vs. approved label artwork and regulatory marking requirements; (e) design transfer records confirming DHF-to-DMR handoff completeness. Flag any BOM line item referencing PT9C, PT3SBT, or BP3L part numbers that lack a documented shared-component or sub-assembly justification. Also check whether PT3SBT references in the design output list and label review document filed under the T1 sample folder are reconciled with the released PT9L DMR.

agent_runs.summary: Cross-corpus scan of the PT9L DHF/DMR package reveals 14 candidate consistency issues spanning legacy product residue in active documents, document-number mismatches, unsigned approvals, wrong-product references in BOM and label documents, regulatory applicability conflicts, software diagram contamination, and blood-pressure-specific language appearing in a thermometer DHF.

Hardware audit of PT9L DHF/DMR reveals five substantive consistency findings: a blood-pressure residue phrase in the battery design-verification plan/report, an unresolved BOM conflict between PT3-P10 dual-spring and PT5-M02/M03 separate springs, a total-assembly drawing part-number anomaly (T-Z1-P10 used for two distinct PCBs), missing pass/fail verdicts in multiple T1 sample review checklists, and object-temperature mode accuracy tolerance (±0.2 °C) applied at 30 °C and 45 °C in software test plans despite the design-input accuracy specification only requiring ±0.2 °C for ≥35 °C and ≤42 °C.

The PT9L risk management file set contains multiple traceability chain breaks: the current Risk Management Report references document number PT9L-FXGB01 V1.0 while the active risk set has been revised to V2.0; the active Risk Management Plan carries document number IFT-FXJH01 rather than PT9L-FXJH01; F0013 (PT2L risk plan) internally carries a PT9L-series document number creating a product-identity conflict; no evidence of Bluetooth-specific hazard verification is present in the supplied corpus; DFMEA files (F0071, F0074) are not cross-referenced to the ISO 14971 risk assessment; and the design verification plan/report cites only PT9L-FXGB01 V1.0 while the current report is V2.0, leaving the closed-loop confirmation potentially misaligned.

PT9L software lifecycle audit reveals five substantive findings: BP3L software diagrams appear in the primary PT9L software design folder and T1 sample subfolder without documented shared-component rationale; the software design document version identifier (E0 23.11) cannot be reconciled with the V1.0 identifier cited in test/validation records and BOM; no Bluetooth software requirements or corresponding test/validation evidence is present in the supplied corpus; the IEC 60601-1 test report references software design document DN:PT9L-RJFA01 V1.0 which does not appear in the evidence catalog; and a label review document filed under the active T1 sample folder carries PT2L as the primary product model without justification.

llm_output.summary: DMR/SOP audit of PT9L design output chain reveals seven substantive findings including a document-number collision on drawing PT9L-F01, a part-number mismatch between the two packaging BOM files, PT3-origin shared-component drawings archived in the PT9L DHF without cross-product justification, an incomplete drawing title-block in a packaging label drawing, a missing outer-carton BOM entry in the primary packaging BOM, a process instruction referencing EBOM by document number without pinning a version, and the design output list carrying blank approval-date fields indicating the formal sign-off record is incomplete.
review_notes: EBOM PT9L-EBOM01 V1.0 (DMR-032 to DMR-037) is internally consistent: PCB line item PT9L-HFMP01 V1.0 matches the schematic drawing reference in the design output list (DMR-044 to DMR-048) and the SMT process instruction (DMR-021).

Process instruction PT9L-GYSM01 V1.0 (DMR-024, DMR-025) covers all major assembly steps (SMT, probe wire soldering, probe bracket assembly, firmware flash, functional test) and each step cites the relevant downstream document.
Tooling document PT9L-GZSM01 (DMR-026 to DMR-031) is consistent with the process instruction references to PT9L-CESHI and PT9L-SHAOXIE fixtures.

Packaging drawing PT9L-CBZP01 is at V2.0 in the drawing file (DMR-077) while the BOM entries in both packaging BOM files list it as V1.0 or without version; this version delta is noted but the drawing number itself is consistent.
Firmware target-code confirmation sheet PT9L-MBSC01 V1.0 (DMR-038, DMR-039) is present and references PT9L, consistent with the process instruction burn step (DMR-022).
Product defect definition PT9L (DMR-008 to DMR-010) and maintenance guide (DMR-006, DMR-007) are present and reference PT9L consistently.

Supplier drawing 75CEE0 (DMR-117 to DMR-122) is identified as an external supplier document; its presence in the DHF is noted but the functional role of the brass heat-sink sleeve in the PT9L assembly is not confirmed by any BOM line item in the supplied EBOM evidence.
