primary_scope_rules: PT9L is the target product model for this DHF
Documents in '2L风险改 - 历史文件' folder are explicitly historical
Documents referencing PT2L, PT3SBT, BP3L, or PT9C outside clearly marked historical/draft folders require justification

key_entities.product_description: 红外非接触式额头温度计 (Infrared No-Touch Forehead Thermometer)
key_entities.intended_use: Intermittent measurement of body temperature from forehead skin surface on people of all ages; consumer home use and healthcare provider use
key_entities.bluetooth: PT9L can transmit temperature to smart device with Bluetooth (per Risk Management Report)

regulatory_baseline: EN ISO 80601-2-56:2017+A1:2018 (EU, applicability differs between draft and final design input)
MDR 2017/745 (EU, applicability differs between draft and final design input)
ISO 14971:2019 / EN ISO 14971:2019 / EN ISO 14971:2019/A11:2021 (risk management)
CE registration: applicability not yet determined per final design input
candidate_discovery_hints: PT9C appears as a sub-component PCB document number and as a standalone product in clinical evaluation and user test documents
PT3SBT appears in design output list two and a label review document filed under T1 sample folder
BP3L software diagrams appear in both the main software design folder and T1 sample subfolder
PT2L risk documents are in a '历史文件' subfolder but one (F0013) carries a PT9L document number internally

mandatory_audit_matrix.check_goal: Verify controlled status, version history, review signatures, and document-control completeness across all stages.

assignment.review_focus: MATRIX-005 — Document control and regulatory completeness across all PT9L DHF/DMR stages. Verify: (1) controlled status, current revision level, and approval signatures for all documents matching PT9L document ID patterns (PT9L-KHXQ01, PT9L-KXPS01, PT9L-FXJH01, PT9L-FXGB01, PT9L-EBOM01, PT9L-T1EB01, PT9L-SJSC01) and PT9C-CNTP01; (2) whether the regulatory standard list is consistent between the draft design input and the final design input — specifically the applicability status of EN ISO 80601-2-56:2017+A1:2018, MDR 2017/745, and CE registration; (3) whether ASTM E1965-98:2016 and ASTM E1965-98:2023 are both cited and whether the transition between versions is documented; (4) whether the 510(k) registration responsibility assignment to 'andon' is documented in the DHF with a formal agreement or design transfer record; (5) whether PT9C-CNTP01 is a controlled PT9L DHF document or a standalone PT9C document incorrectly included, and whether its document-control record reflects the correct product scope.

agent_runs.summary: Cross-corpus scan of the PT9L DHF/DMR package reveals 14 candidate consistency issues spanning legacy product residue in active documents, document-number mismatches, unsigned approvals, wrong-product references in BOM and label documents, regulatory applicability conflicts, software diagram contamination, and blood-pressure-specific language appearing in a thermometer DHF.

Hardware audit of PT9L DHF/DMR reveals five substantive consistency findings: a blood-pressure residue phrase in the battery design-verification plan/report, an unresolved BOM conflict between PT3-P10 dual-spring and PT5-M02/M03 separate springs, a total-assembly drawing part-number anomaly (T-Z1-P10 used for two distinct PCBs), missing pass/fail verdicts in multiple T1 sample review checklists, and object-temperature mode accuracy tolerance (±0.2 °C) applied at 30 °C and 45 °C in software test plans despite the design-input accuracy specification only requiring ±0.2 °C for ≥35 °C and ≤42 °C.

The PT9L risk management file set contains multiple traceability chain breaks: the current Risk Management Report references document number PT9L-FXGB01 V1.0 while the active risk set has been revised to V2.0; the active Risk Management Plan carries document number IFT-FXJH01 rather than PT9L-FXJH01; F0013 (PT2L risk plan) internally carries a PT9L-series document number creating a product-identity conflict; no evidence of Bluetooth-specific hazard verification is present in the supplied corpus; DFMEA files (F0071, F0074) are not cross-referenced to the ISO 14971 risk assessment; and the design verification plan/report cites only PT9L-FXGB01 V1.0 while the current report is V2.0, leaving the closed-loop confirmation potentially misaligned.

PT9L software lifecycle audit reveals five substantive findings: BP3L software diagrams appear in the primary PT9L software design folder and T1 sample subfolder without documented shared-component rationale; the software design document version identifier (E0 23.11) cannot be reconciled with the V1.0 identifier cited in test/validation records and BOM; no Bluetooth software requirements or corresponding test/validation evidence is present in the supplied corpus; the IEC 60601-1 test report references software design document DN:PT9L-RJFA01 V1.0 which does not appear in the evidence catalog; and a label review document filed under the active T1 sample folder carries PT2L as the primary product model without justification.

DMR/SOP audit of PT9L design output chain reveals seven substantive findings including a document-number collision on drawing PT9L-F01, a part-number mismatch between the two packaging BOM files, PT3-origin shared-component drawings archived in the PT9L DHF without cross-product justification, an incomplete drawing title-block in a packaging label drawing, a missing outer-carton BOM entry in the primary packaging BOM, a process instruction referencing EBOM by document number without pinning a version, and the design output list carrying blank approval-date fields indicating the formal sign-off record is incomplete.

llm_output.summary: PT9L DHF regulatory audit identifies eight substantive findings spanning unsigned approval fields across all risk management documents, dual ASTM E1965 version citation without documented transition rationale, inconsistent EN ISO 80601-2-56 and MDR 2017/745 applicability between design input stages, absent 510(k) responsibility agreement for 'andon', biocompatibility reports conducted on PT5 samples rather than PT9L, IFT-prefixed document numbers on active PT9L risk management plans, a historical-folder risk plan (F0013) carrying a PT9L-series document number, and the operation guide referencing MDD rather than MDR for biocompatibility compliance.
review_notes: ISO 14971:2019, EN ISO 14971:2019, and EN ISO 14971:2019/A11:2021 are consistently cited as the governing risk management standards across all active risk documents (REG-002, REG-004, REG-016, REG-032, REG-047).

IEC 60601-1:2005+AMD1:2012+AMD2:2020 Ed.3.2 and IEC 60601-1-2:2014+A1:2020 Ed.4.1 are consistently cited in both the historical and active risk assessment reports (REG-007, REG-008, REG-010, REG-011, REG-020, REG-021, REG-036, REG-037, REG-049, REG-050, REG-052, REG-053).
IEC 60601-1-11:2015+A1:2020 is consistently cited for home healthcare environment applicability (REG-009, REG-010, REG-052).
Transport test reports (cold-hot cycle, compression, simulated transport) carry handwritten approval signatures per REG-138, REG-139, REG-140, which is consistent with physical test records.

The design verification plan and report both mark CE (EN ISO 80601-2-56) and MDR 2017/745 as not applicable (REG-120, REG-121, REG-127, REG-130), which is internally consistent between plan and report.
GB/T 16886 series (Parts 2, 5, 10, 12) are consistently cited across all five biocompatibility test reports (REG-088 through REG-116).
DFMEA files reference IEC 60601-1 marking durability requirements (REG-065, REG-066), indicating some traceability to the applicable safety standard.

findings.claim: All eight active and historical risk management documents in the PT9L DHF carry approval fields with no recorded date or named approver, rendering none of the risk management documents demonstrably approved under a controlled document system.
findings.rationale: Every risk management document in the evidence catalog — Risk Management Plans (REG-001, REG-003, REG-015, REG-031, REG-046), Risk Assessment Reports (REG-006, REG-019, REG-035, REG-048), Verification of Risk Control Measures reports (REG-012, REG-024, REG-040, REG-054), and Risk Management Reports (REG-013, REG-027, REG-043, REG-056) — shows the approval field as 'Approved by (Technical Director) Date:' with no actual signature, name, or date populated. ISO 14971:2019 requires that the risk management file be maintained under a controlled document system with defined responsibilities. Blank approval fields across all documents indicate that formal approval has not been recorded in the DHF corpus.
challenge_questions: Can the manufacturer produce signed paper originals or a document management system audit trail showing dated approvals for each of these risk management documents?
What is the document control procedure that governs approval of risk management file documents, and does it permit electronic or wet-ink signatures outside the document body?
If approvals exist only on physical originals, why are the digital DHF copies not updated to reflect the approved status, version, and date?

findings.claim: The active PT9L Risk Management Plan (F0017) and its PT9L-prefixed counterpart (F0021) both carry document number IFT-FXJH01 rather than PT9L-FXJH01, creating a product-identity mismatch in the controlled document numbering system.
findings.rationale: REG-014 shows the active Risk Management Plan file title as 'Attachment 7 01 Risk Management Plan IFT-FXJH01 V1.0 20240202-All applicable' and REG-030 shows the PT9L-prefixed version as 'PT9L--Attachment 7 01 Risk Management Plan IFT-FXJH01 V1.0 20240202-All applicable'. Both carry document number IFT-FXJH01, not PT9L-FXJH01 as required by the project document ID pattern. The project profile identifies PT9L-FXJH01 as the correct document number for the PT9L Risk Management Plan. An IFT-prefixed document number suggests the document originated for a different product (IFT) and was repurposed without a formal document number change, undermining traceability and controlled status.
challenge_questions: What product does the 'IFT' prefix designate, and is there a formal change record showing this document was re-scoped from IFT to PT9L?
Has a document number change request been raised to assign PT9L-FXJH01 to this plan, and if so, where is that record in the DHF?
Does the document control system treat IFT-FXJH01 and PT9L-FXJH01 as the same document or as separate controlled items?

findings.claim: Document F0013, filed in the '2L风险改 - 历史文件' folder and titled as a PT2L Risk Management Plan, internally carries a PT9L-series document number, creating an irreconcilable product-identity conflict in the controlled document record.
findings.rationale: REG-003 shows the approval field of F0013 (rel_path: '03 风险分析\2L风险改 - 历史文件\V1.0-1 Risk Management Plan PT2L美亚-FXJH01 V1.0') and REG-004 shows its risk management standard citation. The project profile primary scope rules note that F0013 'carries a PT9L document number internally' despite being a PT2L-titled document in a historical folder. A document that is simultaneously identified as PT2L in its title and PT9L in its internal document number cannot be unambiguously assigned to either product's controlled document system, and its presence in the DHF corpus without a formal cross-reference or obsolescence notice creates a traceability gap.
challenge_questions: What is the internal document number shown on F0013, and does it match PT9L-FXJH01 or another PT9L-series identifier?
Has F0013 been formally superseded or obsoleted in the document control system, and is there a change notice linking it to the current PT9L risk management plan?
Why does a PT2L historical document carry a PT9L document number — was this a copy-paste error during document creation, and has it been corrected in the current controlled version?

findings.claim: Both ASTM E1965-98:2016 and ASTM E1965-98:2023 are listed as applicable standards in the design input and design verification plan/report without any documented rationale for citing two versions simultaneously or a transition plan specifying which version governs conformance testing.
findings.rationale: REG-062 and REG-063 show both ASTM E1965-98:2016 and ASTM E1965-98:2023 marked as applicable (■是) in the design input. REG-128 and REG-129 repeat this dual applicability in the design verification plan, and REG-121 and REG-122 confirm both versions are listed as passed in the design verification report. REG-071 shows the label review references ASTM E1965-98:2023. REG-073 (operation guide) cites 'ASTM Standard(E1965-98)' without specifying a year. No evidence in the corpus documents why two editions of the same standard are simultaneously applicable, which edition takes precedence for 510(k) submission, or whether a formal standard transition assessment was conducted when the 2023 edition superseded the 2016 edition.
challenge_questions: What is the substantive technical difference between ASTM E1965-98:2016 and ASTM E1965-98:2023, and has a gap analysis been performed to confirm the device meets both editions?
Which edition of ASTM E1965-98 will be cited in the 510(k) submission, and is there a formal decision record in the DHF?
The operation guide (REG-073) omits the edition year for ASTM E1965-98 — will this be corrected before market release to specify the governing edition?

findings.claim: The project profile records that 510(k) registration responsibility is assigned to 'andon' as the responsible and paying party, but no formal agreement, design transfer record, or regulatory responsibility document evidencing this assignment is present in the supplied DHF evidence catalog.
findings.rationale: The project profile states '510(k) registration: andon responsible and paying' as part of the regulatory baseline. None of the 140 evidence items in the catalog reference a contract, memorandum of understanding, design transfer agreement, or regulatory filing responsibility document between the manufacturer and 'andon'. Under 21 CFR Part 807, the 510(k) submitter must be the legal manufacturer or their authorized representative, and the DHF should contain documentation establishing who holds this responsibility and under what terms. The absence of any such record in the DHF corpus means the regulatory submission chain cannot be verified from the design history file alone.
challenge_questions: Where in the DHF or quality management system is the formal agreement or contract with 'andon' that assigns 510(k) submission responsibility?
Is 'andon' the legal manufacturer, the US agent, or a contract regulatory affairs organization, and is this distinction documented?

findings.claim: All five biocompatibility test reports in the DHF were conducted on PT5 product samples, not PT9L samples, and no bridging justification or material equivalence assessment is present in the evidence catalog to support their applicability to PT9L.
findings.rationale: REG-088 through REG-116 cover five biocompatibility reports (cytotoxicity, two skin irritation, two skin sensitization) all filed under the path '11 T1样机\生物相容性\同PT5生物相容性报告\' with report IDs prefixed 'PT5-'. The operation guide (REG-074) states that materials ABS, TPU, PMMA, PC have passed ISO 10993-5 and ISO 10993-10, but the cited reports are for PT5. ISO 10993-1:2018 requires that biocompatibility evaluation be conducted on the actual device or on materials demonstrated to be equivalent. No material equivalence assessment, bridging study, or formal justification document linking PT5 biocompatibility data to PT9L is present in the evidence catalog.
challenge_questions: Is there a formal material equivalence assessment or biocompatibility bridging document in the DHF that demonstrates PT9L uses the same materials (ABS, TPU, PMMA, PC) in the same patient-contact configuration as PT5?
Were any material changes made between PT5 and PT9L that could affect biocompatibility, such as changes in colorants, surface treatments, or contact duration?
For the 510(k) submission, will new biocompatibility testing on PT9L samples be conducted, or will the PT5 data be submitted with a bridging rationale?

findings.claim: The PT9L operation guide states that patient-contact materials comply with 'Medical Device Directive (MDD) requirements', but MDD 93/42/EEC has been repealed and replaced by MDR 2017/745, making this a regulatory reference to a superseded directive.
findings.rationale: REG-074 states: 'They are in compliance with the Medical Device Directive (MDD) requirements.' MDR 2017/745 fully replaced MDD 93/42/EEC with effect from 26 May 2021. Referencing MDD in a document dated 20240828 (per REG-073 file name) is factually incorrect and could mislead notified bodies, regulators, or users about the applicable EU regulatory framework. This is compounded by the fact that the design input marks CE/MDR as not applicable (REG-064), making the MDD reference in the IFU internally inconsistent with the regulatory scope decision.
challenge_questions: Will the MDD reference in the operation guide be corrected to either remove the EU regulatory claim or update it to reference MDR 2017/745 before market release?
Given that the design input marks CE as not applicable, why does the operation guide contain any EU directive compliance statement for biocompatibility?
Is the WEEE Directive reference (REG-076) in the same operation guide also inconsistent with the decision to exclude EU market scope?

findings.claim: All eight active and historical risk management documents in the PT9L DHF carry approval fields with no recorded date or named approver, rendering none of the risk management documents demonstrably approved under a controlled document system.
findings.rationale: Every risk management document in the evidence catalog — Risk Management Plans (REG-001, REG-003, REG-015, REG-031, REG-046), Risk Assessment Reports (REG-006, REG-019, REG-035, REG-048), Verification of Risk Control Measures reports (REG-012, REG-024, REG-040, REG-054), and Risk Management Reports (REG-013, REG-027, REG-043, REG-056) — shows the approval field as 'Approved by (Technical Director) Date:' with no actual signature, name, or date populated. ISO 14971:2019 requires that the risk management file be maintained under a controlled document system with defined responsibilities. Blank approval fields across all documents indicate that formal approval has not been recorded in the DHF corpus.
challenge_questions: Can the manufacturer produce signed paper originals or a document management system audit trail showing dated approvals for each of these risk management documents?
What is the document control procedure that governs approval of risk management file documents, and does it permit electronic or wet-ink signatures outside the document body?
If approvals exist only on physical originals, why are the digital DHF copies not updated to reflect the approved status, version, and date?

findings.claim: The active PT9L Risk Management Plan (F0017) and its PT9L-prefixed counterpart (F0021) both carry document number IFT-FXJH01 rather than PT9L-FXJH01, creating a product-identity mismatch in the controlled document numbering system.
findings.rationale: REG-014 shows the active Risk Management Plan file title as 'Attachment 7 01 Risk Management Plan IFT-FXJH01 V1.0 20240202-All applicable' and REG-030 shows the PT9L-prefixed version as 'PT9L--Attachment 7 01 Risk Management Plan IFT-FXJH01 V1.0 20240202-All applicable'. Both carry document number IFT-FXJH01, not PT9L-FXJH01 as required by the project document ID pattern. The project profile identifies PT9L-FXJH01 as the correct document number for the PT9L Risk Management Plan. An IFT-prefixed document number suggests the document originated for a different product (IFT) and was repurposed without a formal document number change, undermining traceability and controlled status.
challenge_questions: What product does the 'IFT' prefix designate, and is there a formal change record showing this document was re-scoped from IFT to PT9L?
Has a document number change request been raised to assign PT9L-FXJH01 to this plan, and if so, where is that record in the DHF?
Does the document control system treat IFT-FXJH01 and PT9L-FXJH01 as the same document or as separate controlled items?

findings.claim: Document F0013, filed in the '2L风险改 - 历史文件' folder and titled as a PT2L Risk Management Plan, internally carries a PT9L-series document number, creating an irreconcilable product-identity conflict in the controlled document record.
findings.rationale: REG-003 shows the approval field of F0013 (rel_path: '03 风险分析\2L风险改 - 历史文件\V1.0-1 Risk Management Plan PT2L美亚-FXJH01 V1.0') and REG-004 shows its risk management standard citation. The project profile primary scope rules note that F0013 'carries a PT9L document number internally' despite being a PT2L-titled document in a historical folder. A document that is simultaneously identified as PT2L in its title and PT9L in its internal document number cannot be unambiguously assigned to either product's controlled document system, and its presence in the DHF corpus without a formal cross-reference or obsolescence notice creates a traceability gap.
challenge_questions: What is the internal document number shown on F0013, and does it match PT9L-FXJH01 or another PT9L-series identifier?
Has F0013 been formally superseded or obsoleted in the document control system, and is there a change notice linking it to the current PT9L risk management plan?
Why does a PT2L historical document carry a PT9L document number — was this a copy-paste error during document creation, and has it been corrected in the current controlled version?

assignment.review_focus: Close the verification gap analysis for PT9L. Specifically: (1) Determine whether any verification or validation record in the DHF corpus confirms that the object-temperature mode accuracy tolerance of ±0.2 °C applied at 30 °C and 45 °C in software test plans is intentional and justified against the design-input specification (which requires ±0.2 °C only for ≥35 °C and ≤42 °C body-temperature range). (2) Determine whether any V&V record addresses Bluetooth-specific hazards or Bluetooth functional verification for PT9L, given that the Risk Management Report acknowledges Bluetooth transmission capability but no Bluetooth hazard verification evidence was found by the Risk Traceability Agent. (3) Determine whether the battery design-verification plan/report blood-pressure residue phrase (identified by Hardware Agent) appears in a pass/fail verdict section or only in a boilerplate/template section, and whether the overall battery verification record carries a signed pass verdict. (4) Identify whether any verification record explicitly references the PT9L-FXGB01 V2.0 risk report (rather than V1.0) as the controlling risk document for verification closure. (5) Confirm whether the IEC 60601-1 test report referencing software design document DN:PT9L-RJFA01 V1.0 (noted by Software Agent as absent from the evidence catalog) has any corresponding entry in the design output list or verification index.

primary_scope_rules: PT9L is the target product model for this DHF
Documents in '2L风险改 - 历史文件' folder are explicitly historical
Documents referencing PT2L, PT3SBT, BP3L, or PT9C outside clearly marked historical/draft folders require justification

key_entities.product_description: 红外非接触式额头温度计 (Infrared No-Touch Forehead Thermometer)
key_entities.intended_use: Intermittent measurement of body temperature from forehead skin surface on people of all ages; consumer home use and healthcare provider use
key_entities.bluetooth: PT9L can transmit temperature to smart device with Bluetooth (per Risk Management Report)

regulatory_baseline: EN ISO 80601-2-56:2017+A1:2018 (EU, applicability differs between draft and final design input)
MDR 2017/745 (EU, applicability differs between draft and final design input)
ISO 14971:2019 / EN ISO 14971:2019 / EN ISO 14971:2019/A11:2021 (risk management)
CE registration: applicability not yet determined per final design input
candidate_discovery_hints: PT9C appears as a sub-component PCB document number and as a standalone product in clinical evaluation and user test documents
PT3SBT appears in design output list two and a label review document filed under T1 sample folder
BP3L software diagrams appear in both the main software design folder and T1 sample subfolder
PT2L risk documents are in a '历史文件' subfolder but one (F0013) carries a PT9L document number internally

assignment.review_focus: Close the verification gap analysis for PT9L. Specifically: (1) Determine whether any verification or validation record in the DHF corpus confirms that the object-temperature mode accuracy tolerance of ±0.2 °C applied at 30 °C and 45 °C in software test plans is intentional and justified against the design-input specification (which requires ±0.2 °C only for ≥35 °C and ≤42 °C body-temperature range). (2) Determine whether any V&V record addresses Bluetooth-specific hazards or Bluetooth functional verification for PT9L, given that the Risk Management Report acknowledges Bluetooth transmission capability but no Bluetooth hazard verification evidence was found by the Risk Traceability Agent. (3) Determine whether the battery design-verification plan/report blood-pressure residue phrase (identified by Hardware Agent) appears in a pass/fail verdict section or only in a boilerplate/template section, and whether the overall battery verification record carries a signed pass verdict. (4) Identify whether any verification record explicitly references the PT9L-FXGB01 V2.0 risk report (rather than V1.0) as the controlling risk document for verification closure. (5) Confirm whether the IEC 60601-1 test report referencing software design document DN:PT9L-RJFA01 V1.0 (noted by Software Agent as absent from the evidence catalog) has any corresponding entry in the design output list or verification index.

agent_runs.summary: Cross-corpus scan of the PT9L DHF/DMR package reveals 14 candidate consistency issues spanning legacy product residue in active documents, document-number mismatches, unsigned approvals, wrong-product references in BOM and label documents, regulatory applicability conflicts, software diagram contamination, and blood-pressure-specific language appearing in a thermometer DHF.

Hardware audit of PT9L DHF/DMR reveals five substantive consistency findings: a blood-pressure residue phrase in the battery design-verification plan/report, an unresolved BOM conflict between PT3-P10 dual-spring and PT5-M02/M03 separate springs, a total-assembly drawing part-number anomaly (T-Z1-P10 used for two distinct PCBs), missing pass/fail verdicts in multiple T1 sample review checklists, and object-temperature mode accuracy tolerance (±0.2 °C) applied at 30 °C and 45 °C in software test plans despite the design-input accuracy specification only requiring ±0.2 °C for ≥35 °C and ≤42 °C.

The PT9L risk management file set contains multiple traceability chain breaks: the current Risk Management Report references document number PT9L-FXGB01 V1.0 while the active risk set has been revised to V2.0; the active Risk Management Plan carries document number IFT-FXJH01 rather than PT9L-FXJH01; F0013 (PT2L risk plan) internally carries a PT9L-series document number creating a product-identity conflict; no evidence of Bluetooth-specific hazard verification is present in the supplied corpus; DFMEA files (F0071, F0074) are not cross-referenced to the ISO 14971 risk assessment; and the design verification plan/report cites only PT9L-FXGB01 V1.0 while the current report is V2.0, leaving the closed-loop confirmation potentially misaligned.

PT9L software lifecycle audit reveals five substantive findings: BP3L software diagrams appear in the primary PT9L software design folder and T1 sample subfolder without documented shared-component rationale; the software design document version identifier (E0 23.11) cannot be reconciled with the V1.0 identifier cited in test/validation records and BOM; no Bluetooth software requirements or corresponding test/validation evidence is present in the supplied corpus; the IEC 60601-1 test report references software design document DN:PT9L-RJFA01 V1.0 which does not appear in the evidence catalog; and a label review document filed under the active T1 sample folder carries PT2L as the primary product model without justification.

DMR/SOP audit of PT9L design output chain reveals seven substantive findings including a document-number collision on drawing PT9L-F01, a part-number mismatch between the two packaging BOM files, PT3-origin shared-component drawings archived in the PT9L DHF without cross-product justification, an incomplete drawing title-block in a packaging label drawing, a missing outer-carton BOM entry in the primary packaging BOM, a process instruction referencing EBOM by document number without pinning a version, and the design output list carrying blank approval-date fields indicating the formal sign-off record is incomplete.

PT9L DHF regulatory audit identifies eight substantive findings spanning unsigned approval fields across all risk management documents, dual ASTM E1965 version citation without documented transition rationale, inconsistent EN ISO 80601-2-56 and MDR 2017/745 applicability between design input stages, absent 510(k) responsibility agreement for 'andon', biocompatibility reports conducted on PT5 samples rather than PT9L, IFT-prefixed document numbers on active PT9L risk management plans, a historical-folder risk plan (F0013) carrying a PT9L-series document number, and the operation guide referencing MDD rather than MDR for biocompatibility compliance.

llm_output.summary: PT9L V&V corpus audit reveals five substantive findings: object-temperature accuracy tolerance applied outside the design-input specified range without documented justification; no Bluetooth hazard or functional verification evidence present; blood-pressure residue phrase in battery verification record with no confirmed signed pass verdict in supplied evidence; no verification record references the controlling risk document at V2.0; and the IEC 60601-1 test report's cited software design document (PT9L-RJFA01 V1.0) is absent from the evidence catalog and design output index.
review_notes: External formal test reports ETX202303-07-078-01 through -05 and -03R1 are all present in the evidence catalog (VV-035 through VV-070) with consistent report numbers across final and draft versions, indicating the external lab report set is substantially complete.

The design verification report (VV-010 through VV-015) correctly maps ISO 80601-2-56:2017/Amd1:2018 and ASTM E1965-98:2016/2023 to ETX202303-07-078-03 and -04 as the supporting test reports; the cross-reference structure is internally consistent for those rows.

EN ISO 80601-2-56:2017+A1:2018, EN 12470-3, and EN 12470-5 are marked 'not applicable' (□是 ■否) in the design verification report (VV-011, VV-012, VV-013), which is consistent with the regulatory agent's finding that EU applicability was revised; this is noted but not re-raised here as it is already captured in RUN-0006.

Usability engineering file (VV-016 through VV-027) documents two formative evaluations and establishes acceptance criteria for the summative evaluation; the plan structure is internally consistent across the PDF and HTML renditions (F0247, F0248).

A revised ISO 80601-2-56 test report ETX202303-07-078-03R1 (VV-065 through VV-070) dated 2025-05-29 is present alongside the original -03 report dated 2025-02-12; the design verification report (VV-010) cites only -03 and -04, not -03R1, suggesting the verification closure row has not been updated to reflect the revised report.

Draft test reports (VV-078 through VV-101) are present in a '草稿' subfolder; the draft for -02 carries a truncated report number 'ETX2023-07-078-02' (VV-086, VV-087, VV-088, VV-089) rather than 'ETX202303-07-078-02', which is a minor formatting inconsistency in the draft only and does not affect the final report.

Risk management acceptance criteria are referenced to PT9L-FXJH01 V1.0 in both risk management reports (VV-002, VV-004); no evidence in the supplied catalog confirms that plan document is the current controlled version.

findings.claim: The object-temperature mode accuracy tolerance of ±0.2 °C is applied at 30 °C and 45 °C in software test plans, but no V&V record in the supplied evidence corpus justifies this extension beyond the design-input specified body-temperature accuracy range of ≥35 °C to ≤42 °C; the gap is unresolved in the verification closure evidence.
findings.rationale: The Hardware Agent (RUN-0002) and Software Agent (RUN-0004) both identified that software test plans apply ±0.2 °C at 30 °C and 45 °C while the design input (VV-005, VV-028) specifies ±0.2 °C only for the body-temperature range ≥35 °C to ≤42 °C. No evidence ID in the supplied catalog contains a documented engineering rationale, design input amendment, or verification plan note that explicitly authorises the ±0.2 °C tolerance at 30 °C and 45 °C for object-temperature mode. The design verification report rows (VV-010 through VV-015) address standard compliance but do not contain a tolerance-range justification entry. Without such justification, the verification record cannot be considered closed against the design input.
challenge_questions: Is there a design input amendment or engineering change order that explicitly extends the ±0.2 °C accuracy requirement to the 30 °C–45 °C object-temperature range, and if so, what is its document number and approval date?

Does the software test plan contain a rationale section explaining why object-temperature mode is tested at 30 °C and 45 °C with the same tolerance as body-temperature mode, and has that rationale been reviewed and approved by the design team?
Has the design verification report been updated to include a row that maps the object-temperature accuracy tolerance to the specific test points and the applicable design input requirement?

findings.claim: No Bluetooth-specific hazard analysis, Bluetooth functional verification plan, or Bluetooth validation record for PT9L is present in the supplied evidence corpus, despite the Risk Management Report acknowledging Bluetooth transmission capability as a product feature.
findings.rationale: The Risk Traceability Agent (RUN-0003) confirmed that the risk management reports (VV-001 through VV-004) acknowledge Bluetooth transmission but no Bluetooth hazard verification evidence was found. The Software Agent (RUN-0004) independently confirmed no Bluetooth software requirements or test evidence is present. The external test reports in the catalog (VV-029 through VV-101) cover EMC (ETX202303-07-078-01), safety (ETX202303-07-078-02), ISO 80601-2-56 performance (ETX202303-07-078-03/-03R1), ASTM E1965 performance (ETX202303-07-078-04), and aging (ETX202303-07-078-05); none of these report titles or numbers correspond to a Bluetooth-specific test. The usability engineering file (VV-016 through VV-027) does not address Bluetooth interaction hazards. The design verification report (VV-010 through VV-015) contains no row referencing Bluetooth verification. This constitutes a complete absence of Bluetooth V&V closure evidence.
challenge_questions: Is there a Bluetooth-specific hazard analysis document (e.g., a DFMEA row or ISO 14971 risk worksheet) for PT9L, and if so, what is its document number and where is it filed in the DHF?
Has a Bluetooth functional verification test been conducted for PT9L, and if so, what is the test report number and where is the pass verdict recorded?
Does the design verification report contain a row for Bluetooth functionality, and if not, has a formal decision been made and documented to exclude Bluetooth from the verification scope?

findings.claim: The battery design-verification record contains a blood-pressure residue phrase identified by the Hardware Agent, and no evidence in the supplied catalog confirms that the battery verification record carries a signed pass verdict; the verification closure status for battery performance cannot be confirmed from available evidence.
findings.rationale: The Hardware Agent (RUN-0002) identified a blood-pressure residue phrase in the battery design-verification plan/report. The supplied evidence catalog (VV-001 through VV-101) does not contain any evidence ID corresponding to a battery verification report with a signed pass verdict for PT9L. The external test reports present (VV-035 through VV-070) cover EMC, safety, thermometry performance, and aging; none is identified as a battery-specific verification report. The design verification report rows visible in the catalog (VV-010 through VV-015) address standard compliance rows only. The presence of blood-pressure language in a thermometer battery verification record raises the possibility that the document is a repurposed template from a blood-pressure product, which would call into question whether the acceptance criteria and test conditions are appropriate for PT9L.
challenge_questions: Does the battery design-verification plan/report contain a signed approval block with a pass verdict, and if so, what are the approver name, role, and date?
Has the blood-pressure residue phrase in the battery verification record been reviewed and determined to be inapplicable boilerplate, and is that determination documented?
Are the battery acceptance criteria in the verification record derived from the PT9L design input specification, and is there a traceability link between the two documents?

findings.claim: No verification record in the supplied evidence corpus explicitly references PT9L-FXGB01 V2.0 as the controlling risk document for verification closure; all available cross-references point to V1.0, leaving the verification loop potentially open against the current risk baseline.
findings.rationale: The Risk Traceability Agent (RUN-0003) established that the active risk management report is PT9L-FXGB01 V2.0 (VV-001 through VV-004 are from F0020 and F0024, both titled V2.0 20240530). The design verification report (VV-010 through VV-015) does not contain any explicit citation of PT9L-FXGB01 at any version. The risk management reports themselves (VV-002, VV-004) reference the risk management plan as PT9L-FXJH01 V1.0 but do not confirm that verification activities were closed against V2.0 of the risk report. No other evidence ID in the catalog contains a statement linking verification closure to V2.0. If V2.0 introduced new or revised risks relative to V1.0, those risks may not have been addressed in the verification plan.
challenge_questions: What changes were made between PT9L-FXGB01 V1.0 and V2.0, and were any new or revised risks introduced that require new or updated verification activities?
Has the design verification plan been updated to reference PT9L-FXGB01 V2.0 as the controlling risk document, and if not, is there a documented rationale for why V1.0 remains the reference?
Is there a verification closure review record that explicitly confirms all risks in V2.0 of the risk management report have been addressed by corresponding verification or validation activities?

findings.claim: The software design document PT9L-RJFA01 V1.0, cited in the IEC 60601-1 test report as the controlling software design document, is absent from the evidence catalog and cannot be confirmed as present in the design output list or verification index, creating an unresolved traceability gap between the external safety test report and the software design baseline.
findings.rationale: The Software Agent (RUN-0004) identified that the IEC 60601-1 test report (ETX202303-07-078-02, present as VV-041 through VV-046 for the final version and VV-084 through VV-089 for the draft) references software design document DN:PT9L-RJFA01 V1.0. No evidence ID in the supplied catalog corresponds to a document with identifier PT9L-RJFA01. The design verification report rows (VV-010 through VV-015) do not contain a row referencing PT9L-RJFA01. The design input summary (VV-005, VV-028) does not list PT9L-RJFA01 as a design output. If the software design document cited in the safety test report does not exist in the DHF or has a different document number, the test report cannot be fully traced to the design baseline, and the safety test closure is incomplete.
challenge_questions: Does PT9L-RJFA01 V1.0 exist as a controlled document in the DHF, and if so, why does it not appear in the evidence catalog supplied for this audit?

If PT9L-RJFA01 V1.0 does not exist, what software design document was actually used as the basis for the IEC 60601-1 safety test, and has the test report been corrected to reference the correct document number and version?
Is PT9L-RJFA01 listed in the design output list with an approval date, and does the version cited in the test report match the version approved at the time of testing?

findings.claim: The design verification report cites ETX202303-07-078-03 as the ISO 80601-2-56 test evidence, but a revised report ETX202303-07-078-03R1 dated 2025-05-29 is present in the evidence catalog; the verification closure row has not been updated to reference the current revision of the test report.
findings.rationale: VV-010 shows the design verification report row for ISO 80601-2-56:2017/Amd1:2018 citing 'ETX202303-07-078-03/ETX202303-07-078-04' as the supporting evidence. VV-065 through VV-070 confirm that a revised report ETX202303-07-078-03R1 (dated 2025-05-29) exists in the final reports folder. The original -03 report is dated 2025-02-12 (VV-047 through VV-052). The existence of a revision (R1) implies that the original report was superseded, yet the design verification report still references the original -03. If -03R1 was issued to correct a deficiency or retest finding in -03, the verification closure row referencing -03 may be based on a superseded and potentially non-passing report.
challenge_questions: What was the reason for issuing ETX202303-07-078-03R1, and did the original report ETX202303-07-078-03 contain a failing result or a scope limitation that necessitated retesting?
Has the design verification report been updated to replace the reference to ETX202303-07-078-03 with ETX202303-07-078-03R1, and if not, when is that update planned?
Does the verification closure decision for ISO 80601-2-56 compliance rely on -03 or -03R1, and is that decision documented with the approver's signature and date?

findings.claim: The object-temperature mode accuracy tolerance of ±0.2 °C is applied at 30 °C and 45 °C in software test plans, but no V&V record in the supplied evidence corpus justifies this extension beyond the design-input specified body-temperature accuracy range of ≥35 °C to ≤42 °C; the gap is unresolved in the verification closure evidence.
findings.rationale: The Hardware Agent (RUN-0002) and Software Agent (RUN-0004) both identified that software test plans apply ±0.2 °C at 30 °C and 45 °C while the design input (VV-005, VV-028) specifies ±0.2 °C only for the body-temperature range ≥35 °C to ≤42 °C. No evidence ID in the supplied catalog contains a documented engineering rationale, design input amendment, or verification plan note that explicitly authorises the ±0.2 °C tolerance at 30 °C and 45 °C for object-temperature mode. The design verification report rows (VV-010 through VV-015) address standard compliance but do not contain a tolerance-range justification entry. Without such justification, the verification record cannot be considered closed against the design input.
challenge_questions: Is there a design input amendment or engineering change order that explicitly extends the ±0.2 °C accuracy requirement to the 30 °C–45 °C object-temperature range, and if so, what is its document number and approval date?

Does the software test plan contain a rationale section explaining why object-temperature mode is tested at 30 °C and 45 °C with the same tolerance as body-temperature mode, and has that rationale been reviewed and approved by the design team?
Has the design verification report been updated to include a row that maps the object-temperature accuracy tolerance to the specific test points and the applicable design input requirement?

findings.claim: No Bluetooth-specific hazard analysis, Bluetooth functional verification plan, or Bluetooth validation record for PT9L is present in the supplied evidence corpus, despite the Risk Management Report acknowledging Bluetooth transmission capability as a product feature.
findings.rationale: The Risk Traceability Agent (RUN-0003) confirmed that the risk management reports (VV-001 through VV-004) acknowledge Bluetooth transmission but no Bluetooth hazard verification evidence was found. The Software Agent (RUN-0004) independently confirmed no Bluetooth software requirements or test evidence is present. The external test reports in the catalog (VV-029 through VV-101) cover EMC (ETX202303-07-078-01), safety (ETX202303-07-078-02), ISO 80601-2-56 performance (ETX202303-07-078-03/-03R1), ASTM E1965 performance (ETX202303-07-078-04), and aging (ETX202303-07-078-05); none of these report titles or numbers correspond to a Bluetooth-specific test. The usability engineering file (VV-016 through VV-027) does not address Bluetooth interaction hazards. The design verification report (VV-010 through VV-015) contains no row referencing Bluetooth verification. This constitutes a complete absence of Bluetooth V&V closure evidence.
challenge_questions: Is there a Bluetooth-specific hazard analysis document (e.g., a DFMEA row or ISO 14971 risk worksheet) for PT9L, and if so, what is its document number and where is it filed in the DHF?
Has a Bluetooth functional verification test been conducted for PT9L, and if so, what is the test report number and where is the pass verdict recorded?
Does the design verification report contain a row for Bluetooth functionality, and if not, has a formal decision been made and documented to exclude Bluetooth from the verification scope?

findings.claim: The battery design-verification record contains a blood-pressure residue phrase identified by the Hardware Agent, and no evidence in the supplied catalog confirms that the battery verification record carries a signed pass verdict; the verification closure status for battery performance cannot be confirmed from available evidence.
findings.rationale: The Hardware Agent (RUN-0002) identified a blood-pressure residue phrase in the battery design-verification plan/report. The supplied evidence catalog (VV-001 through VV-101) does not contain any evidence ID corresponding to a battery verification report with a signed pass verdict for PT9L. The external test reports present (VV-035 through VV-070) cover EMC, safety, thermometry performance, and aging; none is identified as a battery-specific verification report. The design verification report rows visible in the catalog (VV-010 through VV-015) address standard compliance rows only. The presence of blood-pressure language in a thermometer battery verification record raises the possibility that the document is a repurposed template from a blood-pressure product, which would call into question whether the acceptance criteria and test conditions are appropriate for PT9L.
challenge_questions: Does the battery design-verification plan/report contain a signed approval block with a pass verdict, and if so, what are the approver name, role, and date?
Has the blood-pressure residue phrase in the battery verification record been reviewed and determined to be inapplicable boilerplate, and is that determination documented?
Are the battery acceptance criteria in the verification record derived from the PT9L design input specification, and is there a traceability link between the two documents?

findings.claim: No verification record in the supplied evidence corpus explicitly references PT9L-FXGB01 V2.0 as the controlling risk document for verification closure; all available cross-references point to V1.0, leaving the verification loop potentially open against the current risk baseline.
findings.rationale: The Risk Traceability Agent (RUN-0003) established that the active risk management report is PT9L-FXGB01 V2.0 (VV-001 through VV-004 are from F0020 and F0024, both titled V2.0 20240530). The design verification report (VV-010 through VV-015) does not contain any explicit citation of PT9L-FXGB01 at any version. The risk management reports themselves (VV-002, VV-004) reference the risk management plan as PT9L-FXJH01 V1.0 but do not confirm that verification activities were closed against V2.0 of the risk report. No other evidence ID in the catalog contains a statement linking verification closure to V2.0. If V2.0 introduced new or revised risks relative to V1.0, those risks may not have been addressed in the verification plan.
challenge_questions: What changes were made between PT9L-FXGB01 V1.0 and V2.0, and were any new or revised risks introduced that require new or updated verification activities?
Has the design verification plan been updated to reference PT9L-FXGB01 V2.0 as the controlling risk document, and if not, is there a documented rationale for why V1.0 remains the reference?
Is there a verification closure review record that explicitly confirms all risks in V2.0 of the risk management report have been addressed by corresponding verification or validation activities?

assignment.review_focus: Perform a cross-finding synthesis and escalation assessment across all completed agent runs (RUN-0002 through RUN-0006) to support final report assembly. Specifically: (1) Assess whether the IFT-prefixed document number on the active Risk Management Plan (IFT-FXJH01 vs. expected PT9L-FXJH01) constitutes a document-control nonconformance under the applicable SOP or whether it is a known legacy prefix with a documented transition record. (2) Assess whether the F0013 PT2L risk plan carrying a PT9L-series document number internally (identified by both Risk Traceability Agent and Regulatory Agent) represents a single root cause or two distinct nonconformances requiring separate corrective actions. (3) Assess whether the biocompatibility reports conducted on PT5 samples rather than PT9L samples are covered by any equivalence or shared-component justification in the DHF, or whether this constitutes an unmitigated gap for 510(k) and CE submissions. (4) Assess whether the operation guide reference to MDD rather than MDR for biocompatibility compliance is a live document in the controlled release set or a draft/historical artifact. (5) Identify any findings across all agent runs that, in combination, suggest a systemic document-control process failure (e.g., unsigned approvals appearing across risk, design output, and DMR documents simultaneously) that should be flagged as a systemic finding rather than individual point findings. (6) Confirm whether the dual ASTM E1965 version citation (1998:2016 and 1998:2023) appears in the same document or in different documents at different design stages, and whether any transition rationale document exists in the corpus.
