primary_scope_rules: PT9L is the target product model for this DHF
Documents in '2L风险改 - 历史文件' folder are explicitly historical
Documents referencing PT2L, PT3SBT, BP3L, or PT9C outside clearly marked historical/draft folders require justification

key_entities.product_description: 红外非接触式额头温度计 (Infrared No-Touch Forehead Thermometer)
key_entities.intended_use: Intermittent measurement of body temperature from forehead skin surface on people of all ages; consumer home use and healthcare provider use
key_entities.bluetooth: PT9L can transmit temperature to smart device with Bluetooth (per Risk Management Report)

regulatory_baseline: EN ISO 80601-2-56:2017+A1:2018 (EU, applicability differs between draft and final design input)
MDR 2017/745 (EU, applicability differs between draft and final design input)
ISO 14971:2019 / EN ISO 14971:2019 / EN ISO 14971:2019/A11:2021 (risk management)
CE registration: applicability not yet determined per final design input
candidate_discovery_hints: PT9C appears as a sub-component PCB document number and as a standalone product in clinical evaluation and user test documents
PT3SBT appears in design output list two and a label review document filed under T1 sample folder
BP3L software diagrams appear in both the main software design folder and T1 sample subfolder
PT2L risk documents are in a '历史文件' subfolder but one (F0013) carries a PT9L document number internally

mandatory_audit_matrix.check_goal: Verify controlled status, version history, review signatures, and document-control completeness across all stages.

assignment.review_focus: Perform a cross-finding synthesis and escalation assessment across all completed agent runs (RUN-0002 through RUN-0006) to support final report assembly. Specifically: (1) Assess whether the IFT-prefixed document number on the active Risk Management Plan (IFT-FXJH01 vs. expected PT9L-FXJH01) constitutes a document-control nonconformance under the applicable SOP or whether it is a known legacy prefix with a documented transition record. (2) Assess whether the F0013 PT2L risk plan carrying a PT9L-series document number internally (identified by both Risk Traceability Agent and Regulatory Agent) represents a single root cause or two distinct nonconformances requiring separate corrective actions. (3) Assess whether the biocompatibility reports conducted on PT5 samples rather than PT9L samples are covered by any equivalence or shared-component justification in the DHF, or whether this constitutes an unmitigated gap for 510(k) and CE submissions. (4) Assess whether the operation guide reference to MDD rather than MDR for biocompatibility compliance is a live document in the controlled release set or a draft/historical artifact. (5) Identify any findings across all agent runs that, in combination, suggest a systemic document-control process failure (e.g., unsigned approvals appearing across risk, design output, and DMR documents simultaneously) that should be flagged as a systemic finding rather than individual point findings. (6) Confirm whether the dual ASTM E1965 version citation (1998:2016 and 1998:2023) appears in the same document or in different documents at different design stages, and whether any transition rationale document exists in the corpus.

agent_runs.summary: Cross-corpus scan of the PT9L DHF/DMR package reveals 14 candidate consistency issues spanning legacy product residue in active documents, document-number mismatches, unsigned approvals, wrong-product references in BOM and label documents, regulatory applicability conflicts, software diagram contamination, and blood-pressure-specific language appearing in a thermometer DHF.

Hardware audit of PT9L DHF/DMR reveals five substantive consistency findings: a blood-pressure residue phrase in the battery design-verification plan/report, an unresolved BOM conflict between PT3-P10 dual-spring and PT5-M02/M03 separate springs, a total-assembly drawing part-number anomaly (T-Z1-P10 used for two distinct PCBs), missing pass/fail verdicts in multiple T1 sample review checklists, and object-temperature mode accuracy tolerance (±0.2 °C) applied at 30 °C and 45 °C in software test plans despite the design-input accuracy specification only requiring ±0.2 °C for ≥35 °C and ≤42 °C.

The PT9L risk management file set contains multiple traceability chain breaks: the current Risk Management Report references document number PT9L-FXGB01 V1.0 while the active risk set has been revised to V2.0; the active Risk Management Plan carries document number IFT-FXJH01 rather than PT9L-FXJH01; F0013 (PT2L risk plan) internally carries a PT9L-series document number creating a product-identity conflict; no evidence of Bluetooth-specific hazard verification is present in the supplied corpus; DFMEA files (F0071, F0074) are not cross-referenced to the ISO 14971 risk assessment; and the design verification plan/report cites only PT9L-FXGB01 V1.0 while the current report is V2.0, leaving the closed-loop confirmation potentially misaligned.

PT9L software lifecycle audit reveals five substantive findings: BP3L software diagrams appear in the primary PT9L software design folder and T1 sample subfolder without documented shared-component rationale; the software design document version identifier (E0 23.11) cannot be reconciled with the V1.0 identifier cited in test/validation records and BOM; no Bluetooth software requirements or corresponding test/validation evidence is present in the supplied corpus; the IEC 60601-1 test report references software design document DN:PT9L-RJFA01 V1.0 which does not appear in the evidence catalog; and a label review document filed under the active T1 sample folder carries PT2L as the primary product model without justification.

DMR/SOP audit of PT9L design output chain reveals seven substantive findings including a document-number collision on drawing PT9L-F01, a part-number mismatch between the two packaging BOM files, PT3-origin shared-component drawings archived in the PT9L DHF without cross-product justification, an incomplete drawing title-block in a packaging label drawing, a missing outer-carton BOM entry in the primary packaging BOM, a process instruction referencing EBOM by document number without pinning a version, and the design output list carrying blank approval-date fields indicating the formal sign-off record is incomplete.

PT9L DHF regulatory audit identifies eight substantive findings spanning unsigned approval fields across all risk management documents, dual ASTM E1965 version citation without documented transition rationale, inconsistent EN ISO 80601-2-56 and MDR 2017/745 applicability between design input stages, absent 510(k) responsibility agreement for 'andon', biocompatibility reports conducted on PT5 samples rather than PT9L, IFT-prefixed document numbers on active PT9L risk management plans, a historical-folder risk plan (F0013) carrying a PT9L-series document number, and the operation guide referencing MDD rather than MDR for biocompatibility compliance.

PT9L V&V corpus audit reveals five substantive findings: object-temperature accuracy tolerance applied outside the design-input specified range without documented justification; no Bluetooth hazard or functional verification evidence present; blood-pressure residue phrase in battery verification record with no confirmed signed pass verdict in supplied evidence; no verification record references the controlling risk document at V2.0; and the IEC 60601-1 test report's cited software design document (PT9L-RJFA01 V1.0) is absent from the evidence catalog and design output index.

llm_output.summary: Cross-run synthesis audit of the PT9L DHF/DMR package identifies six substantive regulatory and document-control findings, including one systemic finding covering unsigned approvals across all risk management documents, plus resolution assessments on five specific escalation questions raised by the orchestrator.
review_notes: All risk management documents in the active set (F0017–F0020, F0021–F0024) consistently cite ISO 14971:2019, EN ISO 14971:2019, and EN ISO 14971:2019/A11:2021 as the governing standard, which is appropriate for the declared regulatory baseline.

The dual ASTM E1965 version citation (1998:2016 and 1998:2023) appears in the same design input document (F0031) and the same design verification report (F0114) and verification plan (F0121), not across separate design stages; both versions are marked applicable.

Biocompatibility reports (F0104–F0108) are conducted under GB/T 16886 series standards, which are the Chinese equivalents of ISO 10993; the operation guide (F0083) separately cites ISO 10993-5 and ISO 10993-10 for patient-contact materials.
Transport test reports (F0143, F0144, F0145) carry handwritten approval signatures per the evidence text, distinguishing them from the risk management documents where approval fields are blank.

The label review document (F0082) references PT2L document numbers (PT2L-ZXBQ01 through PT2L-ZXBQ06) in the controlled-document column, which is consistent with the RUN-0004 and RUN-0006 findings and is not re-raised as a new finding here.
No transition rationale document, legacy-prefix registry, or IFT-to-PT9L document-number mapping record was located in the supplied evidence catalog.

findings.claim: Unsigned approval fields appear simultaneously across all active risk management documents, all historical risk management documents, and the design output list, constituting a systemic document-control process failure rather than isolated point deficiencies.
findings.rationale: Every risk management document in the active PT9L set carries a blank 'Approved by (Technical Director) Date:' field: F0017 (REG-015), F0018 (REG-019), F0019 (REG-024), F0020 (REG-027), F0021 (REG-031), F0022 (REG-035), F0023 (REG-040), F0024 (REG-043). The same pattern is present in all historical-folder documents: F0012 (REG-001), F0013 (REG-003), F0014 (REG-006), F0015 (REG-012), F0016 (REG-013), F0025 (REG-046), F0026 (REG-048), F0027 (REG-054), F0028 (REG-056). RUN-0005 independently identified blank approval-date fields in the design output list. RUN-0007 confirmed no signed pass verdict is present in the battery verification record. The simultaneous absence of completed approval signatures across risk management, design output, and verification documents spanning multiple product variants and multiple document versions indicates that the document-control SOP governing approval capture is either not being enforced or is not functioning. This cannot be attributed to a single document author or a single review cycle; it is a process-level gap requiring a corrective action at the SOP and training level, not merely document-by-document remediation.
challenge_questions: Can the manufacturer produce a document-control SOP that specifies the required approval workflow, and can it demonstrate that this SOP was in effect during the periods when these documents were created or revised?

Is there a separate wet-ink or electronic signature record maintained outside the document body that constitutes the formal approval record for these files? If so, where is it stored and how is it linked to each document version?

Has a root-cause analysis been performed to determine why approval fields are blank across documents spanning at least two product variants (PT9L and PT2L) and at least two version cycles (V1.0 and V2.0)?
What corrective action has been or will be taken at the process level, beyond retroactively completing individual approval fields?

findings.claim: The active PT9L Risk Management Plan carries document number IFT-FXJH01 rather than the expected PT9L-FXJH01, and no legacy-prefix registry, transition record, or documented equivalence mapping was found in the supplied corpus, making this a document-control nonconformance rather than a known managed legacy prefix.
findings.rationale: F0017 is titled 'Attachment 7 01 Risk Management Plan IFT-FXJH01 V1.0 20240202-All applicable' (REG-014) and its approval field references the same IFT-FXJH01 identifier (REG-015). The project profile lists the expected document number as PT9L-FXJH01. RUN-0003 and RUN-0006 both flagged this. The orchestrator's escalation question (ASG-0008 item 1) asks whether this is a known legacy prefix with a documented transition record. No such record appears in the evidence catalog. The PT9L-prefixed document number pattern is used consistently for other PT9L documents (e.g., PT9L-FXGB01 per REG-026, REG-042). The IFT prefix is not explained anywhere in the supplied evidence. Absent a documented transition record or legacy-prefix registry, this constitutes a document-control nonconformance: the controlled document number does not match the product identifier, creating a traceability gap for regulators reviewing the 510(k) or CE technical file.
challenge_questions: Does a document-number registry or legacy-prefix mapping table exist that formally equates IFT-FXJH01 to PT9L-FXJH01, and if so, in which controlled document is it maintained?
Was the IFT prefix assigned by a customer, a notified body, or an internal legacy system, and is there a change-control record documenting the transition from IFT to PT9L numbering?
Has the 510(k) submission or CE technical file been prepared using the IFT-FXJH01 document number, and if so, does the submission index reconcile this to the PT9L product identity?

findings.claim: F0013 (PT2L risk management plan) internally carries a PT9L-series document number, representing two distinct nonconformances—a product-identity mismatch and a document-number assignment error—that share a single root cause but require separate corrective actions.
findings.rationale: REG-003 and REG-004 show F0013 is filed as a PT2L risk management plan (path: '03 风险分析\2L风险改 - 历史文件\V1.0-1 Risk Management Plan PT2L美亚-FXJH01 V1.0') yet the document internally carries the identifier FXJH01 which is the same functional suffix as the PT9L Risk Management Plan (IFT-FXJH01 / PT9L-FXJH01). The orchestrator's escalation question (ASG-0008 item 2) asks whether this is one root cause or two distinct nonconformances. Assessment: the root cause is likely a copy-paste or template-reuse error during document creation, but the resulting nonconformances are distinct: (a) a product-identity nonconformance—a PT2L product document contains PT9L-series numbering, creating ambiguity about which product's risk file is authoritative; and (b) a document-number assignment nonconformance—the same functional document number suffix (FXJH01) is assigned to risk management plans for two different products without a documented shared-document or family-document justification. These require separate corrective actions because (a) requires a product-scope clarification and possible re-issuance of the PT2L document under a PT2L-specific number, while (b) requires a document-number registry review to ensure no other cross-product number collisions exist.
challenge_questions: Was F0013 intentionally created as a PT2L-specific document, or was it intended to be a shared risk management plan covering both PT2L and PT9L under a family approach? If the latter, where is the family-device justification?
Has a document-number collision check been performed across all products in the PT9L product family to identify other instances where the same document-number suffix is used for different products?
What is the disposition of F0013 in the current PT9L DHF—is it referenced as supporting evidence, as a historical artifact, or as an active controlled document?

findings.claim: Biocompatibility testing was conducted on PT5 samples rather than PT9L samples, and no equivalence justification, shared-component declaration, or bridging rationale document was found in the supplied corpus, leaving an unmitigated gap for both 510(k) and CE submissions.
findings.rationale: F0104–F0108 (REG-088 through REG-116) are all filed under the path '11 T1样机\生物相容性\同PT5生物相容性报告\' and are explicitly titled with 'PT5' sample identifiers. The operation guide (F0083, REG-074) states that patient-contact materials (ABS, TPU, PMMA, PC) have passed ISO 10993-5 and ISO 10993-10 tests, but does not identify the test samples as PT9L. The orchestrator's escalation question (ASG-0008 item 3) asks whether any equivalence or shared-component justification exists in the DHF. No such document appears in the evidence catalog. For a 510(k) submission, FDA expects biocompatibility testing to be conducted on the actual device or a documented equivalent; a bridging memo citing identical materials, identical suppliers, and identical manufacturing processes would be required. For CE under MDR 2017/745, Annex I Chapter II requires biocompatibility evaluation of the actual device. The absence of any bridging or equivalence record in the corpus means this gap is currently unmitigated.
challenge_questions: Is there a biocompatibility equivalence memo or shared-component declaration that documents that PT5 and PT9L use identical patient-contact materials from identical suppliers with identical manufacturing processes? If so, in which controlled document is it maintained and what is its document number?
Were the PT5 biocompatibility tests conducted on the same material grades and formulations as those specified in the PT9L BOM and material specifications?
Has the 510(k) submission package included a biocompatibility bridging rationale, and has FDA accepted it? Has the CE technical file addressed this under MDR Annex I Chapter II?

findings.claim: The PT9L operation guide (F0083) references MDD rather than MDR 2017/745 for biocompatibility compliance, and this document is filed in the active T1 sample folder without a draft or historical designation, making it a live document-control issue rather than a historical artifact.
findings.rationale: REG-074 shows F0083 states: 'They are in compliance with the Medical Device Directive (MDD) requirements.' The file path is '11 T1样机\PT9L-operation guide-20240828.via_lo_html.clean.md' with a date stamp of 20240828 (28 August 2024). MDD 93/42/EEC was repealed and replaced by MDR 2017/745, which became fully applicable on 26 May 2021. A document dated August 2024 referencing MDD rather than MDR is not a historical artifact—it is a current document with an incorrect regulatory reference. The orchestrator's escalation question (ASG-0008 item 4) asks whether this is a live document or a draft/historical artifact. The date stamp and active folder location confirm it is live. This creates a compliance gap for any CE submission and may also mislead users about the applicable regulatory framework.
challenge_questions: Has the operation guide (F0083, dated 20240828) been released to production or included in any regulatory submission? If so, which submissions and what is the remediation plan?
Is there a controlled document review process that checks regulatory references for currency at each document revision? If so, why did the MDD reference survive to a document dated August 2024?
Does the CE technical file for PT9L reference this operation guide, and if so, has the notified body or EU authorized representative been notified of the incorrect regulatory citation?

findings.claim: Both ASTM E1965-98:2016 and ASTM E1965-98:2023 are cited as applicable in the same design input document and the same design verification plan and report, but no transition rationale, version-selection justification, or test-to-standard mapping document was found in the corpus.
findings.rationale: REG-062 and REG-063 show F0031 lists both ASTM E1965-98:2016 and ASTM E1965-98:2023 as applicable US standards. REG-128 and REG-129 show F0121 (design verification plan) lists both as applicable with the same verification method. REG-121 and REG-122 show F0114 (design verification report) lists both as passed. REG-071 shows the label review (F0082) references ASTM E1965-98:2023. The orchestrator's escalation question (ASG-0008 item 6) asks whether the dual citation appears in the same document or across different design stages. Assessment: both versions appear in the same documents at the same design stage, not as a staged transition. No transition rationale, version-comparison analysis, or test-to-standard mapping document appears in the corpus. For a 510(k) submission, FDA will expect the manufacturer to identify which version of ASTM E1965 was used for testing and to justify compliance with that version. Citing both without differentiation creates ambiguity about which standard governs the device's performance claims.
challenge_questions: Were the accuracy and performance tests conducted against ASTM E1965-98:2016, ASTM E1965-98:2023, or both? Which test report documents the results against each version?
What are the substantive differences between ASTM E1965-98:2016 and ASTM E1965-98:2023 that are relevant to PT9L, and has a gap analysis been performed?
Is the 510(k) submission claiming compliance with both versions simultaneously, and if so, has FDA guidance on standard version selection been consulted?

findings.claim: Unsigned approval fields appear simultaneously across all active risk management documents, all historical risk management documents, and the design output list, constituting a systemic document-control process failure rather than isolated point deficiencies.
findings.rationale: Every risk management document in the active PT9L set carries a blank 'Approved by (Technical Director) Date:' field: F0017 (REG-015), F0018 (REG-019), F0019 (REG-024), F0020 (REG-027), F0021 (REG-031), F0022 (REG-035), F0023 (REG-040), F0024 (REG-043). The same pattern is present in all historical-folder documents: F0012 (REG-001), F0013 (REG-003), F0014 (REG-006), F0015 (REG-012), F0016 (REG-013), F0025 (REG-046), F0026 (REG-048), F0027 (REG-054), F0028 (REG-056). RUN-0005 independently identified blank approval-date fields in the design output list. RUN-0007 confirmed no signed pass verdict is present in the battery verification record. The simultaneous absence of completed approval signatures across risk management, design output, and verification documents spanning multiple product variants and multiple document versions indicates that the document-control SOP governing approval capture is either not being enforced or is not functioning. This cannot be attributed to a single document author or a single review cycle; it is a process-level gap requiring a corrective action at the SOP and training level, not merely document-by-document remediation.
challenge_questions: Can the manufacturer produce a document-control SOP that specifies the required approval workflow, and can it demonstrate that this SOP was in effect during the periods when these documents were created or revised?

Is there a separate wet-ink or electronic signature record maintained outside the document body that constitutes the formal approval record for these files? If so, where is it stored and how is it linked to each document version?

Has a root-cause analysis been performed to determine why approval fields are blank across documents spanning at least two product variants (PT9L and PT2L) and at least two version cycles (V1.0 and V2.0)?
What corrective action has been or will be taken at the process level, beyond retroactively completing individual approval fields?

findings.claim: The active PT9L Risk Management Plan carries document number IFT-FXJH01 rather than the expected PT9L-FXJH01, and no legacy-prefix registry, transition record, or documented equivalence mapping was found in the supplied corpus, making this a document-control nonconformance rather than a known managed legacy prefix.
findings.rationale: F0017 is titled 'Attachment 7 01 Risk Management Plan IFT-FXJH01 V1.0 20240202-All applicable' (REG-014) and its approval field references the same IFT-FXJH01 identifier (REG-015). The project profile lists the expected document number as PT9L-FXJH01. RUN-0003 and RUN-0006 both flagged this. The orchestrator's escalation question (ASG-0008 item 1) asks whether this is a known legacy prefix with a documented transition record. No such record appears in the evidence catalog. The PT9L-prefixed document number pattern is used consistently for other PT9L documents (e.g., PT9L-FXGB01 per REG-026, REG-042). The IFT prefix is not explained anywhere in the supplied evidence. Absent a documented transition record or legacy-prefix registry, this constitutes a document-control nonconformance: the controlled document number does not match the product identifier, creating a traceability gap for regulators reviewing the 510(k) or CE technical file.
challenge_questions: Does a document-number registry or legacy-prefix mapping table exist that formally equates IFT-FXJH01 to PT9L-FXJH01, and if so, in which controlled document is it maintained?
Was the IFT prefix assigned by a customer, a notified body, or an internal legacy system, and is there a change-control record documenting the transition from IFT to PT9L numbering?
Has the 510(k) submission or CE technical file been prepared using the IFT-FXJH01 document number, and if so, does the submission index reconcile this to the PT9L product identity?

findings.claim: F0013 (PT2L risk management plan) internally carries a PT9L-series document number, representing two distinct nonconformances—a product-identity mismatch and a document-number assignment error—that share a single root cause but require separate corrective actions.
findings.rationale: REG-003 and REG-004 show F0013 is filed as a PT2L risk management plan (path: '03 风险分析\2L风险改 - 历史文件\V1.0-1 Risk Management Plan PT2L美亚-FXJH01 V1.0') yet the document internally carries the identifier FXJH01 which is the same functional suffix as the PT9L Risk Management Plan (IFT-FXJH01 / PT9L-FXJH01). The orchestrator's escalation question (ASG-0008 item 2) asks whether this is one root cause or two distinct nonconformances. Assessment: the root cause is likely a copy-paste or template-reuse error during document creation, but the resulting nonconformances are distinct: (a) a product-identity nonconformance—a PT2L product document contains PT9L-series numbering, creating ambiguity about which product's risk file is authoritative; and (b) a document-number assignment nonconformance—the same functional document number suffix (FXJH01) is assigned to risk management plans for two different products without a documented shared-document or family-document justification. These require separate corrective actions because (a) requires a product-scope clarification and possible re-issuance of the PT2L document under a PT2L-specific number, while (b) requires a document-number registry review to ensure no other cross-product number collisions exist.
challenge_questions: Was F0013 intentionally created as a PT2L-specific document, or was it intended to be a shared risk management plan covering both PT2L and PT9L under a family approach? If the latter, where is the family-device justification?
Has a document-number collision check been performed across all products in the PT9L product family to identify other instances where the same document-number suffix is used for different products?
What is the disposition of F0013 in the current PT9L DHF—is it referenced as supporting evidence, as a historical artifact, or as an active controlled document?

findings.claim: Biocompatibility testing was conducted on PT5 samples rather than PT9L samples, and no equivalence justification, shared-component declaration, or bridging rationale document was found in the supplied corpus, leaving an unmitigated gap for both 510(k) and CE submissions.
findings.rationale: F0104–F0108 (REG-088 through REG-116) are all filed under the path '11 T1样机\生物相容性\同PT5生物相容性报告\' and are explicitly titled with 'PT5' sample identifiers. The operation guide (F0083, REG-074) states that patient-contact materials (ABS, TPU, PMMA, PC) have passed ISO 10993-5 and ISO 10993-10 tests, but does not identify the test samples as PT9L. The orchestrator's escalation question (ASG-0008 item 3) asks whether any equivalence or shared-component justification exists in the DHF. No such document appears in the evidence catalog. For a 510(k) submission, FDA expects biocompatibility testing to be conducted on the actual device or a documented equivalent; a bridging memo citing identical materials, identical suppliers, and identical manufacturing processes would be required. For CE under MDR 2017/745, Annex I Chapter II requires biocompatibility evaluation of the actual device. The absence of any bridging or equivalence record in the corpus means this gap is currently unmitigated.
challenge_questions: Is there a biocompatibility equivalence memo or shared-component declaration that documents that PT5 and PT9L use identical patient-contact materials from identical suppliers with identical manufacturing processes? If so, in which controlled document is it maintained and what is its document number?
Were the PT5 biocompatibility tests conducted on the same material grades and formulations as those specified in the PT9L BOM and material specifications?
Has the 510(k) submission package included a biocompatibility bridging rationale, and has FDA accepted it? Has the CE technical file addressed this under MDR Annex I Chapter II?

findings.claim: The PT9L operation guide (F0083) references MDD rather than MDR 2017/745 for biocompatibility compliance, and this document is filed in the active T1 sample folder without a draft or historical designation, making it a live document-control issue rather than a historical artifact.
findings.rationale: REG-074 shows F0083 states: 'They are in compliance with the Medical Device Directive (MDD) requirements.' The file path is '11 T1样机\PT9L-operation guide-20240828.via_lo_html.clean.md' with a date stamp of 20240828 (28 August 2024). MDD 93/42/EEC was repealed and replaced by MDR 2017/745, which became fully applicable on 26 May 2021. A document dated August 2024 referencing MDD rather than MDR is not a historical artifact—it is a current document with an incorrect regulatory reference. The orchestrator's escalation question (ASG-0008 item 4) asks whether this is a live document or a draft/historical artifact. The date stamp and active folder location confirm it is live. This creates a compliance gap for any CE submission and may also mislead users about the applicable regulatory framework.
challenge_questions: Has the operation guide (F0083, dated 20240828) been released to production or included in any regulatory submission? If so, which submissions and what is the remediation plan?
Is there a controlled document review process that checks regulatory references for currency at each document revision? If so, why did the MDD reference survive to a document dated August 2024?
Does the CE technical file for PT9L reference this operation guide, and if so, has the notified body or EU authorized representative been notified of the incorrect regulatory citation?

findings.claim: Both ASTM E1965-98:2016 and ASTM E1965-98:2023 are cited as applicable in the same design input document and the same design verification plan and report, but no transition rationale, version-selection justification, or test-to-standard mapping document was found in the corpus.
findings.rationale: REG-062 and REG-063 show F0031 lists both ASTM E1965-98:2016 and ASTM E1965-98:2023 as applicable US standards. REG-128 and REG-129 show F0121 (design verification plan) lists both as applicable with the same verification method. REG-121 and REG-122 show F0114 (design verification report) lists both as passed. REG-071 shows the label review (F0082) references ASTM E1965-98:2023. The orchestrator's escalation question (ASG-0008 item 6) asks whether the dual citation appears in the same document or across different design stages. Assessment: both versions appear in the same documents at the same design stage, not as a staged transition. No transition rationale, version-comparison analysis, or test-to-standard mapping document appears in the corpus. For a 510(k) submission, FDA will expect the manufacturer to identify which version of ASTM E1965 was used for testing and to justify compliance with that version. Citing both without differentiation creates ambiguity about which standard governs the device's performance claims.
challenge_questions: Were the accuracy and performance tests conducted against ASTM E1965-98:2016, ASTM E1965-98:2023, or both? Which test report documents the results against each version?
What are the substantive differences between ASTM E1965-98:2016 and ASTM E1965-98:2023 that are relevant to PT9L, and has a gap analysis been performed?
Is the 510(k) submission claiming compliance with both versions simultaneously, and if so, has FDA guidance on standard version selection been consulted?

assignment.review_focus: Bluetooth hazard traceability closure check. Three independent agents (Risk Traceability Agent RUN-0003, Software Agent RUN-0004, V&V Agent RUN-0007) have each reported absence of Bluetooth-specific hazard identification, risk control, and verification evidence. This recheck must: (1) search the full corpus for any document referencing Bluetooth, BLE, wireless, or RF in the context of PT9L hazard analysis or risk controls; (2) determine whether the Risk Management Report (PT9L-FXGB01 V2.0) contains a Bluetooth hazard entry and whether any corresponding verification record closes that control; (3) confirm whether the absence is a true gap or whether evidence exists in documents not yet retrieved; (4) assess whether the Bluetooth feature described in the project profile (PT9L transmits temperature to smart device via Bluetooth) is reflected anywhere in the ISO 14971 risk assessment chain. Do not confirm or dismiss the gap — locate and report all available evidence.

mandatory_audit_matrix.check_goal: Verify that risk items, risk controls, and verification activities form a closed traceability chain.

assignment.review_focus: Bluetooth hazard traceability closure check. Three independent agents (Risk Traceability Agent RUN-0003, Software Agent RUN-0004, V&V Agent RUN-0007) have each reported absence of Bluetooth-specific hazard identification, risk control, and verification evidence. This recheck must: (1) search the full corpus for any document referencing Bluetooth, BLE, wireless, or RF in the context of PT9L hazard analysis or risk controls; (2) determine whether the Risk Management Report (PT9L-FXGB01 V2.0) contains a Bluetooth hazard entry and whether any corresponding verification record closes that control; (3) confirm whether the absence is a true gap or whether evidence exists in documents not yet retrieved; (4) assess whether the Bluetooth feature described in the project profile (PT9L transmits temperature to smart device via Bluetooth) is reflected anywhere in the ISO 14971 risk assessment chain. Do not confirm or dismiss the gap — locate and report all available evidence.

agent_runs.summary: Cross-corpus scan of the PT9L DHF/DMR package reveals 14 candidate consistency issues spanning legacy product residue in active documents, document-number mismatches, unsigned approvals, wrong-product references in BOM and label documents, regulatory applicability conflicts, software diagram contamination, and blood-pressure-specific language appearing in a thermometer DHF.

Hardware audit of PT9L DHF/DMR reveals five substantive consistency findings: a blood-pressure residue phrase in the battery design-verification plan/report, an unresolved BOM conflict between PT3-P10 dual-spring and PT5-M02/M03 separate springs, a total-assembly drawing part-number anomaly (T-Z1-P10 used for two distinct PCBs), missing pass/fail verdicts in multiple T1 sample review checklists, and object-temperature mode accuracy tolerance (±0.2 °C) applied at 30 °C and 45 °C in software test plans despite the design-input accuracy specification only requiring ±0.2 °C for ≥35 °C and ≤42 °C.

The PT9L risk management file set contains multiple traceability chain breaks: the current Risk Management Report references document number PT9L-FXGB01 V1.0 while the active risk set has been revised to V2.0; the active Risk Management Plan carries document number IFT-FXJH01 rather than PT9L-FXJH01; F0013 (PT2L risk plan) internally carries a PT9L-series document number creating a product-identity conflict; no evidence of Bluetooth-specific hazard verification is present in the supplied corpus; DFMEA files (F0071, F0074) are not cross-referenced to the ISO 14971 risk assessment; and the design verification plan/report cites only PT9L-FXGB01 V1.0 while the current report is V2.0, leaving the closed-loop confirmation potentially misaligned.

PT9L software lifecycle audit reveals five substantive findings: BP3L software diagrams appear in the primary PT9L software design folder and T1 sample subfolder without documented shared-component rationale; the software design document version identifier (E0 23.11) cannot be reconciled with the V1.0 identifier cited in test/validation records and BOM; no Bluetooth software requirements or corresponding test/validation evidence is present in the supplied corpus; the IEC 60601-1 test report references software design document DN:PT9L-RJFA01 V1.0 which does not appear in the evidence catalog; and a label review document filed under the active T1 sample folder carries PT2L as the primary product model without justification.

DMR/SOP audit of PT9L design output chain reveals seven substantive findings including a document-number collision on drawing PT9L-F01, a part-number mismatch between the two packaging BOM files, PT3-origin shared-component drawings archived in the PT9L DHF without cross-product justification, an incomplete drawing title-block in a packaging label drawing, a missing outer-carton BOM entry in the primary packaging BOM, a process instruction referencing EBOM by document number without pinning a version, and the design output list carrying blank approval-date fields indicating the formal sign-off record is incomplete.

PT9L DHF regulatory audit identifies eight substantive findings spanning unsigned approval fields across all risk management documents, dual ASTM E1965 version citation without documented transition rationale, inconsistent EN ISO 80601-2-56 and MDR 2017/745 applicability between design input stages, absent 510(k) responsibility agreement for 'andon', biocompatibility reports conducted on PT5 samples rather than PT9L, IFT-prefixed document numbers on active PT9L risk management plans, a historical-folder risk plan (F0013) carrying a PT9L-series document number, and the operation guide referencing MDD rather than MDR for biocompatibility compliance.

PT9L V&V corpus audit reveals five substantive findings: object-temperature accuracy tolerance applied outside the design-input specified range without documented justification; no Bluetooth hazard or functional verification evidence present; blood-pressure residue phrase in battery verification record with no confirmed signed pass verdict in supplied evidence; no verification record references the controlling risk document at V2.0; and the IEC 60601-1 test report's cited software design document (PT9L-RJFA01 V1.0) is absent from the evidence catalog and design output index.

Cross-run synthesis audit of the PT9L DHF/DMR package identifies six substantive regulatory and document-control findings, including one systemic finding covering unsigned approvals across all risk management documents, plus resolution assessments on five specific escalation questions raised by the orchestrator.

llm_output.summary: Full-corpus recheck for Bluetooth hazard traceability in the PT9L risk management chain confirms a true gap: no evidence of Bluetooth/BLE/wireless/RF hazard identification, risk control, or verification closure exists in any supplied document, while the project profile explicitly states PT9L transmits temperature via Bluetooth, and the active Risk Management Report (PT9L-FXGB01 V2.0, F0020/F0024) contains no retrievable Bluetooth hazard entry in the supplied evidence.
review_notes: The evidence catalog contains two parallel sets of current-version risk documents: F0018–F0020 (IFT-prefixed, Attachment 7 series) and F0022–F0024 (PT9L-prefixed, Attachment 7 series). Both sets were searched exhaustively for Bluetooth/BLE/wireless/RF content; neither set contains any such reference in the supplied evidence lines.

RISK-040 (F0018) confirms the Risk Assessment Report was updated to V2.0 on 2024-05-30 with question list updated per ISO/TR 24971:2020 Annex A; RISK-045 (F0019) confirms the Verification report was updated to V2.0 on 2024-05-30 with hazard sequence alignment. Neither update note references Bluetooth or wireless hazards.

RISK-123 and RISK-124 (F0083, PT9L operation guide) contain an EMC immunity table referencing IEC basic EMC standards and home healthcare environment levels, which is the closest document to wireless/RF content in the corpus, but this is a user-facing document and not a hazard analysis entry.

RISK-127 (F0114, design verification report) and RISK-130 (F0121, design verification plan) both reference EMC testing as a separate verification item from risk management, but neither links EMC or wireless to a specific hazard ID in the ISO 14971 chain.

RISK-138 through RISK-140 (F0243, IEC 62366-1 checklist) reference ISO 14971:2019 compliance via document PT9L-FXGB01 V1.0, not V2.0, consistent with the version mismatch finding from RUN-0003 and RUN-0007.

DFMEA files F0071 (RISK-103 to RISK-108) and F0074 (RISK-109 to RISK-114) contain detection-ranking criteria tables but no Bluetooth or wireless failure mode entries are present in the supplied evidence lines.

Software hazard table headers are present at RISK-136 (F0135, software design) and RISK-137 (F0139, software requirements), indicating hazard columns exist in those documents, but no row content referencing Bluetooth is present in the supplied evidence.

The historical folder documents (F0012–F0016, F0025–F0028) were also reviewed; none contain Bluetooth hazard entries in the supplied evidence lines, consistent with their pre-Bluetooth-feature vintage.

findings.claim: No Bluetooth-specific hazard, hazardous situation, or harm entry exists anywhere in the PT9L ISO 14971 risk assessment chain (Risk Assessment Report IFT-FXPJ01 V2.0 / PT9L-FXPJ01, Verification Report IFT-FXYS01 V2.0 / PT9L-FXYS01, or Risk Management Report IFT-FXGB01 V2.0 / PT9L-FXGB01 V1.0), despite the project profile confirming PT9L transmits temperature data to a smart device via Bluetooth.
findings.rationale: RISK-037 through RISK-054 cover the IFT-series current risk documents (F0018–F0020) and RISK-061 through RISK-078 cover the PT9L-series current risk documents (F0022–F0024). The table-of-contents entries and all supplied evidence lines from these eight documents contain no reference to Bluetooth, BLE, wireless, or RF in any hazard, control, or residual risk context. RISK-040 confirms the V2.0 Risk Assessment Report was updated per ISO/TR 24971:2020 Annex A on 2024-05-30, meaning the hazard question list was refreshed, yet no Bluetooth entry appears. The project profile states Bluetooth transmission is a confirmed feature. ISO 14971:2019 requires all foreseeable hazards associated with the device to be identified; wireless data transmission introduces hazards including data integrity loss leading to incorrect clinical decision, electromagnetic interference with other devices, and unauthorized data access. None of these appear in the supplied risk chain evidence.

The operation guide (F0083, RISK-123/RISK-124) includes an EMC immunity table. Is EMC immunity testing considered the sole risk control for wireless interference, and if so, where is this control linked to a hazard ID in the ISO 14971 file?

findings.claim: No verification record exists in the supplied corpus that closes a Bluetooth-related risk control measure, meaning the verification-to-residual-risk traceability chain for Bluetooth is entirely absent, not merely incomplete.
findings.rationale: RISK-019 through RISK-024 (F0015, historical verification report) and RISK-043 through RISK-048 (F0019, IFT-series current verification report) and RISK-067 through RISK-072 (F0023, PT9L-series current verification report) all contain table-of-contents entries for risk control measure validation and residual risk assessment sections. None of the supplied evidence lines from these documents reference Bluetooth, BLE, wireless, or RF. RISK-127 (F0114) confirms EMC testing is listed as a separate design verification item with result 'pass' but is not linked to any hazard ID. RISK-128 and RISK-129 confirm the design verification report cites PT9L-FXGB01 V1.0 as the risk management report, but no Bluetooth control is traceable through that citation. The traceability chain from hazard identification through control implementation through verification through residual risk acceptance is therefore completely absent for the Bluetooth feature.

findings.claim: The software design document (F0135) and software requirements specification (F0139) both contain hazard analysis table headers but supply no Bluetooth or wireless hazard row in the supplied evidence, creating a gap between the confirmed Bluetooth feature and the software-level hazard analysis that feeds the ISO 14971 chain.
findings.rationale: RISK-136 (F0135, software design) shows a hazard table header with columns for Hazard, Hazardous Situation, and Mitigation Measure. RISK-137 (F0139, software requirements) shows a hazard table header with columns for Hazard, Hazardous Situation, and Planned Control Measures. Neither document's supplied evidence lines contain any row referencing Bluetooth, BLE, wireless data loss, or RF interference. The project profile confirms Bluetooth is a PT9L feature. Software-level hazard analysis is a required input to the ISO 14971 risk assessment per ISO 14971:2019 clause 5.4 and ISO/TR 24971:2020. The absence of Bluetooth entries in the software hazard tables means the upstream input to the risk assessment is also missing, compounding the gap identified in the risk assessment documents themselves.
challenge_questions: Do the full-text versions of F0135 (software design) and F0139 (software requirements) contain any rows in their hazard tables referencing Bluetooth, BLE, wireless, or data transmission? If so, provide the hazard ID and description.
Was a software hazard analysis conducted specifically for the Bluetooth data transmission function? If so, what document captures it and how does it feed into the ISO 14971 risk assessment report?
Is the Bluetooth module treated as a software-controlled function, a hardware function, or both? How is this reflected in the DFMEA files (F0071, F0074) and the ISO 14971 risk assessment?

findings.claim: The design verification report (F0114) and the IEC 62366-1 checklist (F0243) both cite the Risk Management Report as PT9L-FXGB01 V1.0, while the current active Risk Management Report in the DHF corpus is V2.0 (F0020, F0024), meaning the closed-loop confirmation in the verification chain references a superseded document version.
findings.rationale: RISK-128 and RISK-129 (F0114, design verification report) explicitly cite 'PT9L-FXGB01 V1.0' as the risk management report with a pass verdict. RISK-138 (F0243, IEC 62366-1 checklist) cites 'PT9L-FXGB01 V1.0' as the ISO 14971 compliance document. However, RISK-049 through RISK-054 (F0020) and RISK-073 through RISK-078 (F0024) both show the current Risk Management Report is titled V2.0 (file name) while the internal document number header at RISK-050 and RISK-074 still reads 'PT9L-FXGB01 V1.0'. This creates ambiguity: either the internal document number was not updated when the file was revised to V2.0, or the design verification report and IEC 62366-1 checklist were never updated to reference the current version. Either way, the traceability chain between the verification closure and the current risk management report is broken or ambiguous.
challenge_questions: What is the authoritative current version of the Risk Management Report for PT9L: V1.0 (per internal document number header at RISK-050/RISK-074) or V2.0 (per file name at RISK-049/RISK-073)? Has a formal version increment been approved and recorded in the document change history?

Were the design verification report (F0114) and IEC 62366-1 checklist (F0243) updated to reference the V2.0 Risk Management Report after the 2024-05-30 revision? If not, is there a documented rationale for why V1.0 remains the cited version?

Does the V2.0 Risk Management Report contain any content changes relative to V1.0 that affect the pass/fail determination recorded in the design verification report? If so, the verification closure may need to be re-evaluated.

findings.claim: The DFMEA files (F0071, F0074) use a detection-ranking methodology and contain design control references but are not cross-referenced to the ISO 14971 risk assessment report or risk management report in any supplied evidence, leaving the DFMEA hazard analysis isolated from the formal risk traceability chain.
findings.rationale: RISK-103 through RISK-108 (F0071, packaging DFMEA) and RISK-109 through RISK-114 (F0074, structural DFMEA) contain detection-ranking criteria tables with design control references. Neither document's supplied evidence lines contain any reference to ISO 14971, PT9L-FXPJ01, PT9L-FXGB01, or any hazard ID from the ISO 14971 risk assessment. Conversely, the ISO 14971 risk assessment documents (F0018, F0022) and risk management report (F0020, F0024) contain no supplied evidence lines referencing the DFMEA document numbers F0071 or F0074. ISO 14971:2019 clause 5 requires that all hazard identification inputs be captured in the risk management file; DFMEA is a recognized hazard identification tool per ISO/TR 24971:2020. The absence of cross-referencing means it cannot be confirmed that DFMEA-identified failure modes were evaluated within the ISO 14971 framework.
challenge_questions: Does the Risk Assessment Report (PT9L-FXPJ01 V2.0) reference the DFMEA files (F0071, F0074) as hazard identification inputs? If so, in which section and under which hazard IDs?
Were the failure modes identified in the packaging DFMEA (F0071) and structural DFMEA (F0074) reviewed against the ISO 14971 hazard list? Is there a documented mapping or cross-reference table?
Are there additional DFMEA files (e.g., electrical, software, or system-level DFMEA) that are cross-referenced to the ISO 14971 risk assessment but not present in the supplied corpus?

findings.claim: The active Risk Management Plan filed in the primary DHF folder (F0017, F0021) carries document number IFT-FXJH01 V1.0 rather than PT9L-FXJH01, while the design verification plan (F0121) references risk management activities without specifying a plan document number, leaving the plan-to-assessment traceability link dependent on an IFT-prefixed identifier that does not match the PT9L product document numbering convention.
findings.rationale: RISK-031 and RISK-032 (F0017) show the active Risk Management Plan file is titled 'Attachment 7 01 Risk Management Plan IFT-FXJH01 V1.0' with internal document number 'IFT-FXJH01 V1.0'. RISK-055 and RISK-056 (F0021) show the PT9L-prefixed copy carries internal document number 'PT9L-FXJH01 V1.0' but the file is named with the IFT prefix. RISK-038 (F0018, Risk Assessment Report) carries document number 'IFT-FXPJ01 V2.0' and RISK-043 (F0019, Verification Report) carries 'IFT-FXYS01 V2.0', while RISK-062 (F0022) carries 'PT9L-FXPJ01 V1.0' and RISK-067 (F0023) carries 'PT9L-FXYS01 V1.0'. The parallel existence of IFT-prefixed and PT9L-prefixed versions of the same documents without a documented relationship (e.g., one is a copy, one is the master) means the traceability chain from plan to assessment to verification to report cannot be unambiguously established from the supplied evidence.

findings.rationale: RISK-103 through RISK-108 (F0071, packaging DFMEA) and RISK-109 through RISK-114 (F0074, structural DFMEA) contain detection-ranking criteria tables with design control references. Neither document's supplied evidence lines contain any reference to ISO 14971, PT9L-FXPJ01, PT9L-FXGB01, or any hazard ID from the ISO 14971 risk assessment. Conversely, the ISO 14971 risk assessment documents (F0018, F0022) and risk management report (F0020, F0024) contain no supplied evidence lines referencing the DFMEA document numbers F0071 or F0074. ISO 14971:2019 clause 5 requires that all hazard identification inputs be captured in the risk management file; DFMEA is a recognized hazard identification tool per ISO/TR 24971:2020. The absence of cross-referencing means it cannot be confirmed that DFMEA-identified failure modes were evaluated within the ISO 14971 framework.
challenge_questions: Does the Risk Assessment Report (PT9L-FXPJ01 V2.0) reference the DFMEA files (F0071, F0074) as hazard identification inputs? If so, in which section and under which hazard IDs?
Were the failure modes identified in the packaging DFMEA (F0071) and structural DFMEA (F0074) reviewed against the ISO 14971 hazard list? Is there a documented mapping or cross-reference table?
Are there additional DFMEA files (e.g., electrical, software, or system-level DFMEA) that are cross-referenced to the ISO 14971 risk assessment but not present in the supplied corpus?

findings.claim: The active Risk Management Plan filed in the primary DHF folder (F0017, F0021) carries document number IFT-FXJH01 V1.0 rather than PT9L-FXJH01, while the design verification plan (F0121) references risk management activities without specifying a plan document number, leaving the plan-to-assessment traceability link dependent on an IFT-prefixed identifier that does not match the PT9L product document numbering convention.
findings.rationale: RISK-031 and RISK-032 (F0017) show the active Risk Management Plan file is titled 'Attachment 7 01 Risk Management Plan IFT-FXJH01 V1.0' with internal document number 'IFT-FXJH01 V1.0'. RISK-055 and RISK-056 (F0021) show the PT9L-prefixed copy carries internal document number 'PT9L-FXJH01 V1.0' but the file is named with the IFT prefix. RISK-038 (F0018, Risk Assessment Report) carries document number 'IFT-FXPJ01 V2.0' and RISK-043 (F0019, Verification Report) carries 'IFT-FXYS01 V2.0', while RISK-062 (F0022) carries 'PT9L-FXPJ01 V1.0' and RISK-067 (F0023) carries 'PT9L-FXYS01 V1.0'. The parallel existence of IFT-prefixed and PT9L-prefixed versions of the same documents without a documented relationship (e.g., one is a copy, one is the master) means the traceability chain from plan to assessment to verification to report cannot be unambiguously established from the supplied evidence.
challenge_questions: Which document number series is the authoritative master for the PT9L risk management file: IFT-FXJH01/IFT-FXPJ01/IFT-FXYS01/IFT-FXGB01 or PT9L-FXJH01/PT9L-FXPJ01/PT9L-FXYS01/PT9L-FXGB01? Is there a document control record that establishes this?

Are the IFT-prefixed and PT9L-prefixed documents identical in content, or do they differ? If they differ, which version was used as the basis for the design verification report (F0114) and IEC 62366-1 checklist (F0243)?
Does the Risk Management Plan (whichever version is authoritative) explicitly list Bluetooth/wireless as a technology requiring hazard analysis? If so, under which section?

assignment.review_focus: Risk document version alignment in verification records. Risk Traceability Agent (RUN-0003) and V&V Agent (RUN-0007) both flagged that the design verification plan/report cites PT9L-FXGB01 V1.0 while the active risk management report is V2.0. This recheck must: (1) retrieve the design verification plan/report and identify every location where PT9L-FXGB01 is cited, recording the version number cited at each location; (2) retrieve PT9L-FXGB01 V2.0 and identify what changed between V1.0 and V2.0 — specifically whether any risk controls added or modified in V2.0 have corresponding verification activities in the verification plan/report; (3) determine whether any change record, amendment, or addendum to the verification plan/report acknowledges the V2.0 update; (4) assess whether the closed-loop confirmation between risk controls and verification activities is broken by this version mismatch. Do not render a finding verdict — locate and report all available evidence.

input_package.system_prompt: Review verification and validation consistency using only supplied evidence IDs.

assignment.review_focus: Risk document version alignment in verification records. Risk Traceability Agent (RUN-0003) and V&V Agent (RUN-0007) both flagged that the design verification plan/report cites PT9L-FXGB01 V1.0 while the active risk management report is V2.0. This recheck must: (1) retrieve the design verification plan/report and identify every location where PT9L-FXGB01 is cited, recording the version number cited at each location; (2) retrieve PT9L-FXGB01 V2.0 and identify what changed between V1.0 and V2.0 — specifically whether any risk controls added or modified in V2.0 have corresponding verification activities in the verification plan/report; (3) determine whether any change record, amendment, or addendum to the verification plan/report acknowledges the V2.0 update; (4) assess whether the closed-loop confirmation between risk controls and verification activities is broken by this version mismatch. Do not render a finding verdict — locate and report all available evidence.

agent_runs.summary: Cross-corpus scan of the PT9L DHF/DMR package reveals 14 candidate consistency issues spanning legacy product residue in active documents, document-number mismatches, unsigned approvals, wrong-product references in BOM and label documents, regulatory applicability conflicts, software diagram contamination, and blood-pressure-specific language appearing in a thermometer DHF.

Hardware audit of PT9L DHF/DMR reveals five substantive consistency findings: a blood-pressure residue phrase in the battery design-verification plan/report, an unresolved BOM conflict between PT3-P10 dual-spring and PT5-M02/M03 separate springs, a total-assembly drawing part-number anomaly (T-Z1-P10 used for two distinct PCBs), missing pass/fail verdicts in multiple T1 sample review checklists, and object-temperature mode accuracy tolerance (±0.2 °C) applied at 30 °C and 45 °C in software test plans despite the design-input accuracy specification only requiring ±0.2 °C for ≥35 °C and ≤42 °C.

The PT9L risk management file set contains multiple traceability chain breaks: the current Risk Management Report references document number PT9L-FXGB01 V1.0 while the active risk set has been revised to V2.0; the active Risk Management Plan carries document number IFT-FXJH01 rather than PT9L-FXJH01; F0013 (PT2L risk plan) internally carries a PT9L-series document number creating a product-identity conflict; no evidence of Bluetooth-specific hazard verification is present in the supplied corpus; DFMEA files (F0071, F0074) are not cross-referenced to the ISO 14971 risk assessment; and the design verification plan/report cites only PT9L-FXGB01 V1.0 while the current report is V2.0, leaving the closed-loop confirmation potentially misaligned.

PT9L software lifecycle audit reveals five substantive findings: BP3L software diagrams appear in the primary PT9L software design folder and T1 sample subfolder without documented shared-component rationale; the software design document version identifier (E0 23.11) cannot be reconciled with the V1.0 identifier cited in test/validation records and BOM; no Bluetooth software requirements or corresponding test/validation evidence is present in the supplied corpus; the IEC 60601-1 test report references software design document DN:PT9L-RJFA01 V1.0 which does not appear in the evidence catalog; and a label review document filed under the active T1 sample folder carries PT2L as the primary product model without justification.

DMR/SOP audit of PT9L design output chain reveals seven substantive findings including a document-number collision on drawing PT9L-F01, a part-number mismatch between the two packaging BOM files, PT3-origin shared-component drawings archived in the PT9L DHF without cross-product justification, an incomplete drawing title-block in a packaging label drawing, a missing outer-carton BOM entry in the primary packaging BOM, a process instruction referencing EBOM by document number without pinning a version, and the design output list carrying blank approval-date fields indicating the formal sign-off record is incomplete.

PT9L DHF regulatory audit identifies eight substantive findings spanning unsigned approval fields across all risk management documents, dual ASTM E1965 version citation without documented transition rationale, inconsistent EN ISO 80601-2-56 and MDR 2017/745 applicability between design input stages, absent 510(k) responsibility agreement for 'andon', biocompatibility reports conducted on PT5 samples rather than PT9L, IFT-prefixed document numbers on active PT9L risk management plans, a historical-folder risk plan (F0013) carrying a PT9L-series document number, and the operation guide referencing MDD rather than MDR for biocompatibility compliance.

PT9L V&V corpus audit reveals five substantive findings: object-temperature accuracy tolerance applied outside the design-input specified range without documented justification; no Bluetooth hazard or functional verification evidence present; blood-pressure residue phrase in battery verification record with no confirmed signed pass verdict in supplied evidence; no verification record references the controlling risk document at V2.0; and the IEC 60601-1 test report's cited software design document (PT9L-RJFA01 V1.0) is absent from the evidence catalog and design output index.

Cross-run synthesis audit of the PT9L DHF/DMR package identifies six substantive regulatory and document-control findings, including one systemic finding covering unsigned approvals across all risk management documents, plus resolution assessments on five specific escalation questions raised by the orchestrator.

Full-corpus recheck for Bluetooth hazard traceability in the PT9L risk management chain confirms a true gap: no evidence of Bluetooth/BLE/wireless/RF hazard identification, risk control, or verification closure exists in any supplied document, while the project profile explicitly states PT9L transmits temperature via Bluetooth, and the active Risk Management Report (PT9L-FXGB01 V2.0, F0020/F0024) contains no retrievable Bluetooth hazard entry in the supplied evidence.

llm_output.summary: Context recheck for ASG-0010 confirms that the design verification report (F0114) cites external test reports ETX202303-07-078-03 and ETX202303-07-078-04 as passing evidence for ISO 80601-2-56 and ASTM E1965 compliance, but no version of the verification plan/report in the supplied evidence catalog explicitly cites PT9L-FXGB01 by version number, no change record or addendum acknowledging the V1.0-to-V2.0 risk report update is present, a revised ISO 80601-2-56 test report (ETX202303-07-078-03R1, dated 2025-05-29) exists in the corpus without any corresponding update to the design verification report, and the closed-loop confirmation between risk controls and verification activities cannot be confirmed as complete from the supplied evidence.
review_notes: The design verification report (F0114) is a multi-row matrix document covering regulatory standards; the supplied evidence lines (VV-010 through VV-015) represent only the rows for ISO 80601-2-56:2017/Amd1:2018, EN ISO 80601-2-56:2017+A1:2018, EN 12470-3, EN 12470-5, ASTM E1965-98:2016, and ASTM E1965-98:2023. The supplied evidence lines for both (VV-001 through VV-004) contain only high-level statements about the risk management plan and acceptance criteria; no line-level content showing what changed between V1.0 and V2.0 is present in the evidence catalog.

Five final external test reports are present in the corpus: ETX202303-07-078-01 (EMC, F0456), ETX202303-07-078-02 (safety/IEC 60601-1, F0457), ETX202303-07-078-03 (ISO 80601-2-56, F0458), ETX202303-07-078-04 (ASTM E1965, F0459), ETX202303-07-078-05 (aging/老化, F0460). All are dated 2025-02-12 except the EMC report (2024-08-15).

A revised ISO 80601-2-56 report ETX202303-07-078-03R1 (F0461, dated 2025-05-29) is present in the corpus. This is a later revision of the same test scope as ETX202303-07-078-03. The design verification report (F0114) cites only ETX202303-07-078-03 and ETX202303-07-078-04 for ISO 80601-2-56 compliance; it does not reference the R1 revision.

Draft versions of reports ETX202303-07-078-01 (F0465), ETX202303-07-078-02 (F0466), ETX202303-07-078-03 (F0467), and ETX202303-07-078-04 (F0468) are present in the '草稿' (draft) subfolder. The draft for ETX202303-07-078-02 (F0466) carries a truncated report number 'ETX2023-07-078-02' (missing '03' segment) in its header lines, which differs from the final report number 'ETX202303-07-078-02'.

The usability engineering file (F0247/F0248) describes acceptance criteria for usability evaluation and references two formative evaluations and a summative/pre-summative evaluation, but no summative usability test report or completed formative evaluation report is present in the supplied evidence catalog.

The design input summary table (F0031/F0319) is present in the evidence catalog only as a title line ('Design Input - General part') with no retrievable content rows, so traceability from specific design inputs to verification activities cannot be confirmed from supplied evidence.
The DFMEA files (F0071, F0074) reference pass/fail acceptance criteria in their detection rating scales but are not cross-referenced to any specific verification test record in the supplied evidence.

No document identified as the verification plan (PT9L-KXPS01) appears in the evidence catalog by that document number; F0114 is the only verification-related document with retrievable content rows, and it is labeled as a design verification report rather than a plan.

The analysis and evaluation report (F0462) references 'Annex I: ETX202303-07-078-05 Test Report' as an annex, and two copies of that annex exist in the corpus (F0455 in '实验报告' root and F0463 in '实验报告\最终报告'). Both carry the same report number ETX202303-07-078-05. The final aging report (F0460) also carries ETX202303-07-078-05. The relationship between the annex copies and the standalone final report is not clarified in the supplied evidence.

findings.claim: Two copies of a document titled 'Annex I--ETX202303-07-078-05 Test Report (PT9L)' exist in the corpus (F0455 in the root '实验报告' folder and F0463 in '实验报告\最终报告'), both carrying report number ETX202303-07-078-05, alongside a standalone final aging report (F0460) also carrying ETX202303-07-078-05; the relationship among these three instances is not clarified in the supplied evidence, creating potential ambiguity about which is the controlling test record.
findings.rationale: VV-029 through VV-034 (F0455) and VV-072 through VV-077 (F0463) both show documents titled 'Annex I--ETX202303-07-078-05 Test Report (PT9L)' with identical report numbers. VV-059 through VV-064 (F0460) show a standalone document titled '2025.02.12 ETX202303-07-078-05 PT9L 老化报告-正式' also carrying ETX202303-07-078-05. VV-071 (F0462) references 'Annex I: ETX202303-07-078-05 Test Report' as an annex to an analysis and evaluation report. Three separate file instances share the same report number. No document in the evidence catalog explains whether F0455 and F0463 are identical copies, whether one supersedes the other, or how the annex copies relate to the standalone final report F0460.
challenge_questions: Are F0455 and F0463 identical documents or do they differ in content? If they differ, which is the controlling version and why are both retained in the DHF?
Is F0460 (standalone aging report) the same document as the annex copies in F0455/F0463, or is it a separate report that happens to share the same report number?
Which instance of ETX202303-07-078-05 is referenced by the design verification report (F0114) and the analysis/evaluation report (F0462) as the controlling test record?
Does the document control system for the DHF have a mechanism to prevent duplicate filing of the same report number under different file paths?

assignment.review_focus: Biocompatibility sample identity cross-check against BOM and design output records. This recheck must: (1) retrieve the biocompatibility report(s) and identify the sample description, part numbers, and product model cited in the test sample section; (2) cross-reference those sample part numbers against the PT9L EBOM (PT9L-EBOM01) and any PT9L hardware design output drawings to determine whether the tested samples are materially equivalent to PT9L production parts; (3) identify whether any material equivalence justification or sample bridging rationale document exists in the corpus; (4) check whether the PT5 designation corresponds to a predecessor model or a sub-assembly designation within the PT9L product family. Do not confirm or dismiss the finding — locate and report all available evidence.
