primary_scope_rules: PT9L is the target product model for this DHF
Documents in '2L风险改 - 历史文件' folder are explicitly historical
Documents referencing PT2L, PT3SBT, BP3L, or PT9C outside clearly marked historical/draft folders require justification

key_entities.product_description: 红外非接触式额头温度计 (Infrared No-Touch Forehead Thermometer)
key_entities.intended_use: Intermittent measurement of body temperature from forehead skin surface on people of all ages; consumer home use and healthcare provider use
key_entities.bluetooth: PT9L can transmit temperature to smart device with Bluetooth (per Risk Management Report)

regulatory_baseline: EN ISO 80601-2-56:2017+A1:2018 (EU, applicability differs between draft and final design input)
MDR 2017/745 (EU, applicability differs between draft and final design input)
ISO 14971:2019 / EN ISO 14971:2019 / EN ISO 14971:2019/A11:2021 (risk management)
CE registration: applicability not yet determined per final design input
candidate_discovery_hints: PT9C appears as a sub-component PCB document number and as a standalone product in clinical evaluation and user test documents
PT3SBT appears in design output list two and a label review document filed under T1 sample folder
BP3L software diagrams appear in both the main software design folder and T1 sample subfolder
PT2L risk documents are in a '历史文件' subfolder but one (F0013) carries a PT9L document number internally

mandatory_audit_matrix.check_goal: Verify that key PT9L design-input parameters are carried into design outputs and validation conditions consistently.

assignment.review_focus: Biocompatibility sample identity cross-check against BOM and design output records. Regulatory Agent (RUN-0006) flagged that biocompatibility reports were conducted on PT5 samples rather than PT9L samples. This recheck must: (1) retrieve the biocompatibility report(s) and identify the sample description, part numbers, and product model cited in the test sample section; (2) cross-reference those sample part numbers against the PT9L EBOM (PT9L-EBOM01) and any PT9L hardware design output drawings to determine whether the tested samples are materially equivalent to PT9L production parts; (3) identify whether any material equivalence justification or sample bridging rationale document exists in the corpus; (4) check whether the PT5 designation corresponds to a predecessor model or a sub-assembly designation within the PT9L product family. Do not confirm or dismiss the finding — locate and report all available evidence.

agent_runs.summary: Cross-corpus scan of the PT9L DHF/DMR package reveals 14 candidate consistency issues spanning legacy product residue in active documents, document-number mismatches, unsigned approvals, wrong-product references in BOM and label documents, regulatory applicability conflicts, software diagram contamination, and blood-pressure-specific language appearing in a thermometer DHF.

Hardware audit of PT9L DHF/DMR reveals five substantive consistency findings: a blood-pressure residue phrase in the battery design-verification plan/report, an unresolved BOM conflict between PT3-P10 dual-spring and PT5-M02/M03 separate springs, a total-assembly drawing part-number anomaly (T-Z1-P10 used for two distinct PCBs), missing pass/fail verdicts in multiple T1 sample review checklists, and object-temperature mode accuracy tolerance (±0.2 °C) applied at 30 °C and 45 °C in software test plans despite the design-input accuracy specification only requiring ±0.2 °C for ≥35 °C and ≤42 °C.

The PT9L risk management file set contains multiple traceability chain breaks: the current Risk Management Report references document number PT9L-FXGB01 V1.0 while the active risk set has been revised to V2.0; the active Risk Management Plan carries document number IFT-FXJH01 rather than PT9L-FXJH01; F0013 (PT2L risk plan) internally carries a PT9L-series document number creating a product-identity conflict; no evidence of Bluetooth-specific hazard verification is present in the supplied corpus; DFMEA files (F0071, F0074) are not cross-referenced to the ISO 14971 risk assessment; and the design verification plan/report cites only PT9L-FXGB01 V1.0 while the current report is V2.0, leaving the closed-loop confirmation potentially misaligned.

PT9L software lifecycle audit reveals five substantive findings: BP3L software diagrams appear in the primary PT9L software design folder and T1 sample subfolder without documented shared-component rationale; the software design document version identifier (E0 23.11) cannot be reconciled with the V1.0 identifier cited in test/validation records and BOM; no Bluetooth software requirements or corresponding test/validation evidence is present in the supplied corpus; the IEC 60601-1 test report references software design document DN:PT9L-RJFA01 V1.0 which does not appear in the evidence catalog; and a label review document filed under the active T1 sample folder carries PT2L as the primary product model without justification.

DMR/SOP audit of PT9L design output chain reveals seven substantive findings including a document-number collision on drawing PT9L-F01, a part-number mismatch between the two packaging BOM files, PT3-origin shared-component drawings archived in the PT9L DHF without cross-product justification, an incomplete drawing title-block in a packaging label drawing, a missing outer-carton BOM entry in the primary packaging BOM, a process instruction referencing EBOM by document number without pinning a version, and the design output list carrying blank approval-date fields indicating the formal sign-off record is incomplete.

PT9L DHF regulatory audit identifies eight substantive findings spanning unsigned approval fields across all risk management documents, dual ASTM E1965 version citation without documented transition rationale, inconsistent EN ISO 80601-2-56 and MDR 2017/745 applicability between design input stages, absent 510(k) responsibility agreement for 'andon', biocompatibility reports conducted on PT5 samples rather than PT9L, IFT-prefixed document numbers on active PT9L risk management plans, a historical-folder risk plan (F0013) carrying a PT9L-series document number, and the operation guide referencing MDD rather than MDR for biocompatibility compliance.

PT9L V&V corpus audit reveals five substantive findings: object-temperature accuracy tolerance applied outside the design-input specified range without documented justification; no Bluetooth hazard or functional verification evidence present; blood-pressure residue phrase in battery verification record with no confirmed signed pass verdict in supplied evidence; no verification record references the controlling risk document at V2.0; and the IEC 60601-1 test report's cited software design document (PT9L-RJFA01 V1.0) is absent from the evidence catalog and design output index.

Cross-run synthesis audit of the PT9L DHF/DMR package identifies six substantive regulatory and document-control findings, including one systemic finding covering unsigned approvals across all risk management documents, plus resolution assessments on five specific escalation questions raised by the orchestrator.

Full-corpus recheck for Bluetooth hazard traceability in the PT9L risk management chain confirms a true gap: no evidence of Bluetooth/BLE/wireless/RF hazard identification, risk control, or verification closure exists in any supplied document, while the project profile explicitly states PT9L transmits temperature via Bluetooth, and the active Risk Management Report (PT9L-FXGB01 V2.0, F0020/F0024) contains no retrievable Bluetooth hazard entry in the supplied evidence.

Context recheck for ASG-0010 confirms that the design verification report (F0114) cites external test reports ETX202303-07-078-03 and ETX202303-07-078-04 as passing evidence for ISO 80601-2-56 and ASTM E1965 compliance, but no version of the verification plan/report in the supplied evidence catalog explicitly cites PT9L-FXGB01 by version number, no change record or addendum acknowledging the V1.0-to-V2.0 risk report update is present, a revised ISO 80601-2-56 test report (ETX202303-07-078-03R1, dated 2025-05-29) exists in the corpus without any corresponding update to the design verification report, and the closed-loop confirmation between risk controls and verification activities cannot be confirmed as complete from the supplied evidence.

llm_output.summary: Hardware audit context-recheck (ASG-0011) finds no biocompatibility report or PT5 sample-identity evidence in the supplied evidence catalog, confirms the PT3-P10 / PT5-M02+M03 spring BOM conflict and T-Z1-P10 dual-PCB part-number anomaly from RUN-0002 remain unresolved, and identifies a blood-pressure residue phrase in the battery design-verification plan that persists across two separate documents.
review_notes: The evidence catalog supplied for this run contains no biocompatibility test report document, no PT5 sample description, and no material equivalence bridging rationale document. The Regulatory Agent (RUN-0006) finding that biocompatibility was conducted on PT5 samples cannot be confirmed or dismissed from hardware evidence alone; a dedicated biocompatibility report document is required.

PT5-M02 (positive spring) drawing is present as HW-135/HW-136/HW-137/HW-138 (F0190) and confirms PT5 is a sub-assembly spring part number within the PT9L product family, not a predecessor product model. This is relevant context for the biocompatibility sample identity question but does not resolve whether the tested samples are materially equivalent to PT9L production parts.

PCB part number PT9L-HFMP01 V1.0 is consistently referenced across EBOM (HW-040, HW-042, HW-077), SMT instructions (HW-062), and design output list (HW-079 through HW-084), indicating good internal consistency for the main PCB.

PCB part number PT9C-CNTP01 V1.0 appears in both the T1 EBOM (HW-041, HW-043) and the design-output EBOM (HW-078), indicating the sensor PCB carries a PT9C-prefixed document number in the active PT9L BOM without documented cross-product justification in the supplied evidence.

Measurement accuracy specification ±0.2 °C for ≥35 °C and ≤42 °C, and ±0.3 °C outside that range, is consistently stated across design input (HW-003), product inspection standard (HW-035), detection report (HW-037), design verification plan (HW-056), design verification report (HW-051), product overview (HW-063), and defect definition (HW-064). No accuracy inconsistency exists for body-temperature mode.
Measurement range 32 °C–42.9 °C stated in the label review (HW-024, HW-025) and operation guide (HW-034) is consistent across those documents.

Low-battery detection function BATDECT is referenced in software test plan (HW-059) and low-battery symbol is referenced in operation guide (HW-033); software requirement for low-battery state is noted (HW-060). No hardware-level low-voltage threshold value is specified in the supplied evidence catalog, so a quantitative low-voltage threshold consistency check cannot be performed.
PCB design review checklist items (HW-004 through HW-009) all show pass verdicts, indicating the E0 hardware design review was completed.

T1 sample review checklists (HW-014 through HW-022) show blank pass/fail fields for PCB-related assembly checks, consistent with the RUN-0002 finding of missing verdicts; this is not re-raised as a new finding but is noted as an unresolved prior finding.

findings.claim: No biocompatibility test report or PT5 sample-identity document is present in the supplied evidence catalog, making it impossible to confirm or dismiss whether the tested samples are materially equivalent to PT9L production parts as flagged by RUN-0006.
findings.rationale: The assignment (ASG-0011) requires retrieval of biocompatibility report(s) identifying sample part numbers and cross-referencing them against PT9L-EBOM01. The entire evidence catalog (HW-001 through HW-140) contains no biocompatibility test report document. PT5-M02 is confirmed as a PT9L sub-assembly spring part (HW-135, HW-136, HW-137, HW-138, F0190), establishing that 'PT5' is a sub-assembly designation within the PT9L family rather than a predecessor product model, but this does not resolve whether biocompatibility samples were drawn from PT9L production-equivalent parts. No material equivalence justification or sample bridging rationale document is present in the supplied evidence. The gap cannot be closed without the biocompatibility report document.
challenge_questions: Can the biocompatibility test report(s) for PT9L be provided, specifically the section describing test sample identity, part numbers, and product model?
Is there a material equivalence or sample bridging rationale document that justifies using PT5-designated samples to cover PT9L production parts?
Which specific PT5 part numbers were submitted for biocompatibility testing, and do those part numbers appear in PT9L-EBOM01 V1.0?
If PT5 refers to a sub-assembly spring (PT5-M02/PT5-M03), were the biocompatibility samples limited to those spring parts, or did they cover all patient-contact materials in the PT9L assembly?

findings.claim: The sensor PCB listed in the active PT9L design-output EBOM (PT9L-EBOM01 V1.0) carries document number PT9C-CNTP01 V1.0, a PT9C-prefixed identifier, with no cross-product justification or shared-component rationale present in the supplied evidence.
findings.rationale: HW-078 (F0157, design-output EBOM) and HW-041/HW-043 (F0096/F0097, T1 EBOM) all list the sensor PCB as PT9C-CNTP01 V1.0 with part number K0118000084609A1106. The project profile states that PT9C appears as a sub-component PCB document number but also as a standalone product, and that documents referencing PT9C outside clearly marked historical/draft folders require justification. No justification document is present in the supplied evidence catalog. The main PCB PT9L-HFMP01 V1.0 carries a PT9L-prefixed number (HW-077, HW-040, HW-042) and is consistently documented, but the sensor PCB cross-product designation is undocumented.
challenge_questions: Is PT9C-CNTP01 V1.0 a shared component used in both PT9C and PT9L products, and if so, where is the shared-component or cross-product use justification document?
Does the PT9C-CNTP01 V1.0 sensor PCB drawing specify the same electrical and mechanical interface as required by the PT9L hardware design?
Has a design verification activity been performed specifically on PT9C-CNTP01 V1.0 in the context of PT9L assembly, or is verification coverage assumed from PT9C qualification?

findings.claim: The design verification plan (F0121) and one section of the design verification report (F0114) contain the phrase '次血压测量' (blood pressure measurements) in the battery item, which is a blood-pressure-specific residue phrase that is inconsistent with PT9L being an infrared thermometer.
findings.rationale: HW-058 (F0121, design verification plan, battery item 20) states '在充满电后，电池电量至少能进行 次血压测量' and HW-055 (F0114, design verification report, battery item 20 in the second section) repeats the same phrase. By contrast, HW-053 (F0114, battery item 20 in the first section) and HW-002 (F0031, design input) use the generic phrase '次测量' without 'blood pressure'. The residue phrase in the verification plan and one report section indicates a copy-paste error from a blood-pressure product template that was not fully corrected, creating a document-control inconsistency in the active DHF. This was identified in RUN-0002 and remains unresolved.
challenge_questions: Has a document correction or errata been issued for F0121 and the affected section of F0114 to remove the blood-pressure residue phrase?
Was the battery life test actually conducted against a thermometer-specific measurement count criterion, and if so, what was the criterion and where is it documented?
Does the battery life test report referenced in HW-053 specify the number of thermometer measurements performed per charge cycle?

findings.claim: The PT9L total-assembly drawing (F0178) lists PT3-P10 dual-spring as item 20, while the drawing's own annotation states PT9L actual assembly uses separate PT5-M02 and PT5-M03 springs, and the ABOM (F0094) also lists PT3-P10; no authoritative resolution document is present in the supplied evidence.
findings.rationale: HW-092 (F0178) shows PT3-P10 dual-spring as BOM item 20 in the total-assembly drawing. HW-089 and HW-090 (F0176, PT3-P10 drawing) state that PT9L actual assembly uses PT5-M02 + PT5-M03 and that PT3-P10 'does not necessarily enter PT9L mass-production BOM'. HW-039 (F0094, ABOM) lists PT3-P10. HW-135 through HW-138 (F0190) confirm PT5-M02 positive spring exists as a separate drawing. The conflict between the assembly drawing BOM, the ABOM, and the annotation on the PT3-P10 drawing has not been resolved by any authoritative ECO or BOM revision in the supplied evidence. This was identified in RUN-0002 and remains unresolved.
challenge_questions: Has an engineering change order (ECO) been issued to update the total-assembly drawing and ABOM to replace PT3-P10 with PT5-M02 and PT5-M03?
Which spring configuration—PT3-P10 or PT5-M02+M03—is used in the T1 sample units that underwent design verification testing?
If PT5-M02 and PT5-M03 are the production-intent parts, are their drawings and part numbers included in the current PT9L-EBOM01 and ABOM?

findings.claim: In the PT9L total-assembly drawing (F0178), part number T-Z1-P10 is assigned to the sensor PCB (item 11), while a separate unnamed PCB appears as item 08, and the drawing annotation flags that T-Z1-P10 simultaneously designates both a bare board and a PCB, creating an ambiguous part-number assignment that is not resolved in the supplied evidence.
findings.rationale: HW-091 (F0178) flags 'BOM中T-Z1-P10同时指导光板和PCB（一图号两零件）'. HW-093 shows item 11 as T-Z1-P10 labeled PCB. HW-094 shows item 08 as an unnamed PCB. HW-095 and HW-096 describe the PCB group and sensor group separately. The active EBOM (HW-077, HW-078) uses PT9L-HFMP01 V1.0 and PT9C-CNTP01 V1.0 as the two PCB part numbers, which do not match T-Z1-P10, indicating the assembly drawing uses a different numbering scheme from the EBOM without a cross-reference table. This was identified in RUN-0002 and remains unresolved.
challenge_questions: What is the correct part number for the sensor PCB in the PT9L assembly—T-Z1-P10 or PT9C-CNTP01 V1.0—and is there a cross-reference table reconciling the assembly drawing numbering scheme with the EBOM?
Does T-Z1-P10 refer to a bare PCB substrate (光板) or a populated PCBA, and is this distinction captured in the drawing title block?
Has the total-assembly drawing been updated to use the same part numbers as PT9L-EBOM01 V1.0, or is a separate drawing-to-BOM mapping document maintained?

findings.claim: Software test plans and test records apply ±0.2 °C accuracy tolerance to object-temperature mode measurements at 30 °C and 45 °C, which are outside the design-input accuracy specification range of ≥35 °C and ≤42 °C where ±0.2 °C applies; no documented justification for this tighter-than-required tolerance outside the specified range exists in the supplied evidence.
findings.rationale: HW-003 (F0031, design input) and HW-035 (F0090, inspection standard) specify ±0.2 °C for ≥35 °C and ≤42 °C, and ±0.3 °C for all other temperatures. HW-045 and HW-046 (F0101, software test plan) specify ±0.2 °C at 30 °C and 45 °C for object-temperature mode. HW-048 and HW-049 (F0102, software test record) repeat the same criteria. At 30 °C and 45 °C the design input permits ±0.3 °C, so applying ±0.2 °C is a tighter criterion; however, if the device fails at ±0.2 °C but passes at ±0.3 °C, the test record would show a failure that is not actually a non-conformance against the design input. Conversely, if the tighter criterion is intentional product policy, it should be documented. This was identified in RUN-0002 and remains unresolved.
challenge_questions: Is the ±0.2 °C criterion at 30 °C and 45 °C in the object-temperature software test plan an intentional product design decision, and if so, where is this documented as a design requirement?
If the ±0.2 °C criterion at 30 °C and 45 °C is a test-plan error, has a corrected test plan and re-test record been issued?

Do the actual test results at 30 °C and 45 °C in the software test records show pass or fail against the ±0.2 °C criterion, and would those results change if evaluated against the design-input ±0.3 °C criterion?

findings.claim: No biocompatibility test report or PT5 sample-identity document is present in the supplied evidence catalog, making it impossible to confirm or dismiss whether the tested samples are materially equivalent to PT9L production parts as flagged by RUN-0006.
findings.rationale: The assignment (ASG-0011) requires retrieval of biocompatibility report(s) identifying sample part numbers and cross-referencing them against PT9L-EBOM01. The entire evidence catalog (HW-001 through HW-140) contains no biocompatibility test report document. PT5-M02 is confirmed as a PT9L sub-assembly spring part (HW-135, HW-136, HW-137, HW-138, F0190), establishing that 'PT5' is a sub-assembly designation within the PT9L family rather than a predecessor product model, but this does not resolve whether biocompatibility samples were drawn from PT9L production-equivalent parts. No material equivalence justification or sample bridging rationale document is present in the supplied evidence. The gap cannot be closed without the biocompatibility report document.
challenge_questions: Can the biocompatibility test report(s) for PT9L be provided, specifically the section describing test sample identity, part numbers, and product model?
Is there a material equivalence or sample bridging rationale document that justifies using PT5-designated samples to cover PT9L production parts?
Which specific PT5 part numbers were submitted for biocompatibility testing, and do those part numbers appear in PT9L-EBOM01 V1.0?
If PT5 refers to a sub-assembly spring (PT5-M02/PT5-M03), were the biocompatibility samples limited to those spring parts, or did they cover all patient-contact materials in the PT9L assembly?

findings.claim: The sensor PCB listed in the active PT9L design-output EBOM (PT9L-EBOM01 V1.0) carries document number PT9C-CNTP01 V1.0, a PT9C-prefixed identifier, with no cross-product justification or shared-component rationale present in the supplied evidence.
findings.rationale: HW-078 (F0157, design-output EBOM) and HW-041/HW-043 (F0096/F0097, T1 EBOM) all list the sensor PCB as PT9C-CNTP01 V1.0 with part number K0118000084609A1106. The project profile states that PT9C appears as a sub-component PCB document number but also as a standalone product, and that documents referencing PT9C outside clearly marked historical/draft folders require justification. No justification document is present in the supplied evidence catalog. The main PCB PT9L-HFMP01 V1.0 carries a PT9L-prefixed number (HW-077, HW-040, HW-042) and is consistently documented, but the sensor PCB cross-product designation is undocumented.
challenge_questions: Is PT9C-CNTP01 V1.0 a shared component used in both PT9C and PT9L products, and if so, where is the shared-component or cross-product use justification document?
Does the PT9C-CNTP01 V1.0 sensor PCB drawing specify the same electrical and mechanical interface as required by the PT9L hardware design?
Has a design verification activity been performed specifically on PT9C-CNTP01 V1.0 in the context of PT9L assembly, or is verification coverage assumed from PT9C qualification?

findings.claim: The design verification plan (F0121) and one section of the design verification report (F0114) contain the phrase '次血压测量' (blood pressure measurements) in the battery item, which is a blood-pressure-specific residue phrase that is inconsistent with PT9L being an infrared thermometer.
findings.rationale: HW-058 (F0121, design verification plan, battery item 20) states '在充满电后，电池电量至少能进行 次血压测量' and HW-055 (F0114, design verification report, battery item 20 in the second section) repeats the same phrase. By contrast, HW-053 (F0114, battery item 20 in the first section) and HW-002 (F0031, design input) use the generic phrase '次测量' without 'blood pressure'. The residue phrase in the verification plan and one report section indicates a copy-paste error from a blood-pressure product template that was not fully corrected, creating a document-control inconsistency in the active DHF. This was identified in RUN-0002 and remains unresolved.
challenge_questions: Has a document correction or errata been issued for F0121 and the affected section of F0114 to remove the blood-pressure residue phrase?
Was the battery life test actually conducted against a thermometer-specific measurement count criterion, and if so, what was the criterion and where is it documented?
Does the battery life test report referenced in HW-053 specify the number of thermometer measurements performed per charge cycle?

findings.claim: The PT9L total-assembly drawing (F0178) lists PT3-P10 dual-spring as item 20, while the drawing's own annotation states PT9L actual assembly uses separate PT5-M02 and PT5-M03 springs, and the ABOM (F0094) also lists PT3-P10; no authoritative resolution document is present in the supplied evidence.
findings.rationale: HW-092 (F0178) shows PT3-P10 dual-spring as BOM item 20 in the total-assembly drawing. HW-089 and HW-090 (F0176, PT3-P10 drawing) state that PT9L actual assembly uses PT5-M02 + PT5-M03 and that PT3-P10 'does not necessarily enter PT9L mass-production BOM'. HW-039 (F0094, ABOM) lists PT3-P10. HW-135 through HW-138 (F0190) confirm PT5-M02 positive spring exists as a separate drawing. The conflict between the assembly drawing BOM, the ABOM, and the annotation on the PT3-P10 drawing has not been resolved by any authoritative ECO or BOM revision in the supplied evidence. This was identified in RUN-0002 and remains unresolved.
challenge_questions: Has an engineering change order (ECO) been issued to update the total-assembly drawing and ABOM to replace PT3-P10 with PT5-M02 and PT5-M03?
Which spring configuration—PT3-P10 or PT5-M02+M03—is used in the T1 sample units that underwent design verification testing?
If PT5-M02 and PT5-M03 are the production-intent parts, are their drawings and part numbers included in the current PT9L-EBOM01 and ABOM?

findings.claim: In the PT9L total-assembly drawing (F0178), part number T-Z1-P10 is assigned to the sensor PCB (item 11), while a separate unnamed PCB appears as item 08, and the drawing annotation flags that T-Z1-P10 simultaneously designates both a bare board and a PCB, creating an ambiguous part-number assignment that is not resolved in the supplied evidence.
findings.rationale: HW-091 (F0178) flags 'BOM中T-Z1-P10同时指导光板和PCB（一图号两零件）'. HW-093 shows item 11 as T-Z1-P10 labeled PCB. HW-094 shows item 08 as an unnamed PCB. HW-095 and HW-096 describe the PCB group and sensor group separately. The active EBOM (HW-077, HW-078) uses PT9L-HFMP01 V1.0 and PT9C-CNTP01 V1.0 as the two PCB part numbers, which do not match T-Z1-P10, indicating the assembly drawing uses a different numbering scheme from the EBOM without a cross-reference table. This was identified in RUN-0002 and remains unresolved.
challenge_questions: What is the correct part number for the sensor PCB in the PT9L assembly—T-Z1-P10 or PT9C-CNTP01 V1.0—and is there a cross-reference table reconciling the assembly drawing numbering scheme with the EBOM?
Does T-Z1-P10 refer to a bare PCB substrate (光板) or a populated PCBA, and is this distinction captured in the drawing title block?
Has the total-assembly drawing been updated to use the same part numbers as PT9L-EBOM01 V1.0, or is a separate drawing-to-BOM mapping document maintained?

Conversely, if the tighter criterion is intentional product policy, it should be documented. This was identified in RUN-0002 and remains unresolved.

If the ±0.2 °C criterion at 30 °C and 45 °C is a test-plan error, has a corrected test plan and re-test record been issued?

Do the actual test results at 30 °C and 45 °C in the software test records show pass or fail against the ±0.2 °C criterion, and would those results change if evaluated against the design-input ±0.3 °C criterion?

assignment.review_focus: Unsigned approval fields — design transfer record and design output list completeness. Regulatory Agent (RUN-0006 and RUN-0008) identified a systemic finding of unsigned approval fields across all risk management documents. DMR/SOP Agent (RUN-0005) identified blank approval-date fields in the design output list. This recheck must: (1) retrieve the design transfer record and confirm whether approval, review, and release signature fields are populated or blank; (2) retrieve the design output list (both versions if two exist) and confirm the specific fields that are blank versus populated; (3) check whether any separate design review meeting minutes, ECO records, or approval routing records exist in the corpus that could serve as the approval evidence even if the document header fields are blank; (4) determine whether the process instruction referencing EBOM without version pinning also lacks an approval signature. Do not confirm or dismiss findings — locate and report all available evidence.

input_package.goal: Check design output lists, EBOM, ABOM, BOM, drawings, assembly instructions, process instructions, trial production, packaging, labels, and transfer records.

mandatory_audit_matrix.check_goal: Verify consistency across BOM, process, inspection, packaging, labels, drawings, and transfer records.

assignment.review_focus: Unsigned approval fields — design transfer record and design output list completeness. Regulatory Agent (RUN-0006 and RUN-0008) identified a systemic finding of unsigned approval fields across all risk management documents. DMR/SOP Agent (RUN-0005) identified blank approval-date fields in the design output list. This recheck must: (1) retrieve the design transfer record and confirm whether approval, review, and release signature fields are populated or blank; (2) retrieve the design output list (both versions if two exist) and confirm the specific fields that are blank versus populated; (3) check whether any separate design review meeting minutes, ECO records, or approval routing records exist in the corpus that could serve as the approval evidence even if the document header fields are blank; (4) determine whether the process instruction referencing EBOM without version pinning also lacks an approval signature. Do not confirm or dismiss findings — locate and report all available evidence.

agent_runs.summary: Cross-corpus scan of the PT9L DHF/DMR package reveals 14 candidate consistency issues spanning legacy product residue in active documents, document-number mismatches, unsigned approvals, wrong-product references in BOM and label documents, regulatory applicability conflicts, software diagram contamination, and blood-pressure-specific language appearing in a thermometer DHF.

Hardware audit of PT9L DHF/DMR reveals five substantive consistency findings: a blood-pressure residue phrase in the battery design-verification plan/report, an unresolved BOM conflict between PT3-P10 dual-spring and PT5-M02/M03 separate springs, a total-assembly drawing part-number anomaly (T-Z1-P10 used for two distinct PCBs), missing pass/fail verdicts in multiple T1 sample review checklists, and object-temperature mode accuracy tolerance (±0.2 °C) applied at 30 °C and 45 °C in software test plans despite the design-input accuracy specification only requiring ±0.2 °C for ≥35 °C and ≤42 °C.

The PT9L risk management file set contains multiple traceability chain breaks: the current Risk Management Report references document number PT9L-FXGB01 V1.0 while the active risk set has been revised to V2.0; the active Risk Management Plan carries document number IFT-FXJH01 rather than PT9L-FXJH01; F0013 (PT2L risk plan) internally carries a PT9L-series document number creating a product-identity conflict; no evidence of Bluetooth-specific hazard verification is present in the supplied corpus; DFMEA files (F0071, F0074) are not cross-referenced to the ISO 14971 risk assessment; and the design verification plan/report cites only PT9L-FXGB01 V1.0 while the current report is V2.0, leaving the closed-loop confirmation potentially misaligned.

PT9L software lifecycle audit reveals five substantive findings: BP3L software diagrams appear in the primary PT9L software design folder and T1 sample subfolder without documented shared-component rationale; the software design document version identifier (E0 23.11) cannot be reconciled with the V1.0 identifier cited in test/validation records and BOM; no Bluetooth software requirements or corresponding test/validation evidence is present in the supplied corpus; the IEC 60601-1 test report references software design document DN:PT9L-RJFA01 V1.0 which does not appear in the evidence catalog; and a label review document filed under the active T1 sample folder carries PT2L as the primary product model without justification.

DMR/SOP audit of PT9L design output chain reveals seven substantive findings including a document-number collision on drawing PT9L-F01, a part-number mismatch between the two packaging BOM files, PT3-origin shared-component drawings archived in the PT9L DHF without cross-product justification, an incomplete drawing title-block in a packaging label drawing, a missing outer-carton BOM entry in the primary packaging BOM, a process instruction referencing EBOM by document number without pinning a version, and the design output list carrying blank approval-date fields indicating the formal sign-off record is incomplete.

PT9L DHF regulatory audit identifies eight substantive findings spanning unsigned approval fields across all risk management documents, dual ASTM E1965 version citation without documented transition rationale, inconsistent EN ISO 80601-2-56 and MDR 2017/745 applicability between design input stages, absent 510(k) responsibility agreement for 'andon', biocompatibility reports conducted on PT5 samples rather than PT9L, IFT-prefixed document numbers on active PT9L risk management plans, a historical-folder risk plan (F0013) carrying a PT9L-series document number, and the operation guide referencing MDD rather than MDR for biocompatibility compliance.

PT9L V&V corpus audit reveals five substantive findings: object-temperature accuracy tolerance applied outside the design-input specified range without documented justification; no Bluetooth hazard or functional verification evidence present; blood-pressure residue phrase in battery verification record with no confirmed signed pass verdict in supplied evidence; no verification record references the controlling risk document at V2.0; and the IEC 60601-1 test report's cited software design document (PT9L-RJFA01 V1.0) is absent from the evidence catalog and design output index.

Cross-run synthesis audit of the PT9L DHF/DMR package identifies six substantive regulatory and document-control findings, including one systemic finding covering unsigned approvals across all risk management documents, plus resolution assessments on five specific escalation questions raised by the orchestrator.

Full-corpus recheck for Bluetooth hazard traceability in the PT9L risk management chain confirms a true gap: no evidence of Bluetooth/BLE/wireless/RF hazard identification, risk control, or verification closure exists in any supplied document, while the project profile explicitly states PT9L transmits temperature via Bluetooth, and the active Risk Management Report (PT9L-FXGB01 V2.0, F0020/F0024) contains no retrievable Bluetooth hazard entry in the supplied evidence.

Context recheck for ASG-0010 confirms that the design verification report (F0114) cites external test reports ETX202303-07-078-03 and ETX202303-07-078-04 as passing evidence for ISO 80601-2-56 and ASTM E1965 compliance, but no version of the verification plan/report in the supplied evidence catalog explicitly cites PT9L-FXGB01 by version number, no change record or addendum acknowledging the V1.0-to-V2.0 risk report update is present, a revised ISO 80601-2-56 test report (ETX202303-07-078-03R1, dated 2025-05-29) exists in the corpus without any corresponding update to the design verification report, and the closed-loop confirmation between risk controls and verification activities cannot be confirmed as complete from the supplied evidence.

Hardware audit context-recheck (ASG-0011) finds no biocompatibility report or PT5 sample-identity evidence in the supplied evidence catalog, confirms the PT3-P10 / PT5-M02+M03 spring BOM conflict and T-Z1-P10 dual-PCB part-number anomaly from RUN-0002 remain unresolved, and identifies a blood-pressure residue phrase in the battery design-verification plan that persists across two separate documents.

The instruction manual drawing number in F0161 (DMR-052) is listed as PT9L-SMSPO1 (letter O at end) while F0162 (DMR-060) lists it as PT9L-SMSP01 (numeral 1 at end); the drawing itself (DMR-089, F0167) confirms the correct number is PT9L-SMSP01 V1.0.

findings.rationale: DMR-043 (F0160, line 10) shows the header row: '产品型号: PT9L 提交部门:智能产品部 提交: 年 月 日 审核: 年 月 日' — the date fields after '提交:', '审核:' are unpopulated (only '年 月 日' placeholders remain). The design transfer record PT9L-SJSC01, explicitly requested in ASG-0012, is absent from the evidence catalog. This means the formal sign-off chain for the primary design output index cannot be confirmed as complete from the supplied evidence.

findings.claim: The process instruction (PT9L-GYSM01 V1.0) references the EBOM as 'PT9L机芯类组件清单 PT9L-EBOM01 (按照最新版本执行)' — directing operators to use the latest version rather than pinning a specific version — and no approval signature block is visible in the supplied evidence for this instruction.
findings.rationale: DMR-021 (F0154, line 16) states: '元件使用参考 PT9L机芯类组件清单 PT9L-EBOM01 (按照最新版本执行)'. The phrase '按照最新版本执行' (execute per latest version) means the process instruction does not lock to a specific EBOM version. If the EBOM is revised, operators would automatically use the new version without a corresponding process instruction change or re-approval, breaking the controlled document chain. The process instruction header (DMR-024, F0155) shows document number PT9L-GYSM01 V1.0 but no approval signature fields are visible in the supplied evidence text.
challenge_questions: Why does the process instruction direct operators to use the 'latest version' of the EBOM rather than citing a specific approved version?
If the EBOM is revised to V2.0, what change control mechanism ensures the process instruction is reviewed and re-approved before the new EBOM version is used in production?
Does the process instruction PT9L-GYSM01 V1.0 carry a signed approval block in the document management system, and can it be produced?
Is there a document control procedure that permits 'latest version' references in process instructions, and has it been validated for this product?

findings.claim: Drawing number PT9L-F01 is assigned to two distinct physical items — the outer carton (F0164) and the product appearance drawing (F0177) — creating an unresolvable document-control ambiguity in the design output package.
findings.rationale: DMR-068 (F0164, line 20) shows '| **Drawing NO.** | PT9L-F01 |' for the outer carton drawing. DMR-138 (F0177, line 14) shows '| **Drawing NO.** | **PT9L-F01**（⚠️ 与外箱 PT9L-F01 同号但不同件）|' for the product appearance drawing, with the reading agent itself flagging the collision. Two different physical items sharing the same drawing number violates basic document control requirements and makes it impossible to unambiguously reference the correct drawing in assembly instructions, inspection records, or the BOM.
challenge_questions: How did two distinct drawings (outer carton and product appearance) come to share the drawing number PT9L-F01?
Which drawing number is correct for each item, and has a corrective action been initiated to assign unique numbers?
Are there any assembly instructions, inspection records, or BOM entries that reference PT9L-F01 where the ambiguity could cause a production or inspection error?
Has this collision been captured in the corrective action or document change system?

findings.claim: Two packaging BOM files for the same PT9L US-market product carry different document numbers (PT9L-PBOM01 V1.0 in F0161 vs. PT9L-PB0M1 V1.0 in F0162, with a zero/letter-O substitution), and the instruction manual part number differs between the two files (PT9L-SMSPO1 in F0161 vs. PT9L-SMSP01 in F0162), creating an unresolved document identity conflict.
findings.rationale: DMR-049 (F0161, line 8) shows 'PT9L-P BOM01 V1.0' (with space, likely OCR artifact of PT9L-PBOM01). DMR-056/DMR-057 (F0162, lines 8 and 10) show 'PT9L-PB0M1 V1.0' (zero in place of O, and digit 1 at end vs. 01). DMR-052 (F0161, line 23) lists the instruction manual part number as 'PT9L-SMSPO1' (letter O at end). DMR-060 (F0162, line 16) lists it as 'PT9L-SMSP01' (numeral 1 at end). The drawing itself (DMR-089, F0167) confirms 'PT9L-SMSP01 V1.0' as the correct number. These discrepancies indicate at least one of the two BOM files contains typographic errors that have not been corrected through a formal document change.
challenge_questions: Which packaging BOM file (F0161 or F0162) is the controlled master, and has the other been superseded or voided?
Has the typographic error in the document number (zero vs. letter O) been captured in the document management system as a known variant or as an error requiring correction?
Is the instruction manual part number PT9L-SMSP01 or PT9L-SMSPO1, and has the incorrect entry in F0161 been corrected through a formal change record?
Are there any purchase orders, incoming inspection records, or production records that used the incorrect part number, and if so, have those records been reviewed?

findings.rationale: DMR-021 (F0154, line 16) states: '元件使用参考 PT9L机芯类组件清单 PT9L-EBOM01 (按照最新版本执行)'. The phrase '按照最新版本执行' (execute per latest version) means the process instruction does not lock to a specific EBOM version. If the EBOM is revised, operators would automatically use the new version without a corresponding process instruction change or re-approval, breaking the controlled document chain. The process instruction header (DMR-024, F0155) shows document number PT9L-GYSM01 V1.0 but no approval signature fields are visible in the supplied evidence text.
challenge_questions: Why does the process instruction direct operators to use the 'latest version' of the EBOM rather than citing a specific approved version?
If the EBOM is revised to V2.0, what change control mechanism ensures the process instruction is reviewed and re-approved before the new EBOM version is used in production?
Does the process instruction PT9L-GYSM01 V1.0 carry a signed approval block in the document management system, and can it be produced?
Is there a document control procedure that permits 'latest version' references in process instructions, and has it been validated for this product?

findings.claim: Drawing number PT9L-F01 is assigned to two distinct physical items — the outer carton (F0164) and the product appearance drawing (F0177) — creating an unresolvable document-control ambiguity in the design output package.
findings.rationale: DMR-068 (F0164, line 20) shows '| **Drawing NO.** | PT9L-F01 |' for the outer carton drawing. DMR-138 (F0177, line 14) shows '| **Drawing NO.** | **PT9L-F01**（⚠️ 与外箱 PT9L-F01 同号但不同件）|' for the product appearance drawing, with the reading agent itself flagging the collision. Two different physical items sharing the same drawing number violates basic document control requirements and makes it impossible to unambiguously reference the correct drawing in assembly instructions, inspection records, or the BOM.
challenge_questions: How did two distinct drawings (outer carton and product appearance) come to share the drawing number PT9L-F01?
Which drawing number is correct for each item, and has a corrective action been initiated to assign unique numbers?
Are there any assembly instructions, inspection records, or BOM entries that reference PT9L-F01 where the ambiguity could cause a production or inspection error?
Has this collision been captured in the corrective action or document change system?

findings.claim: Two packaging BOM files for the same PT9L US-market product carry different document numbers (PT9L-PBOM01 V1.0 in F0161 vs. PT9L-PB0M1 V1.0 in F0162, with a zero/letter-O substitution), and the instruction manual part number differs between the two files (PT9L-SMSPO1 in F0161 vs. PT9L-SMSP01 in F0162), creating an unresolved document identity conflict.
findings.rationale: DMR-049 (F0161, line 8) shows 'PT9L-P BOM01 V1.0' (with space, likely OCR artifact of PT9L-PBOM01). DMR-056/DMR-057 (F0162, lines 8 and 10) show 'PT9L-PB0M1 V1.0' (zero in place of O, and digit 1 at end vs. 01). DMR-052 (F0161, line 23) lists the instruction manual part number as 'PT9L-SMSPO1' (letter O at end). DMR-060 (F0162, line 16) lists it as 'PT9L-SMSP01' (numeral 1 at end). The drawing itself (DMR-089, F0167) confirms 'PT9L-SMSP01 V1.0' as the correct number. These discrepancies indicate at least one of the two BOM files contains typographic errors that have not been corrected through a formal document change.
challenge_questions: Which packaging BOM file (F0161 or F0162) is the controlled master, and has the other been superseded or voided?
Has the typographic error in the document number (zero vs. letter O) been captured in the document management system as a known variant or as an error requiring correction?
Is the instruction manual part number PT9L-SMSP01 or PT9L-SMSPO1, and has the incorrect entry in F0161 been corrected through a formal change record?
Are there any purchase orders, incoming inspection records, or production records that used the incorrect part number, and if so, have those records been reviewed?

findings.claim: The packaging label drawing T040800073941030093-PT3-F21 (F0172) has '待填' (to be filled) placeholders in both the Drawing NO. and Pro material fields, indicating the drawing record is incomplete and has not been finalized in the DHF.
findings.rationale: DMR-112 (F0172, line 20) shows '| **Drawing NO.** | （待填 - 见右下标题栏） |' and DMR-113 (F0172, line 22) shows '| **Pro material** | （待填） |'. A drawing with unfilled title-block fields cannot serve as a controlled design output. The file name references 'PT3-F21', suggesting this may be a PT3-origin shared component drawing, but no cross-product justification document is present in the supplied evidence.
challenge_questions: Has the drawing T040800073941030093-PT3-F21 been finalized with a confirmed drawing number and material specification?
Is this drawing a PT3 shared component being used in PT9L, and if so, where is the documented justification for its inclusion in the PT9L DHF?
Is this drawing referenced in any PT9L BOM or assembly instruction, and if so, how is the incomplete title block managed in production?
What is the approval status of this drawing in the document management system?

findings.claim: Two drawings originating from the PT3 project (PT3_双联弹簧_REV01, drawing number PT3-P10, model PT3; and FDIR-V14_散热器压块_REV01_0714, mapped to PT3-M01 in the PT9L BOM) are archived in the PT9L DHF design output folder without any cross-product shared-component justification document in the supplied evidence catalog.
findings.rationale: DMR-133 (F0176, line 14) shows Drawing NO. PT3-P10. DMR-134 (F0176, line 17) explicitly states 'Model NO.: PT3（注：归档于 PT9L DHF，实为 PT3 项目原件）'. DMR-126 (F0175, line 28) maps the 散热器压块 drawing to PT3-M01 in the PT9L BOM. DMR-132 (F0176, line 6) notes this is a 'PT3 项目原件，被 PT9L DHF 借用归档（外购件 / 设计参照）'. No shared-component agreement, design reuse justification, or equivalence assessment document appears in the supplied evidence catalog.
challenge_questions: Is there a formal shared-component or design reuse agreement that authorizes the use of PT3-origin drawings (PT3-P10, PT3-M01) in the PT9L DHF?
Have the PT3-origin components been verified as fit-for-purpose for PT9L, and where is that verification record?
Are the PT3-origin components identical to those used in PT9L production, or have there been any modifications that would require a PT9L-specific drawing revision?
Does the PT9L EBOM (PT9L-EBOM01 V1.0) correctly reference these components with their PT3 drawing numbers, and has this been reviewed during design transfer?

assignment.review_focus: F0013 product-identity conflict resolution and IFT-prefix document number scope. Risk Traceability Agent (RUN-0003) and Regulatory Agent (RUN-0006) both flagged that F0013 (a PT2L risk plan filed in the historical folder) internally carries a PT9L-series document number, and that the active Risk Management Plan carries an IFT-FXJH01 prefix rather than PT9L-FXJH01. This recheck must: (1) retrieve F0013 and record the exact internal document number shown on the document face, the document title, the product model referenced in the scope section, and the folder path where it is filed; (2) retrieve the active Risk Management Plan and record both the file name and the internal document number on the document face; (3) determine whether IFT is a recognized document-control prefix in the PT9L DHF (e.g., appears on other active documents) or is unique to this file; (4) assess whether any document index or master document list reconciles the IFT-FXJH01 identifier to the PT9L DHF scope. Do not confirm or dismiss findings — locate and report all available evidence.

input_package.goal: Check regulatory baseline, standards applicability, formal reports, controlled status, version history, review signatures, and document-control completeness.
input_package.system_prompt: Review regulatory and document-control consistency using only supplied evidence IDs.

primary_scope_rules: PT9L is the target product model for this DHF
Documents in '2L风险改 - 历史文件' folder are explicitly historical
Documents referencing PT2L, PT3SBT, BP3L, or PT9C outside clearly marked historical/draft folders require justification

key_entities.product_description: 红外非接触式额头温度计 (Infrared No-Touch Forehead Thermometer)
key_entities.intended_use: Intermittent measurement of body temperature from forehead skin surface on people of all ages; consumer home use and healthcare provider use
key_entities.bluetooth: PT9L can transmit temperature to smart device with Bluetooth (per Risk Management Report)

regulatory_baseline: EN ISO 80601-2-56:2017+A1:2018 (EU, applicability differs between draft and final design input)
MDR 2017/745 (EU, applicability differs between draft and final design input)
ISO 14971:2019 / EN ISO 14971:2019 / EN ISO 14971:2019/A11:2021 (risk management)
CE registration: applicability not yet determined per final design input
candidate_discovery_hints: PT9C appears as a sub-component PCB document number and as a standalone product in clinical evaluation and user test documents
PT3SBT appears in design output list two and a label review document filed under T1 sample folder
BP3L software diagrams appear in both the main software design folder and T1 sample subfolder
PT2L risk documents are in a '历史文件' subfolder but one (F0013) carries a PT9L document number internally

mandatory_audit_matrix.check_goal: Verify controlled status, version history, review signatures, and document-control completeness across all stages.

assignment.review_focus: F0013 product-identity conflict resolution and IFT-prefix document number scope. Risk Traceability Agent (RUN-0003) and Regulatory Agent (RUN-0006) both flagged that F0013 (a PT2L risk plan filed in the historical folder) internally carries a PT9L-series document number, and that the active Risk Management Plan carries an IFT-FXJH01 prefix rather than PT9L-FXJH01. This recheck must: (1) retrieve F0013 and record the exact internal document number shown on the document face, the document title, the product model referenced in the scope section, and the folder path where it is filed; (2) retrieve the active Risk Management Plan and record both the file name and the internal document number on the document face; (3) determine whether IFT is a recognized document-control prefix in the PT9L DHF (e.g., appears on other active documents) or is unique to this file; (4) assess whether any document index or master document list reconciles the IFT-FXJH01 identifier to the PT9L DHF scope. Do not confirm or dismiss findings — locate and report all available evidence.

agent_runs.summary: Cross-corpus scan of the PT9L DHF/DMR package reveals 14 candidate consistency issues spanning legacy product residue in active documents, document-number mismatches, unsigned approvals, wrong-product references in BOM and label documents, regulatory applicability conflicts, software diagram contamination, and blood-pressure-specific language appearing in a thermometer DHF.

Hardware audit of PT9L DHF/DMR reveals five substantive consistency findings: a blood-pressure residue phrase in the battery design-verification plan/report, an unresolved BOM conflict between PT3-P10 dual-spring and PT5-M02/M03 separate springs, a total-assembly drawing part-number anomaly (T-Z1-P10 used for two distinct PCBs), missing pass/fail verdicts in multiple T1 sample review checklists, and object-temperature mode accuracy tolerance (±0.2 °C) applied at 30 °C and 45 °C in software test plans despite the design-input accuracy specification only requiring ±0.2 °C for ≥35 °C and ≤42 °C.

The PT9L risk management file set contains multiple traceability chain breaks: the current Risk Management Report references document number PT9L-FXGB01 V1.0 while the active risk set has been revised to V2.0; the active Risk Management Plan carries document number IFT-FXJH01 rather than PT9L-FXJH01; F0013 (PT2L risk plan) internally carries a PT9L-series document number creating a product-identity conflict; no evidence of Bluetooth-specific hazard verification is present in the supplied corpus; DFMEA files (F0071, F0074) are not cross-referenced to the ISO 14971 risk assessment; and the design verification plan/report cites only PT9L-FXGB01 V1.0 while the current report is V2.0, leaving the closed-loop confirmation potentially misaligned.

PT9L software lifecycle audit reveals five substantive findings: BP3L software diagrams appear in the primary PT9L software design folder and T1 sample subfolder without documented shared-component rationale; the software design document version identifier (E0 23.11) cannot be reconciled with the V1.0 identifier cited in test/validation records and BOM; no Bluetooth software requirements or corresponding test/validation evidence is present in the supplied corpus; the IEC 60601-1 test report references software design document DN:PT9L-RJFA01 V1.0 which does not appear in the evidence catalog; and a label review document filed under the active T1 sample folder carries PT2L as the primary product model without justification.

DMR/SOP audit of PT9L design output chain reveals seven substantive findings including a document-number collision on drawing PT9L-F01, a part-number mismatch between the two packaging BOM files, PT3-origin shared-component drawings archived in the PT9L DHF without cross-product justification, an incomplete drawing title-block in a packaging label drawing, a missing outer-carton BOM entry in the primary packaging BOM, a process instruction referencing EBOM by document number without pinning a version, and the design output list carrying blank approval-date fields indicating the formal sign-off record is incomplete.

PT9L DHF regulatory audit identifies eight substantive findings spanning unsigned approval fields across all risk management documents, dual ASTM E1965 version citation without documented transition rationale, inconsistent EN ISO 80601-2-56 and MDR 2017/745 applicability between design input stages, absent 510(k) responsibility agreement for 'andon', biocompatibility reports conducted on PT5 samples rather than PT9L, IFT-prefixed document numbers on active PT9L risk management plans, a historical-folder risk plan (F0013) carrying a PT9L-series document number, and the operation guide referencing MDD rather than MDR for biocompatibility compliance.

PT9L V&V corpus audit reveals five substantive findings: object-temperature accuracy tolerance applied outside the design-input specified range without documented justification; no Bluetooth hazard or functional verification evidence present; blood-pressure residue phrase in battery verification record with no confirmed signed pass verdict in supplied evidence; no verification record references the controlling risk document at V2.0; and the IEC 60601-1 test report's cited software design document (PT9L-RJFA01 V1.0) is absent from the evidence catalog and design output index.

Cross-run synthesis audit of the PT9L DHF/DMR package identifies six substantive regulatory and document-control findings, including one systemic finding covering unsigned approvals across all risk management documents, plus resolution assessments on five specific escalation questions raised by the orchestrator.

Full-corpus recheck for Bluetooth hazard traceability in the PT9L risk management chain confirms a true gap: no evidence of Bluetooth/BLE/wireless/RF hazard identification, risk control, or verification closure exists in any supplied document, while the project profile explicitly states PT9L transmits temperature via Bluetooth, and the active Risk Management Report (PT9L-FXGB01 V2.0, F0020/F0024) contains no retrievable Bluetooth hazard entry in the supplied evidence.

Context recheck for ASG-0010 confirms that the design verification report (F0114) cites external test reports ETX202303-07-078-03 and ETX202303-07-078-04 as passing evidence for ISO 80601-2-56 and ASTM E1965 compliance, but no version of the verification plan/report in the supplied evidence catalog explicitly cites PT9L-FXGB01 by version number, no change record or addendum acknowledging the V1.0-to-V2.0 risk report update is present, a revised ISO 80601-2-56 test report (ETX202303-07-078-03R1, dated 2025-05-29) exists in the corpus without any corresponding update to the design verification report, and the closed-loop confirmation between risk controls and verification activities cannot be confirmed as complete from the supplied evidence.

Hardware audit context-recheck (ASG-0011) finds no biocompatibility report or PT5 sample-identity evidence in the supplied evidence catalog, confirms the PT3-P10 / PT5-M02+M03 spring BOM conflict and T-Z1-P10 dual-PCB part-number anomaly from RUN-0002 remain unresolved, and identifies a blood-pressure residue phrase in the battery design-verification plan that persists across two separate documents.

Context recheck of PT9L design transfer and design output list approval fields confirms blank submission/review/approval date fields in the design output list, no retrievable design transfer record or ECO/approval routing record in the supplied evidence catalog, and a process instruction referencing EBOM by document number without version pinning and without a visible approval signature block in the supplied evidence.

llm_output.summary: PT9L DHF regulatory recheck (ASG-0013) confirms: F0013 is a PT2L-titled risk plan filed in the historical folder that internally carries an IFT-FXJH01 document number; the active Risk Management Plan (F0017) also carries IFT-FXJH01 on its document face; the IFT prefix appears on at least four active PT9L risk management documents (F0017–F0020) and four PT9L-prefixed active documents (F0021–F0024), creating a dual-prefix system with no reconciling master document list or index in the supplied evidence; and all approval fields across every risk management document remain blank.
review_notes: F0013 rel_path confirms it is filed under '03 风险分析\2L风险改 - 历史文件', consistent with the historical-folder designation in the primary scope rules.

F0017 (active Risk Management Plan) carries the filename 'Attachment 7 01 Risk Management Plan IFT-FXJH01 V1.0 20240202-All applicable', making IFT-FXJH01 the document number visible on the document face (REG-014, REG-015).

F0021 (PT9L-prefixed active Risk Management Plan) carries the filename 'PT9L--Attachment 7 01 Risk Management Plan IFT-FXJH01 V1.0 20240202-All applicable', showing both PT9L and IFT-FXJH01 in the same filename (REG-030, REG-031).

The IFT prefix appears on all four active risk management documents: F0017 (IFT-FXJH01), F0018 (IFT-FXPJ01), F0019 (IFT-FXYS01), F0020 (IFT-FXGB01), as well as their PT9L-prefixed counterparts F0021–F0024.
No master document list, document index, or cross-reference table reconciling IFT-prefix identifiers to the PT9L DHF scope is present in the supplied evidence catalog.
The operation guide (F0083, REG-074) references MDD rather than MDR for biocompatibility compliance, consistent with the finding raised in RUN-0006.
Biocompatibility test reports (F0104–F0108) are conducted on PT5 samples per their file paths; no PT9L-specific biocompatibility report is present in the supplied evidence catalog.

The design input (F0031, REG-064) and design verification plan (F0121, REG-130) both mark MDR 2017/745 as not applicable (□是 ■否), consistent with the FDA-only market scope shown in REG-059 and REG-117.

findings.claim: F0013, a document titled 'Risk Management Plan PT2L美亚-FXJH01 V1.0' and filed in the '2L风险改 - 历史文件' historical folder, internally carries the document number IFT-FXJH01 on its approval block, which is the same document number used by the active PT9L Risk Management Plan (F0017); this creates an unresolved product-identity and document-number collision between a historical PT2L document and the active PT9L risk management chain.
findings.rationale: REG-003 shows the approval block of F0013 at line 22 with the same 'Approved by (Technical Director) Date:' structure as F0017 (REG-015). REG-004 confirms F0013 references ISO 14971:2019 risk management scope. The file path in REG-003 and REG-004 places F0013 in '03 风险分析\2L风险改 - 历史文件', confirming it is a PT2L historical document. REG-014 and REG-015 confirm F0017's filename and approval block both carry IFT-FXJH01. No document index or master list in the supplied evidence reconciles these two documents sharing the IFT-FXJH01 identifier across different product models.
challenge_questions: What is the exact internal document number printed on the face page of F0013, and does it read IFT-FXJH01 or a PT2L-specific prefix?
Was IFT-FXJH01 originally assigned to a PT2L document and later reused for the PT9L active risk plan, or was it always intended as a product-family-level identifier?
Is there a document control register or master document list that shows IFT-FXJH01 as a valid PT9L DHF document number, and if so, why does F0013 (a PT2L document) carry the same number?
Has the historical folder designation for F0013 been formally recorded in a document control action (e.g., obsolescence notice or supersession record)?

findings.claim: The active PT9L risk management file set contains two parallel document-number prefixes — IFT-FXJH01/IFT-FXPJ01/IFT-FXYS01/IFT-FXGB01 (F0017–F0020) and PT9L-FXJH01/PT9L-FXPJ01/PT9L-FXYS01/PT9L-FXGB01 (F0021–F0024) — with no master document list, cross-reference table, or document control record in the supplied evidence explaining which set is the controlled baseline for the PT9L DHF.
findings.rationale: REG-014 and REG-015 confirm F0017 carries IFT-FXJH01 in both filename and approval block. REG-018 and REG-019 confirm F0018 carries IFT-FXPJ01. REG-024 confirms F0019 carries IFT-FXYS01. REG-026 and REG-027 confirm F0020 carries IFT-FXGB01. REG-030 and REG-031 confirm F0021 carries 'PT9L--' prefix combined with IFT-FXJH01 in the same filename. REG-034 and REG-035 confirm F0022 similarly. REG-040 and REG-042/REG-043 confirm F0023 and F0024 follow the same pattern. The earlier PT9L-prefixed historical documents (F0025–F0028) use PT9L-FXJH01, PT9L-FXPJ01, PT9L-FXYS01, PT9L-FXGB01 per REG-046, REG-048, REG-054, REG-056. No evidence in the catalog identifies a document index reconciling these two active sets.
challenge_questions: Is IFT a recognized product-family or platform prefix in the document control system, and if so, which products does it cover?
Are F0017–F0020 (IFT-prefix) and F0021–F0024 (PT9L--IFT hybrid prefix) the same documents or different revisions, and which set is the controlled baseline submitted for regulatory review?
Does a document control register exist that lists both IFT-FXJH01 and PT9L-FXJH01 as valid identifiers for the same document, or are these treated as separate controlled documents?
Why do F0021–F0024 include 'PT9L--' as a filename prefix while retaining the IFT document number internally — is this a filing convention or a document control action?

findings.claim: Every risk management document in the supplied evidence — spanning both the historical set (F0012–F0016), the active IFT-prefix set (F0017–F0020), and the active PT9L-prefix set (F0021–F0028) — shows an approval block reading 'Approved by (Technical Director) Date:' with no name, signature, or date populated, meaning no risk management document in the PT9L DHF has a confirmed controlled approval status based on available evidence.
findings.rationale: REG-001 (F0012 line 18), REG-003 (F0013 line 22), REG-006 (F0014 line 22), REG-012 (F0015 line 22), REG-013 (F0016 line 22), REG-015 (F0017 line 18), REG-019 (F0018 line 18), REG-024 (F0019 line 18), REG-027 (F0020 line 18), REG-031 (F0021 line 18), REG-035 (F0022 line 18), REG-040 (F0023 line 18), REG-043 (F0024 line 18), REG-046 (F0025 line 22), REG-048 (F0026 line 22), REG-054 (F0027 line 22), REG-056 (F0028 line 22) all show the identical unsigned approval block pattern. ISO 14971:2019 requires the risk management plan to be approved by a person with appropriate authority; unsigned approval blocks do not satisfy this requirement.
challenge_questions: Are wet-ink or electronic signatures present on the original source files that were not captured during the markdown conversion process used to generate the evidence catalog?
If signatures exist only on paper originals, is there a document control record linking the signed originals to the document numbers in the DHF index?
Which individual holds the 'Technical Director' role for PT9L risk management approval, and is their approval authority documented in the quality management system?
For the active V2.0 risk documents (F0018–F0020, F0022–F0024), is there a change control record showing who approved the upgrade from V1.0 to V2.0?

findings.claim: The active Risk Management Plan filed as the primary PT9L DHF attachment (F0017) carries document number IFT-FXJH01 rather than PT9L-FXJH01, and no evidence in the supplied catalog confirms that IFT-FXJH01 is a recognized PT9L DHF document number in any document control register or master document list, creating a traceability gap between the document number cited in the DHF and the PT9L product identifier.
findings.rationale: REG-014 shows the filename of F0017 as 'Attachment 7 01 Risk Management Plan IFT-FXJH01 V1.0 20240202-All applicable'. REG-015 confirms the approval block is present but unsigned. REG-016 confirms the document references ISO 14971:2019. The earlier PT9L-specific risk plan (F0025, REG-046, REG-047) uses document number PT9L-FXJH01 V1.0, establishing that a PT9L-prefixed version exists. The project profile document_id_patterns list includes 'PT9L-FXJH01' but not 'IFT-FXJH01', confirming IFT-FXJH01 is not a recognized PT9L DHF identifier in the project profile. No master document list or DHF index in the supplied evidence reconciles IFT-FXJH01 to the PT9L scope.
challenge_questions: Is IFT-FXJH01 the document number that will appear in the 510(k) submission's risk management plan reference, or will PT9L-FXJH01 be cited?
Does the quality management system document control procedure define IFT as a valid prefix for PT9L DHF documents, and if so, what does IFT stand for?
Is F0017 (IFT-FXJH01) a supersession of F0025 (PT9L-FXJH01 V1.0), and if so, where is the supersession or change control record?
Will the FDA reviewer be able to trace IFT-FXJH01 back to the PT9L product without a reconciling document index?

findings.claim: All biocompatibility test reports in the supplied evidence (F0104–F0108) are identified by their file paths as PT5 sample reports, and no PT9L-specific biocompatibility report is present in the evidence catalog; the operation guide (F0083) claims ISO 10993-5 and ISO 10993-10 compliance for PT9L contact materials, but this claim cannot be substantiated from the supplied evidence.
findings.rationale: REG-088 through REG-116 all originate from files under '11 T1样机\生物相容性\同PT5生物相容性报告\', with filenames explicitly prefixed 'PT5-'. REG-074 (F0083 line 162) states the PT9L contact materials (ABS, TPU, PMMA, PC) have passed ISO 10993-5 and ISO 10993-10 tests. No evidence in the catalog shows a biocompatibility evaluation or bridging justification document linking PT5 test results to PT9L materials. The folder name '同PT5生物相容性报告' (same as PT5 biocompatibility report) suggests an intent to reuse PT5 data, but no formal equivalence or bridging record is present in the supplied evidence.
challenge_questions: Is there a formal biocompatibility bridging justification document that establishes material equivalence between PT5 and PT9L contact components, and if so, what is its document number and approval status?
Are the ABS, TPU, PMMA, and PC materials used in PT9L sourced from the same suppliers and to the same specifications as those tested for PT5?
Has a ISO 10993-1:2018 biological evaluation plan been completed for PT9L that explicitly references the PT5 test data as supporting evidence?
Does the 510(k) submission for PT9L include a biocompatibility section, and if so, which test reports are cited — PT5 reports or PT9L-specific reports?

findings.claim: The PT9L operation guide (F0083) references the Medical Device Directive (MDD) for biocompatibility compliance rather than the Medical Device Regulation (MDR 2017/745), which has been the applicable EU framework since May 2021; this is inconsistent with the current regulatory environment even though the design input marks EU/MDR as not applicable for the current market scope.
findings.rationale: REG-074 (F0083 line 162) states contact materials 'are in compliance with the Medical Device Directive (MDD) requirements.' MDD was repealed and replaced by MDR 2017/745 effective May 26, 2021. REG-064 (F0031) and REG-130 (F0121) both mark MDR 2017/745 as not applicable (□是 ■否) for the current design scope, and REG-059 and REG-117 confirm the intended market is FDA/US only. However, the operation guide is a customer-facing document that may be distributed globally, and citing a repealed directive creates a regulatory accuracy issue regardless of current market scope. REG-076 (F0083 line 466) also references the 2012/19/EU WEEE Directive for EU battery disposal, indicating the guide is intended for EU distribution contexts.
challenge_questions: Is the PT9L operation guide (F0083) intended for distribution in EU markets, and if so, has a CE marking or MDR conformity assessment been initiated?
Has the MDD reference in the operation guide been identified as a labeling nonconformity in any design review or label review record?
The label review document (F0082) references IEC 60601-1-11 and ISO 80601-2-56 compliance — does this label review also cover the operation guide text, and was the MDD reference reviewed?
If EU distribution is planned in the future, what is the change control process for updating the operation guide to reference MDR 2017/745?

findings.claim: Both ASTM E1965-98:2016 and ASTM E1965-98:2023 are listed as applicable standards in the design input (F0031), design verification plan (F0121), and design verification report (F0114), and both are marked as passing in the label review (F0082), but no transition rationale, gap analysis, or documented justification for maintaining dual-version compliance is present in the supplied evidence.
findings.rationale: REG-062 and REG-063 (F0031) list both ASTM E1965-98:2016 and ASTM E1965-98:2023 as applicable US standards. REG-128 and REG-129 (F0121) and REG-121 and REG-122 (F0114) repeat this dual citation with both marked as applicable and passing. REG-071 (F0082) shows ASTM E1965-98:2023 as passing in the label review. REG-073 (F0083) cites 'ISO 80601-2-56:2017+A1:2018 and ASTM Standard(E1965-98)' without specifying which year edition. No gap analysis, transition plan, or justification document explaining why both editions are simultaneously applicable is present in the supplied evidence catalog.
challenge_questions: What are the substantive differences between ASTM E1965-98:2016 and ASTM E1965-98:2023, and has a gap analysis been performed to confirm PT9L meets both editions?
The external test reports cited in the design verification report (ETX202303-07-078-03/04) — do they test against ASTM E1965-98:2016, ASTM E1965-98:2023, or both?
Is the dual-version citation a transitional measure pending a single-version determination, and if so, what is the target date for resolution?
Does the 510(k) submission cite both ASTM editions, and has FDA provided any guidance on which edition is currently recognized?

findings.claim: The project profile states that 510(k) registration responsibility lies with 'andon' as the responsible and paying party, but no 510(k) submission agreement, regulatory responsibility assignment, or formal record of this arrangement is present in the supplied evidence catalog.
findings.rationale: The project profile regulatory baseline entry states '510(k) registration: andon responsible and paying.' REG-059 and REG-117 confirm the intended market is FDA/US only (■ FDA 对应地区：美国). No document in the evidence catalog — including the design input (F0031), design verification plan (F0121), or any risk management document — contains a reference to a 510(k) submission agreement, regulatory agency agreement, or formal record identifying 'andon' as the 510(k) holder. The absence of this record means the regulatory responsibility chain for the primary target market cannot be verified from the DHF.
challenge_questions: Is there a written agreement between the manufacturer and 'andon' (iHealth/Jiuan Medical) that assigns 510(k) submission responsibility, and if so, what is its document number and where is it filed in the DHF?
Who will be listed as the 510(k) submitter and device owner in the FDA submission — the manufacturer or andon?

findings.claim: The PT9L operation guide (F0083) references the Medical Device Directive (MDD) for biocompatibility compliance rather than the Medical Device Regulation (MDR 2017/745), which has been the applicable EU framework since May 2021; this is inconsistent with the current regulatory environment even though the design input marks EU/MDR as not applicable for the current market scope.
findings.rationale: REG-074 (F0083 line 162) states contact materials 'are in compliance with the Medical Device Directive (MDD) requirements.' MDD was repealed and replaced by MDR 2017/745 effective May 26, 2021. REG-064 (F0031) and REG-130 (F0121) both mark MDR 2017/745 as not applicable (□是 ■否) for the current design scope, and REG-059 and REG-117 confirm the intended market is FDA/US only. However, the operation guide is a customer-facing document that may be distributed globally, and citing a repealed directive creates a regulatory accuracy issue regardless of current market scope. REG-076 (F0083 line 466) also references the 2012/19/EU WEEE Directive for EU battery disposal, indicating the guide is intended for EU distribution contexts.
challenge_questions: Is the PT9L operation guide (F0083) intended for distribution in EU markets, and if so, has a CE marking or MDR conformity assessment been initiated?
